how.gist: Lie on a bench, lower the weight to your lower chest under control, and press it back up to straight arms.
steps: Lie with your eyes under the bar, feet flat, and squeeze your shoulder blades back and down into the bench.
Grip a little wider than shoulder width and take the bar out to straight arms over your shoulders.
Lower it to your lower chest with your elbows angled about 45° from your body.
Press back up and slightly toward your face until your arms are straight.
how.watch: Elbows flaring straight out to the sides and shoulders rolling forward off the bench.
how.easier: Use dumbbells, or do Chest press machine instead.
how.harder: Pause each rep for a second on your chest.

how.gist: On a bench set to about 30–45°, lower the weight to your upper chest and press it back up over your shoulders.
steps: Set the bench to 30–45° and sit back with your feet flat and shoulder blades pinned back.
Start with the weight over your shoulders, arms straight.
Lower it to your upper chest, just below the collarbones, elbows slightly tucked.
Press straight back up until your arms are straight.
how.watch: Bench set too steep, so it turns into a shoulder press.
how.easier: Use dumbbells, which let each arm find its own path.

how.gist: Hook your legs under the pads of a decline bench, lower the weight to your lower chest and press it back up.
steps: Lock your legs under the pads and lie back with your shoulder blades squeezed together.
Take the weight over your shoulders with straight arms; have a spotter hand off a barbell.
Lower it to your lower chest, elbows about 45° from your body.
Press back up to straight arms.
how.watch: Bouncing the bar off the chest.
how.easier: Use dumbbells and a shallower decline.

how.gist: A bench press with your hands about shoulder width apart and elbows tucked, to put more of the work on the triceps.
steps: Set up as for a bench press: shoulder blades back, feet flat.
Grip the bar about shoulder width, wrists stacked over elbows.
Lower it to your lower chest with your elbows close to your sides.
Press up to straight arms, keeping the elbows tucked.
how.watch: A grip so narrow that the wrists bend back and the elbows flare.
how.harder: Pause each rep for a second on your chest.

how.gist: Lying on the floor, lower the weight until your upper arms rest on the floor, pause, then press back to straight arms.
steps: Lie under a bar in a low rack, or on the floor holding dumbbells, knees bent.
Start with straight arms over your shoulders and shoulder blades pulled back.
Lower until your upper arms rest on the floor, elbows about 45° from your body.
Pause for a moment, then press back to straight arms.
how.watch: Letting the elbows crash into the floor and bouncing off it.
how.easier: Use dumbbells, which are easier to get into position alone.
how.harder: Hold the pause on the floor for two seconds.

video.title: How to Floor Press for Maximum Bench Press Strength

how.gist: Lying on a bench, open your arms wide in an arc with elbows slightly bent, then hug the weights back together over your chest.
steps: Lie on a flat bench with the weights over your chest, palms facing each other.
Soften your elbows slightly and keep that bend for the whole set.
Open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Bring the weights back up along the same arc, as if hugging a barrel.
how.watch: Bending the elbows more as you lower, so it turns into a press.
how.easier: Do Pec deck instead, which guides the arc for you.
how.harder: Pause for a second in the stretch.

how.gist: Between two high cables, sweep your hands down and together in front of your hips, then let them open back out slowly.
steps: Set both pulleys high, take a handle in each hand and step forward into a split stance.
Lean slightly forward, arms out wide with a soft bend in the elbows.
Sweep your hands down and in until they meet in front of your hips.
Let your arms open back out slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest.
how.watch: Bending the elbows and rolling the shoulders forward, so it becomes a press.

how.gist: Sitting in the machine, bring the handles together in front of your chest, then let them open under control.
steps: Set the seat so the handles are at chest height and sit with your back flat on the pad.
Take the handles with a slight bend in the elbows and your shoulders down.
Squeeze the handles together in an arc until they meet in front of you.
Let them open slowly until you feel a stretch, without letting the stack touch down.
how.watch: Shoulders shrugging up and forward as the handles come together.

how.gist: Sitting in the machine, press the handles forward to straight arms and let them come back under control.
steps: Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.
Sit back with your shoulder blades against the pad and feet flat.
Press the handles forward until your arms are straight, without slamming the elbows locked.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest.
how.watch: Shoulders rolling forward off the pad as you press.
how.harder: Do Bench press instead.

how.gist: From a straight-body plank on your hands, lower your chest to just above the floor and push back up.
steps: Set your hands just wider than your shoulders, body straight from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your stomach.
Lower until your chest is just above the floor, elbows about 45° from your body.
Push the floor away until your arms are straight.
how.watch: Hips sagging toward the floor.
how.easier: Do Incline push-up or Knee push-up instead.
how.harder: Do Decline push-up, or rest a weight plate on your upper back.

how.gist: A push-up with your hands on a bench, box or bar, which takes some of your weight off your arms.
steps: Put your hands just wider than your shoulders on a sturdy bench, box or bar.
Walk your feet back until your body is straight from head to heels.
Lower your chest to the edge, elbows about 45° from your body.
Push back to straight arms.
how.watch: Hips sagging or piking up as you tire.
how.easier: Use a higher surface, or do Wall push-up.
how.harder: Use a lower surface each week until you can do a Push-up.

how.gist: A push-up with your feet up on a bench or box, which puts more of your weight on your hands and upper chest.
steps: Put your feet on a bench or box and your hands on the floor just wider than your shoulders.
Brace so your body is straight from head to heels.
Lower until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push back up to straight arms.
how.watch: Hips sagging so the low back arches.
how.easier: Use a lower step, or do Push-up.
how.harder: Raise your feet higher, or wear a weighted vest.

how.gist: Supported on parallel bars, lean forward and lower until your shoulders are just below your elbows, then press back up.
steps: Grip the bars and press up to straight arms, shoulders pushed down away from your ears.
Lean your chest forward a little and let your elbows flare slightly.
Lower under control until your shoulders are just below your elbows, or as low as is comfortable.
Press back up to straight arms.
how.watch: Dropping too deep with the shoulders rolling forward at the bottom.
how.easier: Use a band or the assisted machine, or practise Dip support hold.
how.harder: Add weight with a dip belt.

video.title: How To Do Dips For A Bigger Chest and Shoulders (Fix Mistakes!)

how.gist: Lying on a bench, lower a weight in an arc behind your head with nearly straight arms, then pull it back over your chest.
steps: Lie on a bench holding one dumbbell by its end in both hands, arms over your chest.
Keep a slight bend in the elbows and your ribs pulled down.
Lower the weight back over your head in an arc until your upper arms are beside your ears.
Pull it back over your chest along the same arc.
how.watch: Low back arching and ribs flaring as the weight goes behind your head.

video.title: The Dumbbell Pullover

how.gist: Squeeze a plate between flat palms at your chest and press it straight out and back without easing the squeeze.
steps: Stand tall holding a plate (or two small ones) pressed between flat palms at your chest.
Squeeze your palms together as hard as you can.
Keep squeezing as you push the plate straight out until your arms are straight.
Bring it back to your chest, still squeezing.
how.watch: The squeeze going slack, so it is only holding a plate out.

video.title: Svend Press | Exercise Guide

how.gist: Holding the end of a landmine bar in front of your shoulder, press it up and forward to a straight arm, then lower it.
steps: Fix one end of a barbell in a landmine and stand facing the loaded end.
Hold the end in one hand (or both) just in front of your shoulder, feet staggered.
Brace and press up and forward until your arm is straight, letting the shoulder blade reach.
Lower it back to the front of your shoulder under control.
how.watch: Standing at the wrong distance, so the bar starts away from your shoulder.
how.easier: Do it half-kneeling to keep your hips and back still.

video.title: How to Set-up the Landmine Press Effectively

how.gist: Stand facing a wall with your hands on it at shoulder height, bend your elbows to bring your chest to the wall, then push back.
steps: Stand an arm's length from a wall, hands flat on it at shoulder height, a little wider than your shoulders.
Keep your body straight from head to heels; let your heels lift.
Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall.
Push back until your arms are straight.
how.watch: Hips sagging or sticking out, so the body bends in the middle.
how.harder: Do Incline push-ups on a bench or table instead.

how.gist: From your knees, lower your chest to the floor in one straight line from knees to head, then push back up.
steps: Kneel and put your hands on the floor a little wider than your shoulders.
Walk your hands forward until your body is straight from knees to head.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest to just above the floor, elbows about 45° from your sides.
Push the floor away until your arms are straight.
how.watch: Hips bending, so the bottom stays up while the chest drops.
how.easier: Do Incline push-ups instead.
how.harder: Do full Push-ups.

how.gist: A push-up with your hands well outside your shoulders, lowering your chest between them.
steps: Set up in a push-up with your hands about one and a half times shoulder width.
Brace so your body is straight from head to heels.
Lower your chest toward the floor between your hands, elbows bending out to the sides.
Push back up until your arms are straight.
how.watch: Shoulders shrugging up toward the ears at the bottom.
how.easier: Do Knee push-ups with the same wide hands.
how.harder: Do Archer push-ups.

how.gist: With hands very wide, lower toward one hand while the other arm stays straight, push back up, and alternate sides.
steps: Set up in a push-up with your hands about twice shoulder width, fingers turned out.
Shift toward one hand and bend that elbow as you lower your chest beside it.
Keep the other arm straight as a light support.
Push back to the middle and switch sides.
how.watch: Hips twisting and sagging as you shift sideways.
how.easier: Do Wide push-ups, or let the support arm bend a little.
how.harder: Do One-arm push-ups.

video.title: Archer Push Ups | Correct Form Tutorial

how.gist: With feet wide and one hand under your chest, lower and push up on that one arm while your hips stay square to the floor.
steps: Set your feet wider than your shoulders and one hand under your chest; put the other hand behind your back.
Brace hard so your body is straight and your hips level.
Lower until your chest is a fist from the floor, elbow tucking toward your side.
Push back up without letting your hips twist or rise.
how.watch: Hips and torso rotating open as you push up.
how.easier: Do Archer push-ups, or put the hand on a bench.
how.harder: Bring your feet closer together.

video.title: How To One Arm Push-Up For Beginners

how.gist: A push-up with your hands beside your waist and your shoulders leaning forward past them, keeping that lean the whole rep.
steps: Set up in a push-up with your hands beside your waist, fingers turned out or back.
Lean forward until your shoulders are in front of your hands.
Lower your chest toward the floor, elbows close to your sides, without losing the lean.
Push back up to straight arms, still leaning forward.
how.watch: Shoulders drifting back over the hands as you tire, turning it into a normal push-up.
how.easier: Lean less far forward, or hold a Planche lean first.
how.harder: Lean further forward, or raise your feet.

video.title: Pseudo Planche Push Ups Tutorial for Beginners

how.gist: Push up hard enough for your hands to leave the floor, clap once, and catch yourself on soft elbows into the next rep.
steps: Start in a push-up with your body straight.
Lower under control, then push the floor away as fast as you can.
While your hands are in the air, clap once and bring them back under your shoulders.
Land with elbows slightly bent and sink straight into the next rep.
how.watch: Hips sagging, and landing on locked elbows.
how.easier: Push up explosively without the clap, or do them from your knees.
how.harder: Raise your feet on a bench.

video.title: Clapping Pushups | Freeletics 2 Minutes to Master

how.gist: From hips high in an upside-down V, swoop your chest down and forward along the floor into an arch, then push your hips back up.
steps: Start in a push-up with feet wider than hips, then push your hips up into an upside-down V.
Bend your elbows and dive your chest forward and down, skimming close to the floor between your hands.
Keep moving forward and straighten your arms so your chest lifts and your hips sink toward the floor.
Push your hips back up and back into the upside-down V for the next rep.
how.watch: Dropping straight down at the bottom instead of sweeping forward close to the floor.
how.easier: Make the swoop smaller, keeping your chest higher off the floor.

video.title: How to do the Hindu Pushup - and Why!

how.gist: Support yourself on top of a single straight bar, lower until it touches your lower chest, and press back up.
steps: Jump up to support on the bar, hands shoulder-width, arms straight, bar at your hips.
Lean your chest forward over the bar and let your legs come slightly forward for balance.
Bend your elbows to lower until the bar meets your lower chest.
Press back up to straight arms.
how.watch: Shoulders shrugging up to the ears at the bottom.
how.easier: Do Chest dips on parallel bars first.
how.harder: Learn the Muscle-up.

video.title: Straight Bar Dips Tutorial (Form & Progression)

exercises.name: Squeeze press
exercises.equipment: Dumbbells or a plate, and a bench

how.gist: Lie on a bench and press two dumbbells held together over your chest, squeezing them into each other the whole time.
steps: Lie on a bench holding two dumbbells together over your chest, palms facing each other.
Squeeze the dumbbells hard into each other and keep that squeeze for the whole set.
Lower them together to your mid-chest, elbows tucked close to your sides.
Press back up to straight arms without letting the dumbbells drift apart.
how.watch: The dumbbells drifting apart as you press, so the squeeze is lost.
how.easier: Squeeze one plate between flat palms instead of two dumbbells.
how.harder: Do it on an incline bench, or pause 2 seconds at the chest.

video.title: Dumbbell Chest Squeeze Press: Technique, Sets, Reps & Mistakes

how.gist: Lift a loaded barbell from the floor to standing by pushing through your legs with a flat back, then lower it.
steps: Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet, feet about hip-width apart.
Bend down and grip the bar just outside your legs, arms straight.
Bend your knees until your shins touch the bar, then lift your chest so your back is flat.
Push the floor away and drag the bar up your legs until you stand tall.
Lower it the same way: hips back first, then bend your knees once the bar passes them.
how.watch: The bar drifting away from your legs and your back rounding.
how.easier: Learn it with Trap-bar deadlift, or pull from blocks.
how.harder: Do Deficit deadlift, standing on a plate.

video.title: Learning to Deadlift | The Starting Strength Method

how.gist: A deadlift with a wide stance and hands inside your knees: push your knees out and stand up with the bar close.
steps: Stand wide with your toes turned out, shins close to the bar, bar over the middle of your feet.
Reach down between your legs and grip the bar about shoulder width.
Push your knees out over your toes, drop your hips and lift your chest.
Push the floor apart and stand straight up, keeping the bar against your legs.
Lower it under control with your knees still pushed out.
how.watch: Knees caving in as the bar leaves the floor.
how.harder: Pause for a second just after the bar leaves the floor.

video.title: HOW TO SUMO DEADLIFT ft. Larry

how.gist: Stand inside a trap bar, grip the handles at your sides, and stand up by driving through your legs with a flat back.
steps: Stand in the middle of the trap bar, feet hip-width, handles in line with the middle of your feet.
Hinge and bend your knees to grip the centre of the handles, arms straight.
Lift your chest so your back is flat, hips between your knees and shoulders.
Push the floor away and stand tall, then lower the bar the same way.
how.watch: Hips shooting up first so the back does the lifting.
how.harder: Do Deadlift with a straight bar.

video.title: The Trap Bar Deadlift

how.gist: A deadlift started from safety pins or blocks at about knee height, for the top part of the pull.
steps: Set the bar on pins or blocks at or just below your knees.
Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet and grip it just outside your legs.
Push your hips back, flatten your back and pull the slack out of the bar.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, then lower it back to the pins under control.
how.watch: Leaning back at the top instead of finishing straight.
how.harder: Lower the pins step by step toward a full Deadlift.

video.title: How to Rack Pull with Mark Rippetoe

how.gist: Hinge forward with a flat back and row the weight to your lower ribs, then lower it to straight arms.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width, grip just wider than shoulder width, and soften your knees.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is at about 45° or lower, back flat, weight hanging.
Pull the weight to your lower ribs, driving your elbows back past your body.
Lower it under control to straight arms without standing up.
how.watch: Standing more upright each rep and heaving the weight with your hips.
how.easier: Do Chest-supported row, which takes the low back out of it.

how.gist: With your back near parallel to the floor, row the bar from a dead stop on the floor to your lower chest, every rep.
steps: Set up as for a deadlift, but with your hips higher and back nearly parallel to the floor.
Grip a little wider than shoulder width, arms straight and back flat.
Pull the bar fast from the floor to your lower chest or upper stomach.
Lower it back to the floor, let it settle, and reset before the next rep.
how.watch: Lifting the chest and torso to help the bar up.

video.title: How to Perform the Pendlay Row - Exercise Tutorial

how.gist: With one hand and knee on a bench, row a dumbbell from a straight arm up to your hip, then lower it.
steps: Put one knee and the same-side hand on a bench, back flat and roughly parallel to the floor.
Hold the dumbbell in your other hand, arm hanging straight below the shoulder.
Row it up toward your hip, elbow close to your side.
Lower it to a full stretch, finish the set and switch sides.
how.watch: Twisting the torso open to swing the weight up.

how.gist: Lying chest-down on an incline bench or machine pad, row the weights up and lower them to straight arms.
steps: Set a bench to about 30–45° and lie chest-down with your chin just over the top.
Let the weights hang straight down, shoulders relaxed forward.
Row your elbows back and up until the weights reach your sides.
Lower them to straight arms under control.
how.watch: Lifting your chest off the pad to heave the weight.

how.gist: Sitting with feet braced, pull the handle to your stomach with a tall chest, then let your arms straighten slowly.
steps: Sit with your feet on the platform, knees slightly bent, and take the handle with straight arms.
Sit tall with your chest up and torso upright.
Pull the handle to your stomach, elbows driving back close to your sides.
Let your arms straighten slowly, allowing your shoulder blades to slide forward.
how.watch: Rocking the torso back and forth to move the weight.

exercises.equipment: Landmine and V-handle, or T-bar machine

how.gist: Straddling a landmine bar, hinge forward and row the loaded end to your chest with a handle, then lower it.
steps: Load one end of a landmine bar and straddle it, facing the plates.
Hook a V-handle under the bar by the plates and hinge with a flat back, knees soft.
Row the plates up toward your chest, elbows driving back.
Lower to straight arms under control, keeping the same back angle.
how.watch: Jerking the weight up with the hips and legs.

video.title: T-BAR ROW | Back | How-To Exercise Tutorial

how.gist: Side-on to a landmine bar, grip its fat end in one hand and row it toward your back hip with your back flat.
steps: Stand side-on to the loaded end of a landmine bar, the leg nearer the bar forward.
Hinge, rest that forearm on your front knee, and grip the thick end overhand with your other hand.
Row the end up toward your back hip, elbow flaring slightly out.
Lower it until your arm is straight and your shoulder blade stretches forward.
how.watch: Twisting the torso up toward the bar to finish the rep.

video.title: How to Meadows Row "The Right Way"

exercises.equipment: High flat bench, barbell or dumbbells

how.gist: Lying face down on a raised flat bench, row a barbell or dumbbells up to the bench, then lower to straight arms.
steps: Raise a flat bench on blocks so your arms can hang straight without the weight touching the floor.
Lie face down with your chest at one end and the weight hanging under your shoulders.
Row the weight up until it touches the underside of the bench.
Lower it to straight arms under control.
how.watch: Lifting your chest or head off the bench to heave the weight up.
how.easier: Do Chest-supported row on an incline bench.

video.title: Exercise Index - Seal Rows

how.gist: Hanging under a bar with your body straight and heels on the floor, pull your chest up to the bar, then lower.
steps: Set a bar at about waist height, lie under it and grip it a little wider than shoulder width.
Straighten your body from head to heels, heels on the floor.
Pull your chest to the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower until your arms are straight.
how.watch: Hips sagging so only the chest moves.
how.easier: Bend your knees, or raise the bar so you are more upright.
how.harder: Put your feet on a box, or wear a weighted vest.

how.gist: From a high plank holding two dumbbells, row one to your hip without letting your hips twist, then switch sides.
steps: Get into a high plank with your hands on two dumbbells, feet wider than hip-width.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes so your body is straight.
Row one weight to your hip while pushing the other hand into the floor.
Set it down under control and row with the other side.
how.watch: Hips rotating and rising as the weight comes up.
how.easier: Do it from your knees, or set your feet wider.

video.title: Renegade Row Guide | Form Tips, Muscles Worked, and Variations

how.gist: Hang from a bar with palms facing away and pull until your chin clears the bar, then lower to straight arms.
steps: Grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders, palms facing away, and hang with straight arms.
Pull your shoulders down away from your ears to start.
Drive your elbows down toward your ribs until your chin is over the bar.
Lower under control all the way to straight arms.
how.watch: Stopping short at the bottom, so the arms never straighten.
how.easier: Use a band or the assisted machine, or do Negative pull-up.
how.harder: Add weight with a belt, or do Archer pull-up.

how.gist: Hang from a bar with palms facing you and pull until your chin is over it, then lower to straight arms.
steps: Grip the bar about shoulder width, palms facing you, and hang with straight arms.
Brace your stomach and pull your shoulders down.
Pull your elbows down to your sides until your chin is over the bar.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
how.watch: Swinging or kicking the legs to get over the bar.
how.easier: Use a band or the assisted machine, or do Flexed-arm hang.
how.harder: Add weight with a belt or vest.

how.gist: A pull-up on parallel handles with palms facing each other: pull your chin over your hands, then lower to straight arms.
steps: Hang from parallel handles, palms facing each other, arms straight.
Pull your shoulders down away from your ears.
Pull until your chin is above your hands, elbows close to your sides.
Lower under control to straight arms.
how.watch: Half reps that stop before the arms straighten.
how.easier: Use a band or the assisted machine, or do Negative pull-up.
how.harder: Add weight with a belt or vest.

how.gist: A pull-up with your hands well wider than your shoulders: pull until your chin clears the bar, then lower.
steps: Grip the bar about one and a half times shoulder width, palms facing away.
Hang with straight arms, then pull your shoulders down.
Pull your elbows down and out until your chin clears the bar.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
how.watch: A grip so wide that each rep shrinks to a few inches.
how.easier: Use a band, or do Pull-up with a normal grip.

how.gist: Seated under the pulldown, pull the bar to your upper chest with a tall chest, then let it rise to straight arms.
steps: Set the knee pad snug and grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders.
Sit tall and lean back slightly, arms straight.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, driving your elbows down toward your ribs.
Let it rise under control until your arms are straight.
how.watch: Leaning far back and swinging the weight down with your body.
how.harder: Do Pull-up.

how.gist: Facing a high cable, keep your arms straight and sweep the bar down to your thighs, then let it rise.
steps: Fix a bar or rope at the top of a cable and step back so the cable is taut.
Hinge slightly forward, arms straight out in front, elbows soft.
Sweep the bar down in an arc to your thighs, arms staying straight.
Let it rise until your arms are about at eye level.
how.watch: Bending the elbows so it turns into a pushdown.

how.gist: Holding weights with straight arms, lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears, pause, and lower.
steps: Stand tall holding the weights with straight arms.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Pause for a second at the top.
Lower all the way down until you feel a stretch.
how.watch: Rolling the shoulders in circles instead of straight up and down.

how.gist: On a back-extension bench, bend forward at the hips, then raise your body back up to a straight line.
steps: Set the pad just below your hip bones so you can bend freely at the hips, ankles hooked.
Cross your arms on your chest and keep your body straight.
Lower your torso by bending at the hips until you feel your hamstrings stretch.
Raise back up until your body is in a straight line, and stop there.
how.watch: Arching past straight at the top.
how.easier: Do Superman on the floor.
how.harder: Hold a weight plate to your chest.

video.title: STOP Doing Back Extensions Like This!

how.gist: With a bar across your upper back, push your hips back and lean forward with a flat back, then stand back up.
steps: Set the bar on your upper back as for a squat, feet hip-width, knees soft.
Brace your stomach and push your hips straight back.
Lean forward until you feel a strong hamstring stretch or your torso nears parallel.
Drive your hips forward to stand up, keeping your back flat.
how.watch: Rounding the back to reach lower.
how.easier: Learn the pattern with Dowel hip hinge first.

video.title: HOW TO DO THE GOOD MORNING EXERCISE: Build Your Glutes, Hamstrings And Squat With Perfect Technique

how.gist: Hanging from a bar with straight arms, pull your shoulders down away from your ears to rise a little, then lower.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms, shoulders up by your ears.
Keeping your elbows straight, pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Your body rises an inch or two; hold it for a second.
Lower slowly back into the full hang.
how.watch: Bending the elbows, so it turns into a small pull-up.
how.easier: Keep your feet on a box or use a band to take some weight.
how.harder: Hold the top for five seconds each rep, then build to an Active hang.

video.title: Fix Your Pull Ups with Scapula Pull Ups | Tim Keeley | Physio REHAB

how.gist: Jump or step up to the top of a pull-up, chin over the bar, and lower yourself as slowly as you can to a straight-arm hang.
steps: Stand on a box under the bar and grip it slightly wider than your shoulders.
Jump or step up until your chin is over the bar, elbows at your sides.
Lower yourself slowly, taking 3 to 5 seconds, until your arms are straight.
Step back onto the box and repeat.
how.watch: Dropping fast through the bottom half instead of controlling the whole way.
how.easier: Do a Flexed-arm hang, or lower with a band.
how.harder: Do Pull-ups.

video.title: How To Do a Negative Pull-Up | Exercise Guide

how.gist: With a very wide grip, pull up toward one hand while the other arm straightens along the bar, lower, then switch sides.
steps: Hang with your hands about twice shoulder width, palms facing away.
Pull your chest toward one hand, bending that arm.
Let the other arm straighten out along the bar as you rise; it only helps a little.
Lower under control and pull to the other side next.
how.watch: Both arms bending equally, so it becomes a plain wide pull-up.
how.easier: Do Wide-grip pull-ups, or keep the helping arm slightly bent.
how.harder: Push less with the straight arm, working toward a one-arm pull-up.

video.title: How to archer pull ups? | Archer pull ups tutorial

how.gist: Hold your legs straight out in front at hip height and do pull-ups without letting them drop.
steps: Hang from the bar and raise your straight legs until they point forward, level with your hips.
Lock your knees and point your toes.
Pull up until your chin clears the bar, legs staying level.
Lower to straight arms, keeping the L for the next rep.
how.watch: Legs dropping and swinging as you pull.
how.easier: Bend your knees into a tuck, or practise the L-sit on the floor.

video.title: How to L-Sit Pull Up | Full Guide + Progressions

how.gist: A pull-up that goes higher, until your chest touches the bar, elbows driving down and behind you.
steps: Hang from the bar, hands a little wider than your shoulders.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back, then drive your elbows toward your back pockets.
Lean back slightly and pull until your upper chest touches the bar.
Lower under control to straight arms.
how.watch: Chin pushing forward to reach for the bar while the chest stops short.
how.easier: Do Pull-ups to the chin first.
how.harder: Learn the Muscle-up.

video.title: The Strict Chest-to-Bar Pull-Up

how.gist: A CrossFit gymnastics pull-up that uses a swing from arch to hollow to drive the chin over the bar, for fast reps.
steps: Build strict Pull-ups first; the kip adds speed, not strength.
Hang with active shoulders and swing between an arch (chest through) and a hollow (legs forward).
From the arch, snap into the hollow and pull, letting the hip drive lift your chin over the bar.
Push away from the bar at the top and swing back into the arch for the next rep.
how.watch: Swinging on loose shoulders, so they jerk at the bottom of each rep.
how.easier: Do strict Pull-ups, or practise the kip swing on its own.
how.harder: Kip into Chest-to-bar pull-ups.

video.title: The Kipping Pull-up

how.gist: Hang from a bar on straight arms and pull your shoulders down away from your ears, then hold that position.
steps: Grip the bar shoulder-width, palms away, and hang with straight arms.
Without bending your elbows, pull your shoulders down so your body rises slightly.
Keep your legs together and ribs down so you do not swing.
Hold for the time, then relax into a Dead hang or step down.
how.watch: Bending the elbows to help, which turns it into a small pull-up.
how.easier: Keep your toes on a box to take some of your weight.
how.harder: Do Scapular pull-ups, then a Flexed-arm hang and Negative pull-ups.

video.title: Active Hang for Pull-Up Strength

how.gist: Hold yourself at the top of a pull-up, chin above the bar, for as long as you can.
steps: Grip the bar, palms toward or away from you, and step or jump up until your chin is over it.
Pull your elbows down to your sides and keep your chest up.
Hold still without resting your chin on the bar.
When you can no longer hold, lower slowly to straight arms.
how.watch: Head tipping back to keep the chin up as the arms tire.
how.easier: Hold lower, with your elbows at 90°.
how.harder: Finish each hold with a Negative pull-up.

video.channel: U.S. Army Holistic Health and Fitness
video.title: Climbing Drill 2 Exercise 1 - Flexed Arm Hang

how.gist: Climb a hanging rope by locking it between your feet and standing up on it, then reaching higher; climb down the same way.
steps: Reach high, grip the rope and pull your knees up, the rope between your legs.
Run the rope over the outside of one foot and under it, then clamp it with your other foot on top.
Stand up on the locked rope and reach your hands higher.
Repeat to the top, then come down hand under hand, re-locking your feet; do not slide.
how.watch: Pulling with the arms alone and skipping the foot lock, which burns out the grip.
how.easier: Practise the foot lock low on the rope before climbing.
how.harder: Climb with your arms only, legs off the rope.

video.title: The Rope Climb (J-Hook)

how.gist: Hinge over two kettlebells between your feet and row them one at a time, pushing the other bell into the floor.
steps: Stand wide with two kettlebells between your feet, handles in line with your insteps.
Hinge until your back is nearly flat, knees bent, and grip both handles.
Push one bell into the floor and row the other to your hip, elbow close to your side.
Lower it under control to the floor, then row with the other arm.
how.watch: Twisting the torso to heave the bell up instead of keeping the shoulders square.
how.easier: Do a Single-arm row with one hand on a bench.
how.harder: Use heavier bells and pause one second at the hip.

video.title: The Kettlebell Gorilla Row

how.gist: Deadlift with a wide, snatch-width grip, which starts you lower and makes your upper back work harder.
steps: Grip the bar wide: standing with straight arms, it should sit in the crease of your hips.
Set your hips lower than in a normal deadlift, shins to the bar, chest up, back flat.
Pull your shoulders down and back, then push the floor away, keeping the bar close.
Stand tall with your hips through, then lower it along the same path.
how.watch: Hips shooting up first, so the back rounds and the bar drifts forward.
how.easier: Use a normal grip: the Deadlift.
how.harder: Stand on a 1–2 in plate: a Deficit deadlift with a snatch grip.

video.title: Increase Your Deadlift : How To Snatch Grip Deadlift

exercises.name: Deficit deadlift
exercises.equipment: Bar and a low platform or plates

how.gist: Deadlift while standing on a platform 1–3 in high, so the bar starts lower and every rep is a longer pull.
steps: Stand on a sturdy plate or platform 1–3 in high, mid-foot under the bar.
Grip the bar with hips a little lower than usual, back flat, shins touching the bar.
Push the floor away and keep the bar dragging up your legs.
Lock out with hips and knees together, then lower it to the floor under control.
how.watch: Standing on too high a deficit, so the back rounds at the start.
how.easier: Use a smaller deficit, or do a normal Deadlift.
how.harder: Take a wide grip from the deficit, as in the Snatch-grip deadlift.

video.title: How To Deficit Deadlift - Stronger Off the Floor to INCREASE YOUR DEADLIFT

how.gist: Lie face down and lift your arms, chest and legs a little off the floor together, hold briefly, then lower.
steps: Lie face down, arms straight out past your head, legs straight.
Keep your eyes on the floor and squeeze your glutes.
Lift arms, chest and legs a few inches off the floor together and hold 2–3 seconds.
Lower slowly and take a breath before the next rep.
how.watch: Cranking the head up and crunching the low back instead of reaching long.
how.easier: Lift one arm and the opposite leg at a time, or do a Bird dog.
how.harder: Hold a light plate in your hands, or hold the top for longer.

video.title: How to do a Superman | The Right Way | Well+Good

how.gist: Lie face down, lift your arms just off the floor and sweep them in a wide arc from your hips to overhead and back.
steps: Lie face down, forehead on the floor or a towel, arms by your sides, palms down.
Lift your arms and chest slightly and draw your shoulder blades back and down.
Sweep both arms out to the sides and overhead in a wide arc, keeping them off the floor.
Reverse the arc back to your hips slowly and repeat.
how.watch: Hands dropping to the floor as the arms pass shoulder height.
how.easier: Keep your chest on the floor and lift only the arms.
how.harder: Hold very light plates or dumbbells.

video.title: Reverse Snow Angels | CrossFit Invictus Gymnastics

how.gist: Standing, press the bar from your collarbones to straight arms overhead, moving your head out of its way.
steps: Take the bar out of the rack at your collarbones, hands just outside your shoulders, forearms vertical.
Stand with feet hip-width, squeeze your glutes and brace your stomach.
Press the bar straight up, pulling your chin back so it passes your face.
Once it passes your forehead, push your head forward under the bar and lock your arms.
Lower it back to your collarbones under control.
how.watch: Leaning back hard so it turns into an incline press.
how.easier: Do Seated shoulder press with dumbbells.
how.harder: Do Z press, sitting on the floor with no back support.

video.title: Learning to Press | The Starting Strength Method

exercises.equipment: Upright bench and dumbbells or barbell

how.gist: Sitting upright with your back supported, press the weights from shoulder height to straight arms overhead.
steps: Set a bench upright and sit with your back against it, feet flat.
Hold the weights at shoulder height, palms forward, forearms vertical.
Press up until your arms are straight over your shoulders.
Lower back to about chin height under control.
how.watch: Arching the low back off the pad to finish the rep.
how.harder: Do Overhead press standing.

how.gist: Start with dumbbells in front of your shoulders, palms facing you, and turn them palms-forward as you press overhead.
steps: Sit or stand holding the dumbbells in front of your shoulders, palms facing you, elbows in front.
Start pressing up while opening your elbows out to the sides.
Turn your palms forward as you go, finishing with straight arms overhead.
Reverse the same path on the way down, back to palms facing you.
how.watch: Turning first and pressing after, instead of one smooth movement.

how.gist: Dip at the knees and drive up through your legs to launch the bar overhead, then finish the press with your arms.
steps: Hold the bar on your shoulders with elbows slightly forward, feet hip-width.
Dip a few inches by bending your knees, torso upright and heels down.
Drive straight up hard through your legs to push the bar off your shoulders.
Finish pressing to straight arms, head pushed forward under the bar.
Lower it back to your shoulders, softening your knees to absorb it.
how.watch: Dipping forward onto the toes, so the bar drives out in front.
how.harder: Do Push jerk, dropping under the bar.

video.title: Push Press | Olympic Weightlifting Exercise Library

how.gist: Hold a kettlebell upside down by its handle, bell pointing up, and press it overhead without letting it tip.
steps: Bring the kettlebell to your shoulder, handle squeezed hard, bell pointing at the ceiling.
Keep your forearm vertical and wrist straight, elbow under the handle.
Brace and press straight up, keeping the bell balanced over your fist.
Lower it slowly back to your shoulder.
how.watch: A loose grip that lets the bell flop over.
how.easier: Use a lighter bell half-kneeling, or just hold it at your shoulder.

video.title: Bottom Up Press - Build Shoulder Stability FAST!

how.gist: Sitting in the machine, press the handles overhead to straight arms and lower them under control.
steps: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Sit with your back flat against the pad, feet planted.
Press the handles up until your arms are straight.
Lower them slowly back to shoulder height.
how.watch: Arching the low back off the pad as the weight gets heavy.

how.gist: Raise the weights out to your sides with soft elbows up to shoulder height, then lower them slowly.
steps: Stand tall with the weights at your sides and a slight bend in your elbows.
Lean forward a touch and lead with your elbows out to the sides.
Raise until your arms are about level with your shoulders.
Lower slowly, without letting the weights drop.
how.watch: Shrugging and swinging the body to get the weight up.
how.harder: Do Lu raise, carrying on up overhead.

how.gist: Raise the weight straight out in front of you to shoulder height with nearly straight arms, then lower it.
steps: Stand tall holding the weight in front of your thighs, elbows soft.
Brace so your torso does not move.
Raise the weight forward until your arms are level with your shoulders.
Lower slowly back to your thighs.
how.watch: Leaning back and swinging the weight up.

how.gist: Bent forward with a flat back, open your arms out to the sides with soft elbows, then lower them.
steps: Hinge forward until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, weights hanging below your chest.
Soften your elbows and keep that angle throughout.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they are level with your body.
Lower slowly back down.
how.watch: Bending the elbows more and rowing the weight up.
how.easier: Lie chest-down on an incline bench to hold the position.

how.gist: Holding the weight in front of your thighs, pull it up close to your body until your elbows reach shoulder height.
steps: Stand holding the weight in front of your thighs, hands about shoulder width or a little wider.
Lead with your elbows and pull the weight up close to your body.
Stop when your elbows reach about shoulder height, elbows above your wrists.
Lower under control to straight arms.
how.watch: A narrow grip and the elbows pulled up above the shoulders.

video.title: How To Fix The Upright Row: Avoid Shoulder Pain & Maximize Growth

how.gist: Pull a rope from a high cable toward your face, hands finishing beside your ears, then let it return.
steps: Set a rope at about face height and hold it with palms facing down or in.
Step back until your arms are straight and the cable is taut, and stand tall.
Pull the rope toward your face, elbows high and wide.
Finish with your hands beside your ears, knuckles pointing back, then return slowly.
how.watch: Leaning back and pulling with the body instead of the shoulders.

video.title: How To: Face Pull

how.gist: Hold a band at shoulder height with straight arms and pull it apart until it touches your chest, then return.
steps: Hold a light band in front of you at shoulder height, hands about shoulder width.
Keep your arms straight and your shoulders down.
Pull the band apart by sweeping your arms out to the sides until it touches your chest.
Return slowly to the start.
how.watch: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.
how.harder: Use a stronger band, or hold the end position for two seconds.

video.title: How to Do Band Pull Aparts: A Guide from Physical Therapists

how.gist: With your elbow tucked at your side and bent to 90°, rotate your forearm outward against the load, then back in.
steps: Stand side-on to a cable or band set at elbow height, holding it in your far hand.
Tuck a rolled towel between elbow and side, elbow at 90°, forearm across your stomach.
Rotate your forearm out away from your body, keeping the elbow pinned to your side.
Return slowly to the start.
With a dumbbell, do the same lying on your side, the top arm working.
how.watch: The elbow drifting away from your side to swing the weight.

video.title: Shoulder External Rotation (With Cable)

how.gist: With your elbow tucked at your side and bent to 90°, rotate your forearm in across your body, then back out.
steps: Stand side-on to a cable or band set at elbow height, holding it in your near hand.
Tuck a rolled towel between elbow and side, elbow at 90°, forearm turned out toward the cable.
Rotate your forearm in across your stomach, keeping the elbow pinned.
Return slowly to the start.
how.watch: Twisting the torso to pull the handle in.

how.gist: Upright row to elbows at shoulder height, rotate your forearms up to vertical, then press overhead; reverse to lower.
steps: Stand holding light weights in front of your thighs, overhand grip.
Pull them up until your upper arms are level with your shoulders, elbows bent 90°.
Keeping your elbows still, rotate your forearms up until they point at the ceiling.
Press the weights overhead, then reverse each step to lower.
how.watch: Elbows dropping as the forearms rotate up.

video.title: The Cuban Press

how.gist: Lying on your side, raise a light dumbbell from hanging toward the floor in front of you until it points at the ceiling.
steps: Lie on your side on a flat or slightly inclined bench, head resting on your lower hand.
Hold a light dumbbell in your top hand, arm straight and hanging toward the floor in front of you.
Keeping your elbow straight, raise the weight in a straight line until your arm points at the ceiling.
Pause, then lower it slowly to the start.
how.watch: Rolling your body back to help the weight up.

video.title: Exercise Tutorial: Powell Raise

how.gist: Lying face down with one arm hanging off a bench, raise it forward and up at 45° from your head, thumb up.
steps: Lie face down on a flat bench, forehead on your other forearm, working arm hanging off the side.
Hold a light weight with a straight arm, thumb pointing up as you lift.
Draw the shoulder blade down, then raise the arm forward and up at 45° out from your head.
Lift to about ear height, pause, and lower slowly.
how.watch: Shrugging the shoulder up toward the ear as the arm lifts.
how.easier: Do it with no weight.
how.harder: Do Y raise, both arms on an incline bench.

video.title: Prone Lower Trap Raise

how.gist: Chest-down on an incline bench, raise straight arms up and out into a Y beside your head, thumbs up, then lower.
steps: Set a bench to about 30–45° and lie chest-down, feet on the floor, light weights hanging.
Turn your thumbs up and keep your arms straight.
Raise your arms up and out into a Y shape, in line with your ears.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
how.watch: Shrugging up toward the ears instead of drawing the shoulder blades down.
how.easier: Do it with no weight, or lying face down on the floor.

video.title: Dumbbell Y Raise on Incline Bench

how.gist: Chest-down on an incline bench, raise straight arms out to the sides into a T, squeezing your shoulder blades, then lower.
steps: Set a bench to about 30–45° and lie chest-down with light weights hanging below your shoulders.
Keep your arms straight with your thumbs pointing up.
Raise your arms straight out to the sides until they are level with your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, pause, and lower slowly.
how.watch: Bending the elbows and rowing the weight up.
how.easier: Do it with no weight, or lying face down on the floor.

video.title: Dumbbell T Raise on Incline Bench

how.gist: Chest-down on an incline bench with elbows bent 90°, raise your arms into a W, squeezing your shoulder blades, then lower.
steps: Lie chest-down on a bench set to about 30–45°, light weights hanging.
Bend your elbows to about 90° and tuck them a little toward your sides.
Lift elbows and hands up and back into a W, drawing your shoulder blades together and down.
Pause, then lower slowly.
how.watch: Shrugging up toward the ears as the arms lift.
how.easier: Do it with no weight, or lying face down on the floor.

video.title: How To: Incline Dumbbell W Raise

how.gist: In a high plank with straight arms, let your chest sink between your shoulder blades, then push the floor away to spread them.
steps: Get into a high plank, hands under your shoulders, body straight.
Keeping your elbows locked, let your chest sink so your shoulder blades squeeze together.
Push the floor away so your shoulder blades spread and your upper back rounds slightly.
Move slowly between the two; only the shoulder blades move.
how.watch: Bending the elbows, so it turns into a small push-up.
how.easier: Do it on your knees, or with your hands on a wall.
how.harder: Add the spread to the top of each Push-up.

video.title: 4 Scapular Pushup Progressions

how.gist: With your back against a wall and arms in a goalpost shape, slide your arms up into a Y and back down, keeping contact.
steps: Stand with your head, upper back and bottom against a wall, feet a little out from it.
Raise your arms into a goalpost shape, backs of elbows and wrists touching the wall.
Draw your ribs down and slide your arms up into a Y, keeping them on the wall.
Slide back down, pulling your shoulder blades down and back.
how.watch: The low back arching off the wall as the arms go up.
how.easier: Only go as high as you can keep elbows and wrists on the wall.
how.harder: At the top, lift your hands a little off the wall.

video.title: Fix Your Shoulders with Wall Slides - Excel Performance Training

how.gist: In a handstand with your heels against a wall, lower your head to the floor and press back up to straight arms.
steps: Put a folded mat by a wall and your hands just wider than your shoulders, a hand-length from the wall.
Kick up so your heels rest on the wall, arms straight and body tight.
Lower under control until the top of your head touches the mat, a little in front of your hands.
Press back up to straight arms.
how.watch: Dropping fast onto your head instead of lowering under control.
how.easier: Do Pike push-up or Elevated pike push-up instead.
how.harder: Stand your hands on plates or blocks to lower further.

video.title: The Strict Handstand Push-Up

how.gist: With your hips high in an upside-down V, bend your elbows to bring the top of your head toward the floor ahead of your hands.
steps: Start in a push-up, then walk your feet in and lift your hips into an upside-down V.
Keep your legs as straight as you can and your head between your arms.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head to a spot just ahead of your hands.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
how.watch: Hips dropping toward a plank as you lower, so the chest does the work.
how.easier: Lower only partway, or take some weight with a band.
how.harder: Do Elevated pike push-ups.

video.title: How to Master the Pike Pushup (Tutorial + Progressions)

how.gist: A pike push-up with your feet on a box, so your hips sit nearly over your hands and more of your weight is on the shoulders.
steps: Put your feet on a box or bench and walk your hands back until your hips are high, nearly over your shoulders.
Keep your back long and your head between your arms.
Bend your elbows to lower your head to a spot just in front of your hands.
Press back up to straight arms.
how.watch: Hands too far from the box, so the torso slants and the chest takes over.
how.easier: Do Pike push-ups on the floor.
how.harder: Do Handstand push-ups against a wall.

video.title: "Elevated" Pike Push-Up Technique

how.gist: From face down with your feet at a wall, push up and walk your feet up the wall as your hands walk in, until you are near a handstand.
steps: Lie face down with your feet against the base of the wall.
Push up into a plank, put your feet on the wall and start walking them up.
Walk your hands back toward the wall one step at a time, body tight.
Stop when your chest is close to the wall, then walk your hands out and feet down with control.
how.watch: Low back arching as your hands get close to the wall.
how.easier: Walk only partway up, then come back down.
how.harder: Pause at the top in a Handstand hold.

video.title: The Wall Walk

how.gist: Hold a straight-body handstand with your chest facing a wall, pushing tall through your shoulders.
steps: Get into a chest-to-wall handstand with a Wall walk, hands a short way from the wall.
Push the floor away so your shoulders reach up beside your ears.
Squeeze your legs together and pull your ribs in so your body forms one line.
Hold for the time, then walk down, or turn sideways to step off.
how.watch: A banana-shaped back, ribs flared and hips sagging toward the wall.
how.easier: Walk partway up the wall and hold there.
how.harder: Bring your hands closer to the wall, then take one foot off it.

video.title: Chest to Wall Handstand - Tutorial

how.gist: Squat with your hands on the floor, rest your knees high on your upper arms and lean forward until your feet lift.
steps: Squat with your feet together and plant your hands shoulder-width in front, fingers spread.
Bend your elbows a little and set your knees high on the backs of your upper arms.
Look a little ahead of your hands and shift your weight forward onto them.
Lift one foot, then the other, and hold with your upper back rounded.
how.watch: Not leaning far enough forward, so the feet never leave the floor.
how.easier: Lift one foot at a time, with a cushion in front of your face.
how.harder: Straighten your arms toward crane pose.

video.title: Crow Pose |  How To Do Crow Pose | Yoga With Adriene

how.gist: From a push-up position on straight arms, lean your shoulders forward past your hands and hold.
steps: Set up in a push-up with straight arms, fingers turned out or back.
Push the floor away so your upper back rounds slightly and your shoulder blades spread.
Lean forward on your toes until your shoulders are in front of your hands.
Keep your elbows locked and body straight, and hold for the time.
how.watch: Elbows bending, or shoulder blades sinking together, as you lean.
how.easier: Lean less far forward.
how.harder: Lean further, then move on to the Tuck planche.

video.title: How To Planche Lean | Tutorial & Progressions

how.gist: Balance on straight arms with your knees tucked to your chest, feet off the floor and hips at shoulder height.
steps: Squat and place your hands on the floor or parallettes, shoulder-width, fingers turned out.
Lock your elbows, push the floor away and round your upper back.
Lean forward until your shoulders pass your hands, knees pulled tight to your chest.
Lift your feet and raise your hips to shoulder height; hold, then put your feet down.
how.watch: Bending the elbows to get the feet up.
how.easier: Hold a Planche lean, or a tuck with your feet just off the floor.
how.harder: Open your hips and push your knees back toward an advanced tuck.

video.title: TUCK PLANCHE Step by Step

how.gist: Hang from rings, tuck and roll backward through your arms into a hang behind you, then pull back the way you came.
steps: Hang from rings or a bar with straight arms; start on low rings so your feet can touch down.
Pull your knees to your chest and keep rolling back so your legs pass between your arms.
Lower your legs slowly toward the floor behind you; stop where your shoulders feel a stretch.
Tuck tight again, lift your hips back through and return to the hang.
how.watch: Dropping into the bottom fast instead of lowering under control.
how.easier: Use low rings and keep your toes on the floor behind you.

video.title: How to Skin the Cat

how.gist: Sit on the floor with legs straight and press the weight overhead, with no backrest and no help from your legs.
steps: Sit tall on the floor, legs straight out in front and a little apart.
Hold the bar at your collarbones, or the bells at your shoulders.
Brace your trunk and press straight up until your arms lock out overhead.
Lower under control to the start without leaning back.
how.watch: Leaning back or slumping through the low back to get the weight up.
how.easier: Sit cross-legged, or do a Seated shoulder press with back support.
how.harder: Press one dumbbell at a time, so the trunk has to resist leaning.

video.title: How to Z Press CORRECTLY (Feat Pro Strongman Rob Kearney!!)

how.gist: Hold a kettlebell upside down by the horns and circle it close around your head, then go the other way.
steps: Stand tall holding a light kettlebell by the horns, bottom up, in front of your chest.
Keep your hips and low back still; only the arms move.
Circle the bell around your head, passing close behind your neck.
Bring it back to your chest and circle the other way; alternate each rep.
how.watch: Ducking the head out of the way instead of keeping it still and the bell close.
how.easier: Use a light plate, or do it kneeling.
how.harder: Use a heavier bell and slow each circle to about 4 seconds.

video.title: Kettlebell Halo | StrongFirst

how.gist: Raise light weights on straight arms out to your sides and all the way overhead, thumbs up, then lower slowly.
steps: Stand tall with light dumbbells or plates by your thighs, thumbs pointing forward.
Keep the arms straight and raise them out to the sides, a little in front of you.
Keep going past shoulder height until the weights are overhead, letting the traps help.
Lower slowly along the same path, arms straight throughout.
how.watch: Going too heavy, then bending the elbows or arching the back to finish overhead.
how.easier: Stop at shoulder height: a Lateral raise.
how.harder: Pause 2 seconds overhead on every rep.

video.title: Lu Raises - Progressive exercises for shoulder strengthening to reduce the risk of injury

how.gist: Hold a plate at shoulder height on straight arms and turn it left and right like a steering wheel.
steps: Stand tall and grip a plate at 3 and 9 o'clock, arms straight out at shoulder height.
Brace your trunk so you do not lean back.
Turn the plate one way as far as is comfortable, like a big steering wheel.
Turn it back through the middle and over to the other side; each turn is one rep.
how.watch: Letting the plate sink below shoulder height as the arms tire.
how.easier: Use a lighter plate, or hold it closer to your chest.
how.harder: Do a Front raise into each pair of turns.

video.title: Bus Driver Exercise | How to Do For Shoulders, Biceps, Traps, Upper Back | Correct Form & Technique

how.gist: Raise straight arms, thumbs up, in a V about 30° forward of your sides, up to shoulder height, then lower slowly.
steps: Stand tall with light weights at your sides, thumbs pointing forward.
Angle your arms about 30° forward of straight out to the sides, making a V.
Raise them along that line to shoulder height, arms long and shoulders down.
Lower slowly to your sides.
how.watch: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears as the arms rise.
how.easier: Do it one arm at a time, or with no weight.
how.harder: Keep going all the way overhead: a Lu raise.

video.title: How To Do a Dumbbell Scaption Raise

how.gist: Keep the arm straight and reach the weight a few inches further by moving only the shoulder blade, then let it back.
steps: Lie on your back holding a dumbbell straight up, or stand facing away from a band or cable.
Lock the elbow straight and keep it straight the whole time.
Reach the weight a few inches further away by sliding the shoulder blade around the ribs.
Let the shoulder blade glide back slowly without bending the arm.
how.watch: Bending and straightening the elbow, so it turns into a press.
how.easier: Use a light band standing, or no weight lying down.
how.harder: Do a Scapular push-up: the same reach under your bodyweight.

video.title: The Serratus Punch For Shoulder Rehab

how.gist: Stand holding a bar palms up and curl it to your shoulders by bending only at the elbows, then lower it under control.
steps: Stand tall holding the bar at shoulder width, palms facing forward, arms straight.
Pin your elbows to your sides and curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top without letting the elbows drift forward.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight again.
how.watch: Leaning back and swinging the hips to heave the bar up.
how.easier: Use an EZ bar, which puts the wrists at a more natural angle.
how.harder: Do Drag curl, or lower the bar for a slow count of three.

how.gist: Stand with a weight in each hand and curl them to your shoulders, turning your palms up, with your elbows at your sides.
steps: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight, palms facing your thighs.
Curl the weights up, turning your palms to face the ceiling as they rise.
Keep your elbows by your sides and squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly to straight arms. Work both arms together or alternate.
how.watch: Elbows swinging forward so the shoulders do part of the lift.
how.easier: Sit on a bench to take the body swing out of it.
how.harder: Do Incline curl for a longer stretch at the bottom.

how.gist: Curl dumbbells to your shoulders with your palms facing each other the whole way, as if lifting a hammer.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells (or a rope on a low cable) with your palms facing in.
Keep your thumbs pointing up and curl the weights toward your shoulders.
Keep your elbows at your sides and do not turn your wrists.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
how.watch: Swinging the weights up with the back instead of the arms.
how.harder: Curl across your body toward the opposite shoulder, one arm at a time.

how.gist: Lie back on an incline bench with your arms hanging behind your body and curl the dumbbells up without moving your upper arms.
steps: Set a bench to about 45–60° and sit back with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight down, palms forward, elbows slightly behind your body.
Curl the weights up while your upper arms stay still.
Lower all the way until your arms are straight to get the full stretch.
how.watch: Shoulders rolling forward and the elbows lifting out of the hang.
how.easier: Set the bench closer to upright.

how.gist: Rest the backs of your upper arms on a preacher pad and curl the weight up, lowering until your arms are nearly straight.
steps: Sit at the preacher bench with your armpits snug over the top of the pad.
Hold the bar or handle palms up, upper arms flat on the pad.
Curl the weight up until your forearms are close to vertical.
Lower slowly until the elbows are almost straight, without dropping into the bottom.
how.watch: Letting the weight drop fast into a locked-out bottom.
how.harder: Pause for a second at the bottom before each curl.

how.gist: Sit with your elbow braced against the inside of your thigh and curl a dumbbell toward your shoulder, one arm at a time.
steps: Sit on a bench with your feet wide and lean forward a little.
Brace the back of your upper arm against the inside of the same thigh, arm straight.
Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder, upper arm staying on the thigh.
Squeeze at the top, lower slowly to straight, then switch arms.
how.watch: Lifting the elbow off the thigh and using the shoulder to finish the curl.

how.gist: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with your arms hanging straight down and curl the weights up without swinging.
steps: Set a bench to about 45° and lie chest-down on it, chin over the top.
Let your arms hang straight down toward the floor, palms forward.
Curl the weights up, keeping your upper arms vertical and still.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to straight arms.
how.watch: Upper arms swinging forward so the shoulders help lift.
how.harder: Hold the squeeze at the top for two seconds on every rep.

video.title: Spider Curl

how.gist: Curl the bar up while dragging it along your body, letting your elbows travel back rather than forward.
steps: Stand holding the bar at shoulder width, palms forward, resting on your thighs.
Pull your elbows back as you curl, keeping the bar in contact with your body.
Drag it up your torso to about lower-chest height.
Reverse the path slowly, bar close, until your arms are straight.
how.watch: The bar drifting away from your body into an ordinary curl.

video.title: How To: Barbell Drag Curl (Increase Bicep Peaks!)

how.gist: Curl up with your palms facing up, turn them to face down at the top, and lower slowly with an overhand grip.
steps: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Curl both weights to your shoulders, palms up.
At the top, rotate your hands so the palms face down.
Lower slowly palms down, then turn them back up at the bottom.
how.watch: Rushing the palms-down lowering, which is the half that works the forearms.

video.title: Zottman Curl

how.gist: Curl the weight up with an overhand, palms-down grip, keeping your wrists straight and your elbows at your sides.
steps: Stand holding the bar at shoulder width with an overhand grip, palms facing back.
Keep your wrists straight, in line with your forearms.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders without moving your elbows forward.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
how.watch: Wrists bending back as the bar comes up.
how.easier: Use an EZ bar, which angles the wrists slightly.

how.gist: Face a low cable and curl the bar or handle to your shoulders, keeping your elbows pinned to your sides.
steps: Attach a bar or handle to a low pulley, or stand on a band, and hold it palms up.
Stand tall a step back, arms straight, elbows by your sides.
Curl up toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows still.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight, keeping tension on the cable.
how.watch: Leaning back to pull the weight up.
how.easier: Do one arm at a time with a single handle.

how.gist: Lean back from the straps on straight arms, palms up, and curl your hands toward your forehead to pull your body up.
steps: Hold the handles palms up, walk your feet forward and lean back, arms straight at shoulder height.
Keep your body straight from head to heels.
Bend only at the elbows to bring your hands toward your forehead, elbows staying high.
Straighten your arms slowly to lower back.
how.watch: Elbows dropping to your sides, turning it into a row.
how.easier: Stand more upright.
how.harder: Walk your feet further forward so you lean back more.

video.title: STOP Doing TRX Bicep Curls Like This (4 Mistakes Slowing Your Bicep Gains)

how.gist: Face away from a low cable and curl it from behind your body, so the biceps works from a stretched position.
steps: Set a cable low, take the handle in one hand and step forward until the arm is drawn behind you.
Stand in a split stance, chest up, elbow just behind your torso.
Curl the handle up and forward while the elbow stays back.
Lower slowly until the arm is straight and stretched behind you again.
how.watch: The elbow swinging forward as you curl, which takes the stretch out.
how.easier: Use a light band anchored low behind you.
how.harder: Pause one second at the bottom, in the stretch, on every rep.

video.title: Bayesian Curl Masterclass: Tips, Tricks, and Setup for Maximum Bicep Gains 💪

how.gist: Keep your upper arm still and straighten your elbow against the load, then bend it slowly back.
steps: Choose a position (lying, overhead or bent over) and fix your upper arms where they will stay.
Start with your elbows bent and the weight near your head or shoulder.
Straighten your elbows fully, moving only your forearms.
Bend them slowly back to the start.
how.watch: Upper arms moving so the shoulders help push the weight.

how.gist: Hold the weight overhead and lower it behind your head by bending your elbows, then straighten your arms back up.
steps: Sit or stand tall with one dumbbell in both hands overhead, or a rope facing away from a cable.
Keep your elbows pointing forward and close to your head.
Bend your elbows to lower the weight behind your head as far as is comfortable.
Straighten your arms back overhead without flaring the elbows.
how.watch: Elbows flaring out wide while the low back arches.
how.easier: Sit on a bench with a back support.

how.gist: Lie on a bench with the weight above your chest and bend only at the elbows to lower it toward your forehead, then press it back up.
steps: Lie on a bench holding the bar with a narrow overhand grip, arms straight above your chest.
Tilt your arms back slightly toward your head and keep them there.
Bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead or just behind your head.
Straighten your elbows to bring it back up without moving your upper arms.
how.watch: Elbows flaring wide and the upper arms rocking as the bar comes up.
how.easier: Use dumbbells with your palms facing each other.

video.title: Get Bigger Triceps with Skull Crushers | Form Check | Men’s Health

how.gist: Stand at a high cable with your elbows pinned to your sides and push the bar or rope down until your arms are straight.
steps: Attach a rope or bar to a high pulley and stand close, facing it.
Pin your elbows to your sides with your forearms about level with the floor.
Push down until your arms are straight; with a rope, pull the ends apart at the bottom.
Let your forearms come back up slowly while your elbows stay put.
how.watch: Elbows drifting forward and leaning over the bar to push with your body.

how.gist: Hinge forward with your upper arm held level with your back and straighten your elbow to press the weight back.
steps: Hinge forward with a flat back, free hand on a bench for support.
Raise your working upper arm until it is level with your torso and keep it there.
Straighten your elbow until your whole arm is in a line, weight behind you.
Bend the elbow slowly back to 90° without the upper arm dropping.
how.watch: Upper arm dropping toward the floor so the weight swings instead of lifting.

how.gist: Support yourself on bars, or on a bench behind you, and bend your elbows to lower with an upright torso, then press back up.
steps: Support yourself on parallel bars with straight arms, or with your hands on a bench behind you.
Keep your torso upright and your elbows pointing back, not out.
Bend your elbows until your upper arms are about level with the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.
how.watch: Shoulders rolling forward as you sink too deep at the bottom.
how.easier: Do bench dips with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
how.harder: On bars, add weight with a dip belt; on a bench, raise your feet on a second bench.

how.gist: A cross between a close-grip bench and a skull crusher: lower the bar toward your chin by folding your elbows, then press it back up.
steps: Lie on a bench and unrack the bar with a shoulder-width grip, arms straight over your upper chest.
Keep your elbows tucked and pointing toward your feet.
Lower the bar toward your chin, letting your forearms fold onto your upper arms.
Stop a few inches above your chin, then press back up to straight arms.
how.watch: Drifting into a plain bench press or skull crusher instead of the path between.
how.easier: Use a Smith machine to keep the bar path steady.

video.title: The Official JM Press Tutorial

how.gist: Lie on a bench with dumbbells pressed up and bend your elbows out to the sides to bring the bells down to your chest, then press back.
steps: Lie on a bench with dumbbells pressed up over your chest, palms facing your feet.
Point your elbows out to the sides and keep your upper arms still.
Bend your elbows to lower the inner ends of the dumbbells until they touch your chest.
Straighten your elbows back to the start.
how.watch: Upper arms moving so it turns into a press instead of an elbow bend.

video.title: How To: Tate Press | INCREASE YOUR BENCH & BUILD BIGGER TRICEPS!

how.gist: Do a push-up with your hands close together under your chest, thumbs and index fingers making a diamond.
steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands under your chest, fingertips touching in a diamond.
Brace so your body is a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows back along your sides to lower your chest to your hands.
Press back up to straight arms.
how.watch: Hips sagging toward the floor as the arms tire.
how.easier: Do it from your knees, as in Knee push-up.
how.harder: Raise your feet on a bench or wear a weight vest.

how.gist: Hold yourself up at the top of a dip on straight arms, shoulders pushed down away from your ears.
steps: Grip parallel bars or rings and jump up until your arms are straight.
Push down so your shoulders sit low, away from your ears.
Lock your elbows and keep your body still, legs together and slightly in front.
On rings, keep them close to your sides and turn your palms slightly forward.
Hold for the time, then step down.
how.watch: Shoulders shrugged up to the ears instead of pressed down.
how.harder: Move on to Chest dips.

video.title: How to RING SUPPORT HOLD (Beginner guide)

exercises.name: Bodyweight triceps extension
exercises.equipment: Bar at hip height, rings or straps

how.gist: Lean onto a bar in a plank and bend only your elbows to lower your head below the bar, then straighten your arms to come back.
steps: Hold a fixed bar, rings or straps at about hip height, hands shoulder-width, and walk your feet back into a plank.
Keep your body straight and your arms straight out in front.
Bend only at the elbows, letting your head go down and under the bar.
Press into the bar to straighten your elbows and return.
how.watch: Shoulders moving or hips bending, so it turns into a push-up.
how.easier: Use a higher bar, or stand more upright.
how.harder: Use a lower bar, or walk your feet further back.

video.title: How to Bodyweight Tricep Extension | Calisthenics Triceps

how.gist: Rest your forearms palms up on a bench or your thighs and curl the weight up by bending only at the wrists.
steps: Sit and rest your forearms on your thighs or a bench, palms up, wrists just past the edge.
Let the weight roll down toward your fingertips.
Curl it back into your palm, then bend your wrists up as far as they go.
Lower slowly back down.
how.watch: Forearms lifting off the support so the elbows help.

how.gist: Rest your forearms palms down with your wrists over the edge and lift the backs of your hands up, then lower slowly.
steps: Sit and rest your forearms on your thighs or a bench, palms down, wrists just past the edge.
Hold a light weight and let your hands drop down.
Lift the backs of your hands toward the ceiling, moving only at the wrist.
Lower slowly to the bottom.
how.watch: Going so heavy that the elbows and shoulders heave the weight up.

how.gist: Hold a wrist roller out in front and turn it hand over hand to wind a hanging weight up, then unwind it slowly.
steps: Hold the roller with an overhand grip, arms straight out in front at shoulder height.
Roll it toward you one hand at a time to wind up the cord and lift the weight.
When the weight reaches the roller, reverse to lower it slowly to the floor.
On the next rep, roll the other way to work the opposite side of the forearm.
how.watch: Arms sinking toward your waist, which takes the work off the forearms.
how.easier: Keep your elbows bent and close to your body.

video.title: How to use The Wrist Roller for Stronger Wrists and Forearms

how.gist: With your forearm supported, hold a weight off-centre and rotate your palm from facing up toward facing down against the load.
steps: Sit with your forearm on your thigh or a bench, elbow bent 90°, hand past the edge.
Grip a hammer, or a dumbbell handle loaded at one end, with the weight on your thumb side.
Start palm up, then rotate your forearm until your thumb points at the ceiling.
Lower slowly back to palm up.
how.watch: Elbow lifting or the upper arm turning so the shoulder does the rotation.
how.harder: Hold the handle further from the weight.

video.title: Resisted Forearm Pronation and Supination - Dumbbell

how.gist: With your forearm supported, hold a weight off-centre and rotate your palm from facing down toward facing up against the load.
steps: Sit with your forearm on your thigh or a bench, elbow bent 90°, hand past the edge.
Grip a hammer, or a dumbbell handle loaded at one end, with the weight on your thumb side.
Start palm down, then rotate your forearm until your thumb points at the ceiling.
Lower slowly back to palm down.
how.watch: Elbow lifting or the upper arm turning so the shoulder does the rotation.
how.harder: Hold the handle further from the weight.

video.title: Dumbbell Wrist Supination & Pronation - Forearm Strength & Rehab @Ott_Physical_Therapy

how.gist: With your arm at your side, hold a hammer with the head in front and tilt your wrist up toward the thumb to raise it, then lower.
steps: Stand with your arm straight at your side, thumb pointing forward.
Hold the handle of a hammer or end-loaded dumbbell with the weight in front of your thumb.
Tilt your wrist up toward the thumb side to lift the weight, elbow staying straight.
Lower slowly as far as your wrist allows.
how.watch: Bending the elbow or swinging the arm to lift the weight.
how.harder: Hold the handle further from the weight.

video.title: HOW TO: Dumbbell Radial Deviation | Made to Move

how.gist: With your arm at your side, hold a hammer with the head behind you and tilt your wrist back toward the little finger to raise it.
steps: Stand with your arm straight at your side, thumb pointing forward.
Hold the handle of a hammer or end-loaded dumbbell with the weight behind your little finger.
Tilt your wrist back toward the little-finger side to lift the weight, arm staying still.
Lower slowly as far as your wrist allows.
how.watch: Swinging the arm back instead of moving at the wrist.
how.harder: Hold the handle further from the weight.

video.title: Dumbbell Ulnar Deviation

how.gist: Loop a band around your fingertips and thumb and spread your fingers open against it, then let them close slowly.
steps: Loop a rubber band around the tips of your four fingers and thumb, held together.
Spread your fingers and thumb open as wide as you can.
Hold for a moment, then let them close slowly against the band.
how.watch: Bending the wrist back to help open the hand.
how.harder: Double the band over or use a thicker one.

video.title: Finger Extension Strengthening for Rock Climbers

how.gist: Squeeze a spring gripper until the handles touch, then let it open slowly.
steps: Set the gripper deep in your hand, one handle across your palm, fingers wrapped round the other.
Squeeze until the handles touch, keeping your wrist straight.
Hold the close for a second, then let it open slowly.
Do all the reps on one hand, then switch.
how.watch: Letting the gripper spring open instead of controlling it.
how.harder: Move to a stiffer gripper, or hold each close for 5–10 seconds.

video.title: How to Use the Captains of Crush Hand Gripper

how.gist: Pinch two plates together between your fingers and thumb, smooth sides out, and hold them at your side for time.
steps: Stand two plates of the same size together, smooth sides facing out.
Pinch them with your thumb on one side and flat fingers on the other.
Stand tall and hold them at your side, arm straight.
Hold for the set time, set them down under control, then switch hands.
how.watch: Resting the plates against your leg to take some of the weight.
how.harder: Pinch three plates to widen the grip, or use bigger plates.
