how.gist: Hang from a bar with straight arms and a full grip for time.
steps: Grip the bar overhand about shoulder width, using a box to reach it if needed.
Lift your feet and hang with straight arms and relaxed legs.
Breathe steadily and hold until the time is up.
Step down on to the box rather than dropping.
how.watch: Letting go suddenly at failure instead of stepping down.
how.easier: Keep your toes on a box to take some of your weight.
how.harder: Hang from a thicker bar or towels, or hold with one arm.

how.gist: Pick up a heavy weight in each hand and stand tall holding them at your sides for time.
steps: Stand between the weights and deadlift them up with a flat back.
Stand tall, shoulders down and back, arms straight at your sides.
Squeeze the handles hard and breathe steadily for the set time.
Set the weights down by bending at the hips and knees, not by dropping them.
how.watch: Shoulders rounding forward and creeping up as the grip tires.
how.harder: Walk with them: do Farmer's carry instead.

how.gist: Push your hand deep into a bucket of rice and open, close, twist and bend it against the grains.
steps: Fill a deep bucket with rice and push one hand in up to the wrist or deeper.
Open your fingers as wide as you can, then make a tight fist; repeat.
Turn your hand palm up and palm down, then bend the wrist up and down.
Work each movement for 20–30 seconds, then switch hands.
how.watch: Staying near the surface, where the rice gives little resistance.

video.title: Hand & Wrist Strength & Durability - Rice or Sand Bucket

how.gist: Hang towels over a pull-up bar, grip the towels instead of the bar, and do pull-ups.
steps: Drape two towels over the bar about shoulder-width apart.
Grab each towel in a tight fist and hang with straight arms.
Pull until your hands reach your chin, squeezing the towels the whole way.
Lower under control to straight arms.
how.watch: Hands slowly sliding down the towels as the grip loosens on the way down.
how.easier: Use one towel and keep the other hand on the bar.
how.harder: Hang one towel and hold it with both hands.

video.title: The Towel Pull-Up

how.gist: Let the bar roll down to your fingertips, then curl your fingers closed to roll it back into your palm.
steps: Sit with forearms on your thighs or a bench, palms up, wrists just past the edge, holding a bar.
Open your fingers slowly and let the bar roll down to your fingertips.
Curl the fingers closed to roll the bar back into your palm.
Squeeze at the top, then roll it down again.
how.watch: Using a load so heavy the bar slips off the fingertips at the bottom.
how.easier: Use light dumbbells, one hand at a time.
how.harder: Finish each rep with a full Wrist curl.

video.title: How To Perform Finger Curls Tutorial

how.gist: With a bar across your upper back, sit down between your knees until your thighs are at least level, then stand back up.
steps: Set the bar in a rack at mid-chest height and step under so it sits across your upper back.
Unrack, take two steps back and stand with feet about shoulder width, toes slightly out.
Brace your trunk, then bend hips and knees together, knees tracking over your toes.
Go down until your hip crease is at least level with your knees, then drive back up.
how.watch: Knees caving inward as you stand up.
how.easier: Learn the depth with Goblet squat or Box squat.
how.harder: Pause for two seconds at the bottom of each rep.

how.gist: Hold the bar across the front of your shoulders with your elbows high and squat down with an upright chest, then stand.
steps: Set the bar on the front of your shoulders against your neck, fingertips under it.
Lift your elbows high so your upper arms point forward.
Brace, then sit straight down between your heels with your chest upright.
Go as deep as you can keep the elbows up, then drive up through the whole foot.
how.watch: Elbows dropping, so the chest tips forward and the bar rolls off.
how.easier: Cross your arms over the bar, or do Goblet squat.

video.title: How To Front Squat (WAYS TO KEEP YOUR CHEST UP!)

how.gist: Squat back onto a box, sit on it briefly while staying braced, then drive back up.
steps: Set a box behind you so your thighs are about level with the floor when seated.
Stand a short step in front of it with a slightly wider stance than usual.
Push your hips back and sit down onto the box under control.
Pause with your trunk braced, then drive up off the box.
how.watch: Crashing down onto the box and letting your trunk go soft.
how.easier: Use a higher box.
how.harder: Use a lower box.

video.title: How to Box Squat Correctly | Westside Barbell com

how.gist: Hold a weight against your chest and squat down between your knees, then stand back up.
steps: Hold a kettlebell by the horns, or a dumbbell by one end, tight against your chest.
Stand with feet a little wider than hips, toes slightly out.
Sit straight down with your elbows inside your knees and your chest up.
Go as low as you can with a flat back, then stand up through your whole foot.
how.watch: Heels lifting off the floor at the bottom.
how.easier: Squat down to a bench, as in Box squat.
how.harder: Do Front squat with a barbell.

how.gist: With your back on the machine pad and shoulders under the yokes, squat the sled down and press it back up.
steps: Stand on the platform with your back on the pad, shoulders under the pads, feet shoulder width.
Release the safety handles to unlock the sled.
Bend your knees to lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the platform.
Push back up through your whole foot without snapping your knees straight.
Lock the safety handles again at the end of the set.
how.watch: Hips lifting off the pad at the bottom.

how.gist: Hold the bar in the crooks of your elbows against your body and squat down with an upright chest, then stand up.
steps: Set the bar in a rack at about waist height; wrap it in a pad or towel if it digs in.
Dip under it and cradle it in the crooks of your elbows, hands clasped.
Stand up and step back, keeping the bar tight to your body.
Squat down between your knees with your chest up, then drive back up.
how.watch: Upper back rounding as the bar pulls you forward.

video.title: How to Perform Zercher Squats - Leg Squat Exercise

exercises.equipment: Belt squat machine or dip belt

how.gist: Wear a belt that hangs the load from your hips and squat down and up with your torso upright.
steps: Fasten the belt around your hips and hook it to the machine, or hang plates from a dip belt.
Stand on the platform, or on two boxes, feet shoulder width, holding the handles for balance.
Squat down between your knees, chest up, as deep as you can control.
Stand back up by driving through your whole foot.
how.watch: Pulling on the handles to help yourself up.

video.title: Exercise Tutorial - How to use a belt squat

how.gist: Sit in the machine with your feet on the platform and lower it toward your chest, then press it back out.
steps: Sit with your back flat on the pad and your feet shoulder width on the platform.
Press to release the safeties, then bend your knees to lower the platform.
Go as deep as you can before your low back starts to lift off the pad.
Press back out to nearly straight legs without locking your knees.
how.watch: Hips and low back curling off the seat at the bottom.

how.gist: Sit in the machine with the pad on your lower shins and straighten your knees to lift it, then lower slowly.
steps: Adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine’s pivot.
Set the pad on the front of your lower shins, just above the ankles.
Hold the handles and straighten your legs fully.
Lower slowly until your knees are bent about 90° or more.
how.watch: Kicking the weight up fast and letting it drop.

how.gist: Stand in a long split stance and lower your back knee toward the floor, then push back up, feet staying put.
steps: Take a long step forward into a split stance, back heel raised, feet hip-width apart.
Keep your torso upright and your weight on the front foot.
Lower straight down until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push up through the front foot. Finish the set, then switch legs.
how.watch: Feet in one line, as if on a tightrope, so you lose balance.
how.harder: Raise the back foot on a bench: Bulgarian split squat.

how.gist: With your back foot on a bench behind you, lower your back knee toward the floor and push up through the front foot.
steps: Stand about a stride in front of a bench and rest the top of your back foot on it.
Keep most of your weight on the front foot.
Lower until your back knee is close to the floor, front shin slightly forward.
Push up through the front foot. Finish the set, then switch legs.
how.watch: Front foot too close to the bench, so the front heel lifts.
how.easier: Keep both feet on the floor: Split squat.

video.title: The PERFECT Bulgarian Split Squat (Avoid These Errors!)

how.gist: Step forward into a long stride, lower your back knee toward the floor, then push back to standing.
steps: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart.
Take a long step forward and land heel first.
Lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor, torso upright.
Push off the front foot to step back to the start. Alternate legs or finish one side.
how.watch: Front knee collapsing inward as you push back.
how.easier: Do Split squat, with your feet staying put.
how.harder: Hold dumbbells, or do Walking lunge.

how.gist: Lunge forward, then bring the back leg through into the next lunge, travelling forward with each step.
steps: Stand tall with feet together and step forward into a long lunge.
Lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through the front foot and bring the back leg forward into the next lunge.
Keep going for the set number of steps.
how.watch: Short, choppy steps that let the front heel lift.
how.easier: Pause standing upright between steps.
how.harder: Hold dumbbells at your sides.

how.gist: Step back into a lunge, lower your back knee toward the floor, then push through the front foot to stand.
steps: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart.
Take a long step backward, landing on the ball of your foot.
Lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor, weight on the front foot.
Drive through the front foot to bring the back leg forward to standing.
how.watch: Pushing off the back foot instead of standing up with the front leg.
how.harder: Stand on a low step to lower further, or hold dumbbells.

how.gist: Step wide to the side and sit back into that hip with the other leg straight, then push back to standing.
steps: Stand tall, feet together.
Take a wide step out to the side, toes pointing forward.
Sit your hips back over the stepping leg, other leg straight and its foot flat.
Push off the bent leg to return to the start. Alternate sides or finish one.
how.watch: Heel of the bent leg lifting and the knee shooting forward.
how.harder: Hold a kettlebell at your chest, or do Cossack squat.

how.gist: Put one foot on a box and stand up on it using that leg, then step back down under control.
steps: Face a box or bench about knee height and plant one whole foot on it.
Lean forward slightly and drive through that foot to stand up on the box.
Stand tall at the top, bringing the other foot up beside it.
Step down slowly with the trailing leg and repeat.
how.watch: Pushing off the floor with the back foot to bounce up.
how.easier: Use a lower box.
how.harder: Use a higher box or hold dumbbells.

exercises.equipment: Something to hold, or a sissy bench

how.gist: Rise onto your toes and lean back, pushing your knees forward and down while your hips stay straight, then come back up.
steps: Stand holding a post or rack with one hand, feet hip-width apart.
Rise onto the balls of your feet.
Push your knees forward and down as you lean back, a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Lower as far as you can control, then come back up using your quads.
how.watch: Hips bending so it turns into an ordinary squat.
how.easier: Use a sissy squat bench, or go only part way down.
how.harder: Hold a plate against your chest.

video.title: Sissy Squat Correct Form | Gareth Sapstead

how.gist: On one leg, with the other held straight out in front, squat all the way down and stand back up.
steps: Stand on one leg with the other leg lifted straight out in front of you.
Reach your arms forward for balance.
Sit down on the standing leg until your hamstring rests on your calf, heel flat.
Stand back up without letting the lifted foot touch the floor.
how.watch: Heel of the standing foot lifting as you reach the bottom.
how.easier: Do Box pistol squat, sitting down to a box.
how.harder: Hold a kettlebell or dumbbell out in front.

video.title: How to Get Your First PISTOL SQUAT (Step-by-Step Progression)

how.gist: Lean your back against a wall and slide down until your thighs are level with the floor, then hold.
steps: Stand with your back flat against a wall, feet about two feet out in front.
Slide down until your knees are bent about 90°, thighs level with the floor.
Keep your knees over your ankles and your back on the wall.
Hold for the set time, then slide back up.
how.watch: Pushing on your thighs with your hands to take some of the load.
how.easier: Hold higher, with your knees bent less than 90°.
how.harder: Rest a plate on your thighs, or hold on one leg.

how.gist: Squat down, then jump straight up as high as you can and land softly into the next squat.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width, arms by your sides.
Dip into a quarter to half squat, swinging your arms back.
Jump straight up, swinging your arms up.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and bend your knees to absorb it.
how.watch: Landing stiff-legged with the knees caving inward.
how.harder: Hold light dumbbells, or pause at the bottom before each jump.

how.gist: Stand with feet about shoulder-width and sit your hips down between your heels as low as you can control, then stand up.
steps: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width, toes turned out a little.
Reach your arms forward and sit your hips back and down.
Let your knees travel over your toes, heels flat and chest up.
Go as low as you can stay balanced, then push the floor away to stand.
how.watch: Knees caving inward as you stand up.
how.harder: Do Jump squats, or work toward the Box pistol squat.

how.gist: On one leg, hold your other foot behind you and lower until that back knee touches the floor, then stand back up.
steps: Stand on one leg, bend the other knee and hold that foot behind you with the same-side hand.
Reach your free arm forward for balance.
Bend the standing leg until the back knee touches the floor or a pad, torso leaning forward.
Push through the whole standing foot to stand back up.
how.watch: Dropping hard onto the back knee instead of touching it down.
how.easier: Do Skater squats, which leave the back foot free.
how.harder: Hold the back foot with both hands, or hold a dumbbell.

video.title: Shrimp Squat Tutorial

how.gist: On one leg with the other knee bent behind you, lower until the back knee touches a pad, leaning forward, then stand up.
steps: Stand on one leg with the other knee bent so that foot is behind you, off the floor.
Reach your arms forward as a counterweight.
Lean forward slightly and bend the standing knee until the back knee lightly touches a pad.
Drive through the standing foot to return to tall.
how.watch: Standing knee caving in toward the other leg.
how.easier: Lower to a taller stack of pads, or do Step-downs.
how.harder: Do Shrimp squats, holding the back foot.

video.title: Skater Squats

how.gist: On one leg with the other held straight out in front, sit down to a box with control and stand back up on the one leg.
steps: Stand on one leg with your back to a box or bench, the other leg held straight out in front.
Reach your arms forward and sit back and down slowly.
Touch the box lightly without dropping onto it or resting.
Drive through the whole foot to stand up without rocking.
how.watch: Falling the last few inches onto the box, or rocking back to get up.
how.easier: Use a taller box, or do Bodyweight squats.
how.harder: Use a lower box, then do the full Pistol squat.

video.title: Single-Leg Squat To Box | Exercise Guide

how.gist: From a wide stance, squat deep onto one leg while the other stays straight with toes up, then shift across to the other side.
steps: Stand with your feet about twice shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
Shift your weight to one side and squat down on that leg, heel flat.
Keep the other leg straight and let its toes point up as you sink.
Push back up to the middle and go to the other side.
how.watch: The heel of the bending leg lifting as you go low.
how.easier: Go only as deep as your heel stays down, or do Lateral lunges.
how.harder: Hold a kettlebell or dumbbell at your chest.

video.title: How to Cossack Squat Mobility Exercise: Tutorial & Progressions

how.gist: From a lunge, jump up and swap legs in the air, landing softly in a lunge on the other side.
steps: Start in a lunge, front knee over the ankle, back knee just off the floor.
Jump straight up, driving through both feet.
Switch legs in the air.
Land softly, front foot flat, and sink straight into the next lunge.
how.watch: Landing stiff, with the front knee caving in.
how.easier: Do Reverse lunges at a quick pace.
how.harder: Pause in the bottom of each lunge before jumping.

video.title: Exercises with an Athletic Trainer: Alternating Jump Lunges

how.gist: Step one leg back and across behind the other, as in a curtsy, lower until the back knee nears the floor, then return.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width.
Step your right foot back and across behind your left, landing on the ball of the foot.
Bend both knees to lower until the back knee is just off the floor, hips facing forward.
Push through the front foot to stand and bring your feet together; then do the other side.
how.watch: Hips twisting toward the back leg instead of staying square to the front.
how.easier: Hold onto a support, or do Reverse lunges.
how.harder: Hold dumbbells, or a kettlebell at your chest.

video.title: Curtsy Lunge Beginner Exercise Demonstrated by Physical Therapist

how.gist: Kneel upright and lean back from the knees in one straight line from knees to head, then pull yourself back up with your thighs.
steps: Kneel on a pad, knees hip-width, body upright.
Squeeze your glutes so your hips stay straight.
Lean back slowly from the knees, keeping one line from knee to head.
Go only as far as you can control, then use your thighs to come back upright.
how.watch: Hips bending so the body folds, which takes the load off the quads.
how.easier: Lean back less, or hold a band anchored in front of you.
how.harder: Lean back further, toward your heels.

video.title: How to Safely Set Up, Perform, & Program Reverse Nordics (Progressions | Regressions | Alternatives)

how.gist: Standing on one leg on a step, slowly lower the other heel to tap the floor beside or in front, then stand back up.
steps: Stand on a step on one leg, the other foot hanging off the side or front.
Push your hips back slightly and slowly bend the standing knee.
Lower until the free heel lightly taps the floor, without putting weight on it.
Straighten the standing leg to return to the top.
how.watch: Standing knee caving inward as you lower.
how.easier: Use a lower step.
how.harder: Use a higher step, or do Skater squats.

video.title: How To Do Lateral Step Downs - Strength & Balance - Wellen

exercises.name: Spanish squat
exercises.equipment: Heavy band and a fixed post

how.gist: With a heavy band behind your knees anchored to a post in front, sit back into a squat with upright shins, then stand.
steps: Loop a heavy band (or one per leg) around a fixed post at knee height and set it behind your knees.
Walk back until the band is tight, feet hip-width.
Sit back into the band, keeping your shins vertical and your torso upright.
Go to about 90° at the knee or where it is comfortable, hold if you like, then stand.
how.watch: Shins tipping forward instead of staying vertical against the band.
how.easier: Squat less deep, or hold the bottom instead of doing reps.
how.harder: Hold the bottom longer each rep.

video.title: How to Set Up and Perform Spanish Squats Correctly (Don't Make This Mistake!)

exercises.name: Heel-elevated squat
exercises.equipment: Wedge or small plates under the heels

how.gist: Squat with your heels raised on a wedge or plates, so your knees travel well forward and your torso stays upright.
steps: Put your heels on a slant board or small plates 1–2 in high, feet about hip width.
Hold a dumbbell at your chest, or a bar on your back, and brace.
Sit straight down, knees travelling well forward over your toes, chest tall.
Go as deep as you control, then stand by pushing through the whole foot.
how.watch: Weight tipping onto the toes so the heels come off the wedge.
how.easier: Use bodyweight only, arms out in front.
how.harder: Hold heavier weight, or pause 2 seconds at the bottom.

video.title: Heel Elevated Goblet Squat + (Tutorial)[Quads][Glutes]

how.gist: Stand side-on to a box, step up sideways with the near leg and stand tall on it, then lower slowly.
steps: Stand side-on to a low box or step and put the near foot flat on top.
Lean slightly forward and push through the whole foot on the box.
Stand up tall on that leg, letting the other foot come up beside it.
Lower the outside foot slowly to the floor, knee in line with the toes.
how.watch: Pushing off the floor foot instead of standing up with the leg on the box.
how.easier: Use a lower step, or hold a rail.
how.harder: Hold dumbbells or use a higher box; or try a Step-down.

video.channel: Momentum Physical Therapy and Performance Training
video.title: Lateral Step Up

how.gist: Hold the end of a landmine bar at your chest and squat down and up, leaning slightly into the bar.
steps: Hold the end of the bar at your chest with both hands, elbows tucked, feet shoulder width.
Step your feet a little forward so you lean slightly into the bar.
Squat down between your knees, chest up, as deep as you control.
Drive up through the whole foot back to standing.
how.watch: Letting the bar drift away from the chest, so the back rounds.
how.easier: Squat to a box or bench to set the depth.
how.harder: Add plates, or pause 2 seconds at the bottom.

video.title: Landmine Squat Tutorial

how.gist: Stand wide with toes turned out, hold a weight between your legs and squat straight down, knees following your toes.
steps: Stand with feet well wider than shoulders, toes turned out about 30–45°.
Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at arm's length between your legs, chest up.
Squat straight down, pushing your knees out over your toes.
Stand up by squeezing your glutes, without letting the knees cave in.
how.watch: Knees collapsing inward instead of tracking over the toes.
how.easier: Use bodyweight only, or squat to a box.
how.harder: Stand on two boxes so the weight can go lower, or hold more.

video.title: How To Do A Sumo Squat | The Right Way | Well+Good

how.gist: With a band behind your knee, straighten the knee from slightly bent to fully locked against the band, then ease back.
steps: Anchor a band at knee height, face the anchor and loop the band behind one knee.
Step back until the band pulls, with the knee slightly bent and the heel down.
Straighten the knee fully against the band, tightening the front of the thigh.
Hold a second, then let the knee bend slightly again under control.
how.watch: Swinging the hips back and forth instead of the knee doing the work.
how.easier: Use a lighter band, or stand closer to the anchor.
how.harder: Use a heavier band, or lift the other foot and stand on one leg.

video.title: Terminal Knee Extension (TKEs) to Work on Getting Your Knee Straight

how.gist: From standing, push your hips back with soft knees to lower the weight down your legs, then drive your hips forward to stand.
steps: Stand holding the bar at your thighs, feet hip width, knees slightly bent.
Push your hips back, sliding the bar down your thighs with a flat back.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, usually just below the knees.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, keeping the bar close.
how.watch: Rounding the back to reach lower instead of pushing the hips back.
how.easier: Learn the movement with Dowel hip hinge first.
how.harder: Do Single-leg deadlift.

video.title: HOW TO DO ROMANIAN DEADLIFTS (RDLs): Build Beefy Hamstrings With Perfect Technique

how.gist: With your knees almost straight, hinge forward to lower the bar as far as your back stays flat, then stand back up.
steps: Stand holding the bar at your thighs, feet hip width, knees only slightly bent.
Keep that knee bend fixed and push your hips back to lower the bar along your legs.
Go as low as your back stays flat, touching the floor if you can.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
how.watch: Bending the knees more on the way down, which turns it into an RDL.
how.easier: Do Romanian deadlift, with more knee bend.

video.title: How to STIFF LEG DEADLIFT (and Why You Probably Should)

how.gist: Balance on one leg and hinge forward, reaching the weight toward the floor as the other leg goes back, then stand up.
steps: Stand on one leg with a soft knee, weight in the opposite hand.
Hinge at the hip, reaching the weight down as your free leg extends straight behind you.
Keep your hips square to the floor until your torso is nearly level.
Drive the standing hip forward to come back up.
how.watch: The hip of the lifted leg rotating up and out.
how.easier: Do B-stance Romanian deadlift, toes of the back foot on the floor.

video.title: How To Do A Single Leg Deadlift | The Right Way | Well+Good

how.gist: Lying or seated in the machine with the pad behind your ankles, curl your heels toward your glutes, then lower slowly.
steps: Adjust the machine so your knees line up with its pivot.
Set the pad behind your lower legs, just above the heels.
Curl your heels toward your glutes as far as you can.
Lower slowly until your legs are nearly straight.
how.watch: Hips lifting off the bench or seat to finish the curl.
how.harder: Do Nordic hamstring curl.

exercises.equipment: Ankle anchor and a knee pad

how.gist: Kneel with your ankles held down and lower your body toward the floor as slowly as you can, then push back up.
steps: Kneel on a pad with your ankles held down by a partner, bench or strap.
Keep a straight line from knees to shoulders, hips pushed forward.
Lean forward slowly, fighting the fall with your hamstrings.
Catch yourself with your hands, then push off lightly and pull back up.
how.watch: Bending at the hips to shorten the lever instead of staying straight.
how.easier: Lower only part way, or use a band from above to take some weight.
how.harder: Hold a plate at your chest.

video.title: Nordic Hamstring Curls for Beginners (In 1 Minute!)

how.gist: On a GHD with your feet locked in, curl your body up from horizontal to upright with your hamstrings, then lower it.
steps: Set the footplate so your knees sit just behind the pad and lock your feet in.
Start with your body horizontal, straight from knees to head.
Push your toes into the plate and curl your body up until it is upright.
Lower slowly back to horizontal, keeping your hips straight.
how.watch: Bending at the hips so the low back does the work instead.
how.easier: Use a band anchored in front of you for help.
how.harder: Hold a plate at your chest.

video.title: Best Hamstring Exercise? How To Perform Glute Ham Raises

how.gist: With your upper back on a bench and a bar across your hips, drive your hips up until your body is level, then lower.
steps: Sit with your upper back against a bench edge and roll a padded bar over your hips.
Plant your feet flat, hip width, so your shins are vertical at the top.
Tuck your chin slightly and drive through your heels to lift your hips.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, body level from shoulders to knees, then lower.
how.watch: Arching the low back at the top instead of finishing with the glutes.
how.easier: Do Glute bridge from the floor.
how.harder: Do Single-leg hip thrust.

video.channel: Girls Gone Strong | Women's Health & Fitness
video.title: How To Do a Barbell Hip Thrust

how.gist: Lie on your back with your knees bent and push through your heels to lift your hips, then lower.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart.
Press your low back gently toward the floor and brace.
Drive through your heels until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower slowly.
how.watch: Pushing up into an arched low back instead of squeezing the glutes.
how.harder: Do Single-leg glute bridge, or Hip thrust with a bar.

how.gist: Lie on your back with one foot planted and the other leg lifted, and bridge your hips up on the planted leg.
steps: Lie on your back, one knee bent with the foot flat, the other leg straight up or knee pulled in.
Press through the planted heel to lift your hips.
Keep both hips level at the top and squeeze.
Lower slowly, finish the set, then switch legs.
how.watch: The hip on the lifted side dropping as you rise.
how.easier: Do Glute bridge on both feet.
how.harder: Do Single-leg hip thrust with your back on a bench.

exercises.equipment: Low cable with rope, or band

how.gist: Facing away from a low cable with the rope between your legs, hinge forward, then drive your hips through to stand tall.
steps: Attach a rope to a low pulley and stand facing away, rope between your legs.
Walk out a couple of steps and set your feet a bit wider than your hips.
Push your hips back with soft knees, letting the rope travel back between your legs.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall and squeeze your glutes; arms stay long.
how.watch: Squatting down or pulling with the arms instead of hinging at the hips.

video.title: How to Do Cable Pull Throughs

how.gist: Hike the kettlebell back between your legs, then snap your hips forward so it floats up to chest height.
steps: Stand with the bell a foot in front, feet just wider than hips; hinge and grip it.
Hike it back high between your legs, like passing a ball.
Snap your hips forward to stand tall; the bell floats up to about chest height.
Let it fall, hinge as your forearms meet your thighs, and go straight into the next rep.
how.watch: Squatting the bell and lifting it with the arms instead of the hips.
how.harder: Swing with one hand, or use a heavier bell.

video.title: Kettlebell Swing

how.gist: Push your knees apart, or one leg out to the side, against resistance, then let it come back slowly.
steps: Machine: sit with the pads outside your knees. Cable or band: attach it to the ankle away from the anchor.
Sit or stand tall and brace so your trunk stays still.
Push your knees apart, or lift the leg out to the side, as far as you can control.
Return slowly, keeping tension on the load.
how.watch: Leaning or rocking the body to swing the leg out.
how.easier: Do Clamshell or Side-lying leg raise on the floor.

how.gist: Squeeze your knees together, or one leg in across your body, against resistance, then let it go back out slowly.
steps: Machine: sit with the pads inside your knees. Cable or band: attach it to the ankle nearer the anchor.
Sit or stand tall and brace so your trunk stays still.
Squeeze your knees together, or sweep the leg in across your body.
Let your legs, or leg, go back out slowly.
how.watch: Letting the weight snap the legs back open.
how.harder: Do Copenhagen plank.

how.gist: Lie on your side with knees bent and feet together, and open your top knee like a clamshell without rolling back.
steps: Lie on your side, hips and knees bent about 45°, feet together.
Stack your hips and rest your head on your arm.
Keep your feet together and lift the top knee as high as you can without your pelvis rolling back.
Lower slowly, finish the set, then switch sides.
how.watch: Top hip rolling backward to get the knee higher.
how.harder: Loop a mini band just above your knees.

how.gist: With a band around your legs and knees slightly bent, walk forward and back in wide diagonal steps, keeping the band tight.
steps: Loop a mini band above your knees or around your ankles.
Stand with feet hip width or wider, knees and hips slightly bent.
Step forward and out on a diagonal, then bring the other foot forward and out.
Keep the band tight the whole time; walk forward, then backward.
how.watch: Feet drifting together so the band goes slack.
how.harder: Move the band down to your ankles or feet, or use a stronger band.

video.title: Monster Walks - Strengthening the gluteus medius

how.gist: Hold a side plank with your top leg resting on a bench and the bottom leg hanging free, hips lifted.
steps: Lie on your side next to a bench, propped on your forearm, elbow under your shoulder.
Rest the inside of your top leg on the bench: knee for a short lever, ankle for a long one.
Lift your hips until your body is straight; the bottom leg hangs or lifts to the bench.
Hold for the set time, then switch sides.
how.watch: Hips sagging toward the floor.
how.easier: Rest your knee on the bench instead of your ankle.
how.harder: Rest your ankle on the bench and lift the bottom leg up to meet it.

video.title: How to Set Up, Perform, & Program Copenhagen Planks (Progressions | Regressions | Alternatives)

how.gist: Lie face down with your hips at the edge of the machine or a bench and lift your straight legs up behind you, then lower.
steps: Lie face down with your hips at the end of the pad and your legs hanging down.
Grip the handles or the bench to keep your upper body still.
Squeeze your glutes to lift your legs until they are level with your body.
Lower under control, letting your hips bend as the legs swing down.
how.watch: Swinging the legs past level into a big low-back arch.

video.title: Reverse Hypers

how.gist: With your upper back on a bench and one foot planted, drive your hips up until your body is straight from knee to shoulders.
steps: Sit with your upper back on the edge of a bench, one foot flat so the shin is vertical at the top.
Lift the other foot off the floor, knee bent or leg straight.
Tuck your chin and ribs, then push through the planted heel to raise your hips level.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
how.watch: Arching the low back at the top instead of finishing with the hips.
how.easier: Do the Single-leg glute bridge on the floor.
how.harder: Rest a dumbbell or plate on the working hip.

video.title: Perfect Your Single Leg Hip Thrust: Boost Glute Strength & Stability

how.gist: Lying on your back with heels on sliders, lift your hips and curl your heels toward you, then slide them out with hips still up.
steps: Lie on your back with your heels on sliders, a towel on a smooth floor, or a stability ball.
Push your heels down and lift your hips off the floor.
Keeping your hips up, pull your heels toward your glutes.
Slide your heels slowly back out to nearly straight legs, hips still up.
how.watch: Hips sagging to the floor as the legs straighten.
how.easier: Only slide out slowly, then lower your hips and reset.
how.harder: Go one leg at a time, then move on to Nordic hamstring curls.

video.title: How To: Slider Leg Curl

how.gist: Lie on your back with the soles of your feet together and knees out, heels near your hips, and pump your hips up and down.
steps: Lie on your back, put the soles of your feet together and let your knees fall out.
Pull your heels in toward your hips and tuck your chin.
Push through the outside edges of your feet to lift your hips, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Lower and repeat at a steady pace.
how.watch: Arching the low back to get higher instead of squeezing the glutes.
how.easier: Do Glute bridges with your feet flat.
how.harder: Hold a dumbbell or plate on your hips.

video.title: Frog Pump

how.gist: On hands and knees, lift one bent leg so the sole of the foot pushes toward the ceiling, without arching your back.
steps: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Keep one knee bent at 90° and flex that foot.
Push the sole of the foot up toward the ceiling until your thigh is level with your body.
Lower the knee back toward the floor without touching; finish the reps, then switch sides.
how.watch: Low back arching as the leg goes higher than the hip.
how.easier: Lift the leg only partway.
how.harder: Add an ankle weight, or a band from the foot to the hands.

video.title: How to Do Donkey Kicks: A Guide from Physical Therapists

how.gist: On hands and knees, lift one bent knee out to the side as high as your hip allows without tipping your body, then lower.
steps: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Keep one knee bent at 90° and lift it out to the side.
Raise it toward hip height while your hips and shoulders stay level.
Lower with control; finish the reps, then switch sides.
how.watch: Leaning the whole body away to get the leg higher.
how.easier: Lift the knee only partway, or do Clamshells.
how.harder: Add a band around your thighs above the knees.

video.title: How to Do a Fire Hydrant Exercise: A Guide from Physical Therapists

how.gist: Lie on your side and lift the straight top leg, slightly behind your body with toes forward, then lower it slowly.
steps: Lie on your side, bottom knee bent for balance, top leg straight in line with your body.
Move the top leg slightly behind your hips and point the toes forward, not up.
Lift the leg toward the ceiling without rolling your hips back.
Lower slowly and repeat; then switch sides.
how.watch: Hips rolling back so the toes turn up and the front of the hip does the work.
how.easier: Do Clamshells instead.
how.harder: Add an ankle weight, or a band around your ankles.

video.title: Foolproof Guide to Side Lying Hip Abduction

exercises.name: Hip airplane
exercises.equipment: None, or a wall for balance

how.gist: Standing on one leg with your torso tipped forward, rotate your pelvis open toward the ceiling, then back closed over the standing hip.
steps: Stand on one leg, knee soft, and hinge forward until your torso and back leg are nearly level.
Hold a wall or rack lightly if you need it for balance.
Turn your hips and chest open, away from the standing leg, rotating at the standing hip.
Turn back past square so your chest points down toward the standing side; that is one rep.
how.watch: Turning only the shoulders while the pelvis stays still.
how.easier: Keep a hand on a wall and turn through a smaller range.
how.harder: Do it slowly with no support.

video.title: Hip Airplane Exercise For Improved Balance, Mobility, And Glute Med Strength

how.gist: Do a Romanian deadlift with most of your weight on the front leg and the back foot just touching down as a kickstand.
steps: Stand with one foot forward and the other back, its toes level with the front heel.
Put most of your weight on the front leg, back heel up, both knees soft.
Push your hips back and lower the weights along the front leg, back flat.
At a good hamstring stretch, drive the hips forward to stand. Switch legs each set.
how.watch: Pushing off the back foot, so the front leg does not do most of the work.
how.easier: Keep both feet level: a Romanian deadlift.
how.harder: Lift the back foot off the floor: a Single-leg deadlift.

video.channel: Women's Strength Nation by Holly Perkins
video.title: B Stance RDL (Romanian Deadlift)

exercises.name: Cable glute kickback
exercises.equipment: Cable with ankle strap, or band

how.gist: With an ankle strap on a low cable, kick one leg straight back by squeezing the glute, then bring it back slowly.
steps: Fit an ankle strap on a low cable, face the stack and hold the frame, hinged slightly forward.
Stand on the other leg with that knee soft and your hips square.
Push the strapped leg back and a little up until the hip is straight, squeezing the glute.
Return slowly until the foot is beside the standing one.
how.watch: Arching the low back to kick higher instead of finishing with the glute.
how.easier: Do a Donkey kick on all fours.
how.harder: Pause one second at the back of every rep.

video.title: Glute Kickbacks with a Cable Machine (Less is More)

exercises.name: Hamstring bridge
exercises.equipment: None, or a bench or box

how.gist: Lie on your back with heels on the floor or a bench and legs nearly straight, and lift your hips by digging the heels in.
steps: Lie on your back with heels on the floor or on a bench, knees only slightly bent.
Pull your toes up and dig your heels down and back toward you.
Lift your hips until your body is in a straight line, squeezing glutes and hamstrings.
Lower slowly. The straighter the legs, the harder it is.
how.watch: Arching the low back at the top instead of lifting through the heels.
how.easier: Bend the knees more: a Glute bridge.
how.harder: Do it on one leg, the other held up.

video.title: Long Lever Hamstring Bridge (Build Resilient Hamstrings)

how.gist: Hold a stick along your back touching head, upper back and tailbone, and hinge forward without it losing contact.
steps: Hold a dowel behind you, one hand at your neck and one at your low back.
Set it so it touches the back of your head, your upper back and your tailbone.
Unlock the knees and push your hips back, letting your chest come forward.
Stop at a hamstring stretch, or when a contact point lifts, then stand tall.
how.watch: The stick leaving the tailbone or the head as the back rounds or the chin lifts.
how.easier: Stand a foot from a wall and push your hips back to touch it.
how.harder: Move on to a light Romanian deadlift.

video.title: How To Do A Hip Hinge w/ A Dowel - Tangelo Health

how.gist: Lie on your back, knees bent, with a ball between your knees, and squeeze it steadily for the set time.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent and feet flat, with a ball or folded pillow between your knees.
Squeeze your knees together into the ball, building up steadily rather than in a jerk.
Hold the squeeze for the set time, breathing normally.
Relax slowly and rest before the next hold.
how.watch: Holding your breath while you squeeze.
how.easier: Squeeze at about half effort.
how.harder: Do a Copenhagen plank.

video.title: Adductor Ball Squeeze

how.gist: Stand on the balls of your feet on a step, lower your heels below it, then rise as high as you can.
steps: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step or platform, heels hanging off.
Keep your knees straight but not locked.
Lower your heels slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves.
Rise as high as you can onto your toes, pause, and lower again.
how.watch: Bouncing at the bottom instead of lowering into a slow stretch.
how.harder: Do Single-leg calf raise.

how.gist: Sit with your knees bent and the load on your thighs, and raise your heels as high as you can, then lower into a stretch.
steps: Sit with the balls of your feet on a block and the pad or weight across your lower thighs.
Release the safety and lower your heels as far as they go.
Push through the balls of your feet to lift your heels as high as possible.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
how.watch: Short, fast bounces that skip both the bottom and the top.

how.gist: Stand on one foot on a step, lower your heel below it and rise as high as you can on that foot.
steps: Stand on the ball of one foot on a step, holding something for balance.
Hook the other foot behind your ankle.
Lower the heel slowly below the step.
Rise as high as you can, pause, and lower again. Then switch feet.
how.watch: Rolling onto the outside of the foot as you rise.
how.easier: Do Standing calf raise on both feet.
how.harder: Hold a dumbbell in the hand on the working side.

exercises.equipment: Donkey calf machine or a step

how.gist: Bent forward at the hips with straight legs, rise onto your toes from a deep heel stretch, then lower slowly.
steps: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step, hinge forward and rest your forearms on a bench.
On a machine, set the pad across your hips instead.
Keep your knees almost straight and lower your heels into a deep stretch.
Rise as high as you can onto your toes, then lower slowly.
how.watch: Bending the knees, which takes the stretch off the calves.
how.harder: Hang a plate from a dip belt.

video.title: The Donkey Calf Raise

how.gist: In the leg press, put the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform and push it with your ankles only.
steps: Sit in the leg press with the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
Press it out with your legs nearly straight; leave the safeties locked if the machine allows.
Let your toes come back toward you to stretch your calves.
Push through the balls of your feet to point your toes as far as you can.
how.watch: Feet slipping on the edge of the platform.

how.gist: Lean your back against a wall with your heels out in front and lift your toes toward your shins, then lower slowly.
steps: Stand with your back against a wall, heels about a foot out in front.
Keep your legs straight and your weight on your heels.
Lift your toes and the front of your feet as high as you can.
Lower slowly until your toes almost touch the floor.
how.watch: Toes slapping down instead of lowering slowly.
how.easier: Stand with your heels closer to the wall.
how.harder: Move your heels further out, or use a tib bar or a plate on your feet.

video.title: Tibialis Wall Raises Exercise

how.gist: Sitting with a band around your forefoot pulling it inward, turn the foot outward against the band, then return slowly.
steps: Sit with your legs straight and loop a band around the front of one foot.
Anchor the band to the inside: around the other foot or a fixed post.
Keep the leg still and turn the sole of your foot outward against the band.
Return slowly to the start.
how.watch: Rotating the whole leg instead of moving at the ankle.

video.title: Ankle Eversion with Resistive Band - Ask Doctor Jo

how.gist: Sitting with a band around your forefoot pulling it outward, turn the foot inward against the band, then return slowly.
steps: Sit with your legs straight and loop a band around the front of one foot.
Anchor the band to the outside: a fixed post, or the other foot crossed over.
Keep the leg still and turn the sole of your foot inward against the band.
Return slowly to the start.
how.watch: Rotating the whole leg instead of moving at the ankle.

video.title: Seated ankle inversion/eversion

how.gist: Bounce quickly on the balls of your feet with stiff ankles and nearly straight knees, spending as little time on the ground as you can.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width and knees almost straight.
Rise onto the balls of your feet and keep your ankles stiff.
Bounce off the floor from your ankles, a few inches each time.
Keep each contact short and quiet, arms swinging lightly.
how.watch: Bending the knees to jump, which turns it into a squat jump.
how.easier: Bounce lower, or skip with a Jump rope.
how.harder: Hop on one leg, or bounce higher.

video.title: Pogo Jumps - Common Mistakes

how.gist: Walk forward on your heels with your toes and the balls of your feet pulled up off the floor.
steps: Stand tall and pull your toes and the fronts of your feet up as high as they go.
Walk forward in short steps on your heels only.
Keep your hips under you rather than leaning back.
Walk the set number of steps, then lower your feet and rest.
how.watch: Toes dropping toward the floor as the shins tire.
how.easier: Do a Tibialis raise with your back against a wall.
how.harder: Take more steps, or walk backwards on your heels.

video.title: Exercises with an Athletic Trainer: Heel Walking

how.gist: Stand on one foot with the knee soft and hold steady for the set time, then switch legs.
steps: Stand near a wall or counter you can touch if you need to.
Lift one foot and balance on the other, knee soft and hips level.
Spread your weight across the big toe, little toe and heel, and keep still.
Hold for the set time, then switch legs.
how.watch: The standing hip sagging out to the side.
how.easier: Keep a fingertip on the wall.
how.harder: Close your eyes, stand on a cushion, or try a Hip airplane.

video.title: Single Leg Balance Exercise

how.gist: Barefoot, lift your arch by drawing the ball of your foot toward your heel without curling your toes, hold, then relax.
steps: Sit with one bare foot flat and relaxed on the floor.
Keep the toes long and flat, and draw the ball of the foot toward the heel.
Feel the arch lift while the big toe and heel stay down.
Hold about 5 seconds, then relax fully.
how.watch: Curling or clawing the toes instead of shortening the foot.
how.easier: Shape the arch with your hand the first few times to find it.
how.harder: Do it standing, then standing on one leg.

video.title: The Short Foot exercise | A great way to strengthen your feet

how.gist: Hold a straight line from head to heels on your forearms and toes, ribs down and glutes tight.
steps: Set your forearms on the floor, elbows under your shoulders, and step your feet back.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your stomach as if about to be poked.
Keep one straight line from head to heels, eyes on the floor.
Breathe steadily and hold until the line starts to sag.
how.watch: Hips sagging toward the floor so the low back arches.
how.easier: Hold it from your knees instead of your toes.
how.harder: Do RKC plank instead, or rest a plate across your upper back.

how.gist: Hold your body in a straight sideways line on one forearm and the edges of your feet, hips lifted.
steps: Lie on your side, elbow under your shoulder, legs straight and feet stacked.
Lift your hips until your body is straight from head to heels.
Keep the top hip stacked over the bottom one rather than rolling forward.
Hold, then switch sides.
how.watch: Hips sinking toward the floor or drifting back behind the line.
how.easier: Bend your knees and hold from the bottom knee.
how.harder: Do Side plank leg raise instead.

how.gist: Hang from a bar and raise straight legs to hip height or higher, curling the pelvis up without swinging.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar, hands shoulder-width, shoulders pulled down from your ears.
Brace and tilt your pelvis back slightly before the legs move.
Raise straight legs to at least hip height, curling your hips up at the top.
Lower slowly to a dead stop before the next rep.
how.watch: Swinging the body so momentum, not the abs, lifts the legs.
how.easier: Do Hanging knee raise instead.
how.harder: Do Toes to bar instead.

video.title: Hanging Leg Raise | HOW-TO

how.gist: Hang from a bar and draw your knees up toward your chest, rolling the pelvis up, then lower under control.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar, shoulders active and legs together.
Bring your knees up toward your chest.
Curl your hips up at the top so your pelvis tilts toward you.
Lower slowly until the legs hang still.
how.watch: Lifting the thighs to hip height without ever curling the pelvis.
how.easier: Do Captain's chair knee raise instead.
how.harder: Do Hanging leg raise instead.

how.gist: Hang from a bar and lift your feet all the way up to touch the bar between your hands.
steps: Hang from the bar with hands about shoulder-width apart.
Pull the bar down toward your hips with straight arms as the legs start to rise.
Bring your feet up and touch the bar between your hands.
Lower with control; in a kipping set, let the legs swing back behind you into the next rep.
how.watch: Shoulders going slack, so the body swings and the feet fall short of the bar.
how.easier: Do Knees to elbows instead.
how.harder: Do them strict, with no swing between reps.

video.title: CrossFit Movement Progression: Toes-To-Bar

how.gist: Support yourself on straight arms and hold your legs straight out in front at hip height.
steps: Put your hands beside your hips on parallettes, dip bars or the floor, arms straight.
Push down hard so your shoulders lift away from your ears.
Lift your legs straight out in front, together, at hip height.
Lock your knees, point your toes and hold.
how.watch: Shoulders shrugging up to the ears as the body sinks between the arms.
how.easier: Hold it with one or both knees tucked to your chest.
how.harder: Hold it on rings.

video.title: L-Sit: Step-by-Step Progressions

how.gist: Lie on your back, low back pressed down, and hold straight arms and legs just off the floor in a shallow banana shape.
steps: Lie on your back and press your low back into the floor.
Lift your shoulders, arms overhead and straight legs a few inches off the floor.
If your low back starts to lift, raise the legs higher.
Hold the shape, breathing short and steady.
how.watch: Low back peeling off the floor.
how.easier: Bend your knees and keep your arms by your sides.
how.harder: Do Hollow rock instead.

video.title: How to Do a Hollow Hold: A Guide from Physical Therapists

how.gist: Hold the hollow body shape and rock back and forth along your back without letting the shape break.
steps: Get into a hollow hold: low back down, arms overhead, legs straight and off the floor.
Lock that shape so your body moves as one piece.
Rock toward your shoulders, then toward your hips.
Keep your arms by your ears and legs together throughout.
how.watch: Bending at the hips or knees to make the rock, so the shape breaks.
how.easier: Do Hollow hold instead.
how.harder: Hold a light plate in your hands.

video.title: Hollow Rock Guide | How To, Benefits, and Mistakes

how.gist: Kneel holding an ab wheel, roll it forward as far as you can without the low back sagging, then pull it back.
steps: Kneel with the wheel under your shoulders, arms straight.
Tuck your pelvis slightly and squeeze your glutes.
Roll the wheel forward slowly, hips moving in line with your shoulders.
Stop before your low back sags, then pull back with your abs.
how.watch: Low back arching as the wheel rolls out.
how.easier: Roll out toward a wall so it stops the wheel short.
how.harder: Do it from your feet instead of your knees.

video.title: Ab Wheel- How to PROPERLY Use an Ab Wheel | MIND PUMP

how.gist: Lean onto a pair of low-hung rings with straight arms, let them glide forward overhead, then pull them back under you.
steps: Hang the rings around hip height and stand or kneel behind them, gripping with straight arms.
Brace into a straight line from feet or knees to shoulders.
Lean forward and let the rings move forward and up, arms straight.
Go only as far as you can keep the line, then pull the rings back to your hips.
how.watch: Hips sagging and the low back arching at the far end.
how.easier: Raise the rings so you stay more upright.
how.harder: Lower the rings toward the floor.

video.title: Ring Rollout

how.gist: Kneel facing a high cable, hold the rope beside your head and curl your ribs down toward your hips.
steps: Kneel facing a high pulley, holding the rope beside your head.
Set your hips slightly back and keep them still for the whole set.
Round your spine to bring your elbows down toward your thighs.
Pause, then uncurl slowly against the pull.
how.watch: Sitting back at the hips instead of rounding the spine.

video.title: The Kneeling Cable Rope Crunch (Awesome 6-Pack Ab Exercise)

how.gist: Lie on your back with knees bent and curl your head and shoulders up off the floor toward your hips.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat, fingertips lightly at your temples.
Breathe out and curl your head and shoulders off the floor.
Bring your ribs toward your hips while your low back stays down.
Lower slowly without resting at the bottom.
how.watch: Pulling on your head with your hands.
how.harder: Hold a plate on your chest.

how.gist: Lie on your back with knees bent, sit all the way up, then lower back down with control.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat; anchor them if you need to.
Cross your arms on your chest or reach them forward.
Curl up off the floor and sit up tall.
Lower back down slowly, one part of your spine at a time.
how.watch: Yanking yourself up with the arms and neck instead of curling.
how.easier: Do Crunch instead.
how.harder: Do Decline sit-up instead.

how.gist: Lie flat, then lift straight arms and straight legs together to meet over your hips, balancing on your seat.
steps: Lie on your back, arms overhead and legs straight.
Brace and lift your arms and legs at the same time.
Reach your hands toward your toes at the top, balanced on your seat.
Lower both slowly to just above the floor.
how.watch: Legs bending and dropping to the floor instead of lowering with control.
how.easier: Do Alternating V-up instead.
how.harder: Hold a light medicine ball or plate in your hands.

video.title: V-Ups Tutorial For Beginners (4 Variations Covered)

how.gist: Lie on your back, arms up and knees over hips, and slowly lower opposite arm and leg while your low back stays flat.
steps: Lie on your back, arms pointing at the ceiling, knees bent 90° over your hips.
Breathe out and press your low back gently into the floor.
Slowly reach one arm overhead as you straighten the opposite leg toward the floor.
Stop just before your back starts to arch, return, and switch sides.
how.watch: Low back arching off the floor as the leg goes down.
how.easier: Keep the knee bent and just tap the heel to the floor.
how.harder: Hold a light dumbbell or plate in the straight arms.

video.title: How to Do a Dead Bug: A Guide from Physical Therapists

how.gist: On hands and knees, reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back without letting your hips or back move.
steps: Kneel on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Brace gently so your back stays flat.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg straight back.
Pause, return without the hips tipping, and switch sides.
how.watch: Hips rotating or the low back arching as the leg goes up.
how.easier: Move only the leg, or only the arm, at first.
how.harder: Hold each reach for 5 to 10 seconds.

video.title: How to Do the Bird Dog Exercise: A Guide from Physical Therapists

how.gist: Sit leaning back with knees bent and turn your chest side to side, bringing the weight beside each hip.
steps: Sit with knees bent and lean back about 45°, back long and straight.
Hold the weight at your chest.
Turn your shoulders to one side, then the other, bringing the weight beside each hip.
Keep your chest up and turn from the ribs, not just the arms.
how.watch: Back rounding while only the arms swing side to side.
how.easier: Keep your heels on the floor and use no weight.
how.harder: Lift your feet off the floor.

how.gist: Stand side-on to a cable or band and press the handle straight out from your chest without letting it turn you.
steps: Stand side-on to a cable or band at chest height, handle held at your breastbone in both hands.
Step away until there is tension, feet hip-width, knees soft.
Press the handle straight out in front of your chest.
Hold for a breath, resisting the twist, then bring it back in.
how.watch: Torso turning toward the anchor as the arms straighten.
how.easier: Use a lighter band or stand closer to the anchor.
how.harder: Do it half-kneeling, or hold the press out longer.

video.channel: Girls Gone Strong | Women's Health & Fitness
video.title: Pallof Press - How To Do Pallof Presses + Variations

how.gist: Hang from a bar with your legs raised toward it and rotate them from side to side like a wiper, under control.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar and raise straight legs until your feet are near the bar.
Hold your hips up in that pike.
Rotate your legs down to one side, only as far as you can control.
Bring them back through the middle and over to the other side.
how.watch: Hips dropping and the legs swinging instead of rotating under control.
how.easier: Do Lying windshield wipers instead.
how.harder: Keep the legs fully straight and go further to each side.

video.title: How To: Hanging Windshield Wiper

how.gist: Lie on a bench gripping it behind your head and lower your straight body, shoulders to toes, as one rigid lever.
steps: Lie on a bench and grip it behind your head.
Raise your hips and legs until they point up, weight on your upper back.
Lock a straight line from shoulders to toes.
Lower slowly, body straight, to just above the bench, then raise it again.
how.watch: Bending at the hips so the body folds instead of moving as one piece.
how.easier: Bend your knees, or do only the slow lowering.
how.harder: Pause for 2 seconds halfway down.

video.title: Master the DRAGON FLAG | Learn in 5 Minutes

how.gist: Hang from a bar and raise your straight body up to horizontal with straight arms, then lower back to the hang.
steps: Hang from a bar or rings, arms straight, shoulders pulled down.
Press the bar toward your hips with straight arms to lift your body.
Rise until your body is horizontal, face up, hips level with your shoulders.
Lower slowly back to the hang without bending the arms.
how.watch: Elbows bending, which turns it into a row.
how.easier: Do it with your knees tucked to your chest.
how.harder: Pause at horizontal for 2 seconds.

video.title: Front Lever RAISES Tutorial | How To Achieve A Front Lever

how.gist: Hang from a bar and hold your body straight and horizontal, face up, with straight arms.
steps: Hang from a bar, hands shoulder-width, arms straight.
Pull the bar down toward your hips without bending your elbows.
Lift until your body is horizontal, hips in line with shoulders and feet.
Squeeze your glutes, point your toes and hold.
how.watch: Hips sagging below the line of the shoulders.
how.easier: Hold it with knees tucked, then with one leg out, as you get stronger.

video.title: Front Lever for Beginners (ALL PROGRESSIONS)

how.gist: Hold your body straight and horizontal, face down, below a bar or rings with straight arms.
steps: From a hang, tuck your knees and roll back through your arms until you hang upside down.
Lower your body slowly, face down, until it is horizontal.
Keep your arms straight and your body in one line.
Hold, then tuck and roll back out the way you came.
how.watch: Bending the elbows or piking at the hips.
how.easier: Hold it with your knees tucked, or with your legs straddled wide.

video.title: Back Lever Tutorial (Progressions + Training Structure)

how.gist: Lie on your back with straight legs just off the floor and kick them up and down in small, quick alternating beats.
steps: Lie on your back, hands under your hips or by your sides.
Press your low back down and lift both legs a few inches off the floor.
Kick the legs up and down in small, quick alternating beats.
Keep the low back down the whole time.
how.watch: Low back arching off the floor as the legs tire.
how.easier: Kick with the legs higher, closer to vertical.
how.harder: Lift your shoulders too, as in a hollow hold.

how.gist: From a high plank, drive your knees toward your chest one at a time, quickly, keeping your hips level.
steps: Start in a push-up position, hands under your shoulders.
Drive one knee toward your chest.
Switch legs quickly, as if running in place.
Keep your hips level with your shoulders throughout.
how.watch: Hips piking up high as the pace rises.
how.easier: Step the feet in one at a time, slowly.
how.harder: Do Cross-body mountain climber instead.

how.gist: Stand holding a weight in one hand, bend sideways toward it, then pull yourself back upright.
steps: Stand tall with a weight in one hand and the other hand on your hip.
Bend sideways toward the weight, sliding it down your leg.
Return upright using the opposite side of your waist.
Finish the set, then switch hands.
how.watch: Twisting or leaning forward instead of bending straight to the side.
how.harder: Do Roman chair side bend instead.

how.gist: Pull a cable, band or ball diagonally across your body from high on one side to low on the other, turning through the trunk.
steps: Set the cable or band high on one side; hold the handle or ball in both hands, arms long.
Stand side-on to it, feet wider than your hips.
Pull down and across to the opposite hip, turning your trunk and pivoting the back foot.
Return slowly along the same line.
how.watch: Pulling with the arms alone while the trunk stays still.

video.title: How to perform a Cable Wood Chop

how.gist: From a forearm plank with your feet on sliders, push your body back and forth from the elbows while your hips stay level.
steps: Get into a forearm plank with your feet on sliders, a towel or in suspension straps.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes so your body is one straight line.
Push through your forearms to slide your body back until your shoulders pass your elbows.
Pull yourself forward again with your forearms, back to the start.
how.watch: Hips sagging toward the floor as the body slides back.
how.easier: Slide back only a few inches, or do a Plank.
how.harder: Slide farther back, or set your feet in suspension straps.

video.title: Body Saw | Plank Variation Core Workout

how.gist: Hold a plank with your forearms on a stability ball and draw small circles with your elbows without letting your hips move.
steps: Rest your forearms on a stability ball, elbows under your shoulders, and walk your feet back into a plank.
Set your feet a little wider than your hips and brace your stomach.
Draw small circles with your forearms, as if stirring a pot.
Do the set number of circles one way, then the same the other way.
how.watch: Hips swaying or sagging as the ball moves.
how.easier: Do a Stability ball plank instead, or make the circles smaller.
how.harder: Make the circles bigger, or bring your feet closer together.

video.title: How To Perform A Swiss Ball Stir The Pot Exercise

how.gist: Kneel with your forearms on a stability ball and roll it forward until your body is long, then pull it back without your back sagging.
steps: Kneel behind a stability ball and rest your forearms or fists on top of it.
Brace your stomach and tuck your tailbone slightly so your back is flat.
Roll the ball forward, letting your hips and arms extend together.
Stop before your low back arches, then pull the ball back with your arms.
how.watch: Low back arching at the far end of the roll.
how.easier: Roll out a shorter distance.
how.harder: Do an Ab wheel rollout instead.

video.title: Trainer Tips: Stability Ball Rollout

how.gist: Kneel holding a barbell loaded with round plates and roll it forward until your body is long, then pull it back with a flat back.
steps: Load a barbell with small round plates and kneel behind it, hands shoulder-width on the bar.
Set your shoulders over the bar, brace your stomach and tuck your tailbone slightly.
Roll the bar forward, letting your hips and arms extend together.
Stop before your low back arches, then pull the bar back to under your shoulders.
how.watch: Hips piking up first on the way back instead of the body moving as one.
how.easier: Do a Stability ball rollout instead.
how.harder: Roll out farther, or start from standing on your feet.

video.title: How to : Barbell Ab Rollout - Abs Roller Exercise

how.gist: Hold a forearm plank while squeezing everything hard and pulling your elbows toward your toes, for short, all-out holds.
steps: Set up a forearm plank with elbows under your eyes and hands in fists.
Squeeze your glutes and tilt your pelvis so your tailbone tucks under.
Lock your knees and squeeze your thighs.
Pull your elbows toward your toes without moving them, and hold for 10–20 seconds.
how.watch: Letting the squeeze fade so it turns back into an ordinary relaxed plank.
how.easier: Do a Plank instead.
how.harder: Set your elbows a little farther forward.

video.title: RKC Plank | Core Strengthening Exercise

how.gist: Hold a forearm plank with your forearms on a stability ball, keeping the ball and your body still.
steps: Rest your forearms on a stability ball, elbows under your shoulders.
Walk your feet back until your body makes one straight line.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes.
Hold, keeping the ball from rolling.
how.watch: Hips sagging toward the floor as you tire.
how.easier: Do it from your knees, or do a Plank.
how.harder: Do Stir the pot instead.

video.title: How to Plank on a Stability Ball | Health

how.gist: From a high plank, tap each hand to the opposite shoulder in turn while your hips stay still.
steps: Get into a high plank, hands under shoulders and feet a little wider than your hips.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes.
Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder, then put it back down.
Switch hands, keeping your hips level the whole time.
how.watch: Hips rocking side to side with each tap.
how.easier: Set your feet wider, or do it from your knees.
how.harder: Bring your feet together, or pause on each tap.

video.title: How To Properly Do a Plank with Shoulder Taps - Strength Exercises - Wellen

how.gist: Move from a forearm plank up to a high plank one arm at a time, then back down, while your hips stay level.
steps: Start in a forearm plank, feet about hip-width apart.
Place one hand where its elbow was and push up, then do the same with the other hand.
Lower back to one forearm, then the other.
Switch which arm leads each rep, or each set.
how.watch: Hips swinging side to side as you change arms.
how.easier: Do it from your knees.
how.harder: Bring your feet together, or wear a weight plate on your back.

video.title: How to do an Up-Down Plank

how.gist: On hands and knees with toes tucked, lift your knees an inch off the floor and hold with a flat back.
steps: Get on hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Tuck your toes under and brace your stomach.
Lift your knees an inch off the floor.
Hold, keeping your back flat and breathing.
how.watch: Hips rising high so the weight shifts onto the hands.
how.easier: Lift your knees for shorter holds, or do a Bird dog instead.
how.harder: Lift one hand, or one hand and the opposite foot, without rocking.

video.title: How To Do A Bear Plank with Traci Copeland | The Right Way | Well+Good

how.gist: From a plank, bring one knee out to the side toward the same elbow, return it, and alternate.
steps: Get into a high plank or a forearm plank.
Lift one foot and draw the knee out to the side toward the elbow on that side.
Return the foot to the start without the hips lifting.
Switch sides each rep.
how.watch: Hips piking up as the knee comes forward.
how.easier: Move slowly from a forearm plank, bringing the knee only part way.
how.harder: Pause with the knee at the elbow for a second.

video.title: Spiderman Plank

how.gist: From a high plank, reach one arm straight ahead, hold a beat, put it back and switch, while your hips stay square.
steps: Get into a high plank, feet a little wider than your hips.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes.
Reach one arm straight out in front at shoulder height and hold for a second.
Put it back down and switch arms.
how.watch: Hips turning toward the lifted arm.
how.easier: Set your feet wider, or do it from a forearm plank.
how.harder: Reach the opposite leg back at the same time.

video.title: How To Do A STRAIGHT ARM PLANK REACH | Exercise Demonstration Video and Guide

how.gist: From a high plank with a weight beside you, reach under with the far hand and drag the weight across, then alternate.
steps: Get into a high plank with a kettlebell or other weight just behind one hand.
Set your feet a little wider than your hips and brace your stomach.
Reach under your body with the opposite hand and drag the weight across to the other side.
Put that hand back down and drag it back with the other hand.
how.watch: Hips twisting or lifting as you reach under.
how.easier: Set your feet wider, or use a lighter weight.
how.harder: Bring your feet closer together, or use a heavier weight.

video.title: Core Stability- Kettlebell Plank Pull Through

how.gist: Hold a high plank and jump your feet out wide and back in, like a jumping jack, while your hips stay level.
steps: Get into a high plank, hands under shoulders and feet together.
Brace your stomach so your body is one line.
Jump both feet out wide, then jump them back together.
Keep going at a steady pace without bouncing your hips.
how.watch: Hips bouncing up and down with each jump.
how.easier: Step one foot out and in at a time.
how.harder: Go faster, or do it from a forearm plank.

video.title: Plank Jacks

how.gist: In a side plank, lower your hip toward the floor and lift it back up above a straight line.
steps: Lie on your side, elbow under your shoulder, legs straight and stacked.
Lift your hips into a side plank.
Lower your hip until it nearly touches the floor.
Lift it back up a little past straight, then repeat. Switch sides.
how.watch: Hips drifting backward or rolling forward instead of moving straight down and up.
how.easier: Do it with your knees bent and resting on the floor.
how.harder: Rest a weight plate on your top hip.

video.title: How to do a Side Plank with Hip Lift - Hip Dip

how.gist: Hold a side plank and raise and lower your top leg while your hips stay high.
steps: Lie on your side, elbow under your shoulder, legs straight and stacked.
Lift your hips into a side plank.
Raise your top leg as high as you can without your hips dropping.
Lower it with control and repeat, then switch sides.
how.watch: Hips sagging or rolling back as the leg lifts.
how.easier: Bend your bottom knee and rest it on the floor.
how.harder: Loop a band around your knees or ankles.

video.title: Core Exercises: Side Plank With Leg Lift

how.gist: In a side plank, reach your top arm to the ceiling, then thread it under your body as you turn down, and open back up.
steps: Get into a side plank on your forearm, top arm reaching to the ceiling.
Keep your hips high and still.
Turn your chest toward the floor and reach the top arm under your body.
Turn back open and reach to the ceiling again. Switch sides after the set.
how.watch: Hips dropping toward the floor as you turn.
how.easier: Do it with your knees bent and resting on the floor.
how.harder: Hold a light dumbbell in the top hand.

video.title: Side plank: thread the needle

exercises.name: Suitcase deadlift
exercises.equipment: A dumbbell, kettlebell or trap bar

how.gist: Deadlift a single weight held at one side, standing up tall without leaning toward it.
steps: Stand with a dumbbell or kettlebell beside one foot.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to grip it, chest up and back flat.
Brace and stand up, keeping your shoulders level.
Lower it back beside your foot the same way. Switch sides after the set.
how.watch: The torso leaning or twisting toward the weight.
how.easier: Use a lighter weight, or lift it from a box or step.
how.harder: Do a Suitcase carry with the same weight.

video.title: Kettlebell Suitcase Deadlift

how.gist: Lie sideways on a 45° back extension bench and bend your torso down toward the floor, then lift it back up.
steps: Set up sideways on a 45° back extension bench, hip on the pad and feet locked in.
Cross your arms on your chest or put your hands behind your head.
Bend sideways to lower your torso toward the floor.
Lift back up until your body is straight or a little past. Switch sides after the set.
how.watch: Twisting forward or back instead of bending straight to the side.
how.easier: Do a Side bend standing instead.
how.harder: Hold a weight plate or dumbbell to your chest.

video.title: 45 Degree Side Bend

how.gist: With a bell locked out overhead, push your hip out and hinge down sideways to reach the floor, eyes on the bell, then stand.
steps: Press a kettlebell overhead in one hand and lock the arm. Turn both feet about 45° away from it.
Look up at the bell and push your hip out on the bell side.
Hinge down and sideways, sliding your free hand down the inside of the front leg toward the floor.
Keep the bell arm vertical as you go down and as you stand back up. Switch sides after the set.
how.watch: The bell arm drifting off vertical or the elbow bending.
how.easier: Do it with no weight, or hold the bell in the low hand instead.
how.harder: Use a heavier bell, keeping the arm straight.

video.title: How To: Kettlebell Windmill - Step By Step Breakdown

how.gist: Hold the end of a landmine bar at arm's length and swing it in an arc from one hip to the other, turning with your feet.
steps: Stand facing a landmine and hold the end of the bar at chest height in both hands, arms straight.
Brace your stomach and keep your arms straight.
Turn the bar down in an arc to one hip, pivoting your back foot.
Bring it back over the top and down to the other hip.
how.watch: Bending the arms so the shoulders do the work instead of the trunk.
how.easier: Use the bar with no plates, and keep the arc small.
how.harder: Add a small plate, keeping the arc smooth and controlled.

video.title: Standing Landmine Rotation

how.gist: Half-kneel side-on to a low cable and pull the handle up and across your body to above the far shoulder, torso tall.
steps: Set a cable or band low and half-kneel side-on to it, one knee down.
Hold the rope or handle in both hands by the hip nearest the cable.
Pull it up and across your chest, then press it out above the far shoulder.
Return along the same line with control. Switch sides after the set.
how.watch: The torso twisting and leaning instead of staying tall while the arms move.
how.easier: Do a Pallof press instead.
how.harder: Do it standing in a split stance, or do a Woodchop.

video.channel: Keep It Moving Physical Therapy & Wellness
video.title: Half Kneeling Cable Lift

how.gist: Stand side-on to a chest-high cable, arms straight, and turn your trunk away from it, then return slowly.
steps: Set a cable or band at chest height and stand side-on to it, feet shoulder-width.
Hold the handle in both hands at arm's length in front of your chest.
Turn your chest and hips away from the machine, letting your back heel pivot.
Return slowly to the start. Switch sides after the set.
how.watch: Bending the elbows and pulling with the arms instead of turning the trunk.
how.easier: Do a Pallof press instead.
how.harder: Do a Woodchop.

video.title: How To Do A STANDING CABLE CORE ROTATION | Exercise Demonstration Video and Guide

how.gist: Sit in a rotary torso machine and turn your trunk to one side against the resistance, then return slowly.
steps: Set the start position and sit with your legs locked in and chest against the pad.
Hold the handles and sit tall.
Turn your trunk to one side in a smooth, controlled arc.
Return slowly. Switch the setting to train the other side.
how.watch: Swinging fast so momentum does the work.
how.easier: Use a lighter setting and a smaller range.
how.harder: Do a Standing cable rotation instead.

video.title: Life Fitness Signature Series Torso Rotation Instructions

how.gist: Stand tall and pass a kettlebell around your waist from hand to hand, keeping your hips still, then change direction.
steps: Stand tall, feet hip-width, holding a kettlebell by the handle in front of you.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes.
Pass the bell around your waist, swapping hands behind your back and in front.
Do the set one way, then the other.
how.watch: Hips swaying to chase the bell around.
how.easier: Use a lighter bell.
how.harder: Use a heavier bell, or go faster without moving your hips.

video.title: kettlebell 3 - fundamental warmup movement - Around the World

how.gist: From a high plank, drive each knee toward the opposite elbow in turn, keeping your hips low.
steps: Get into a high plank, hands under your shoulders.
Brace your stomach so your body is one line.
Drive one knee across toward the opposite elbow, then return the foot.
Switch legs, keeping a steady rhythm.
how.watch: Hips bouncing up into a pike as the knees come in.
how.easier: Step each knee across slowly.
how.harder: Go faster, keeping the hips level.

video.title: How to Do Cross Body Mountain Climbers
