how.gist: Lie on your back with both knees dropped to one side and crunch your shoulders up off the floor.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, and let both knees drop to one side.
Put your fingertips lightly at your temples.
Breathe out and curl your shoulders up off the floor, ribs toward hips.
Lower slowly. Switch sides after the set.
how.watch: Pulling on the head with the hands.
how.easier: Cross your arms on your chest and curl up only a little.
how.harder: Do a Side jackknife instead.

video.title: How To: Oblique Floor Crunch

how.gist: Lie on your side and lift your stacked legs and your upper body toward each other, then lower.
steps: Lie on your side with legs straight and stacked, bottom arm along the floor.
Put your top hand lightly behind your head.
Lift both legs and your upper body at the same time, top elbow toward your hip.
Lower with control. Switch sides after the set.
how.watch: Rolling back onto the back instead of staying on the side.
how.easier: Do an Oblique crunch instead, or lift only the legs.
how.harder: Pause at the top for a second.

video.title: How To Do A SIDE JACKKNIFE | Exercise Demonstration Video and Guide

how.gist: Lying with your shoulders lifted, turn one elbow toward the opposite knee as the other leg straightens, and alternate slowly.
steps: Lie on your back, hands lightly behind your head, knees bent over your hips.
Curl your head and shoulders up off the floor.
Turn one shoulder toward the opposite knee as you straighten the other leg.
Switch sides slowly, keeping your shoulders up.
how.watch: Flapping the elbows and pulling the head while the shoulders barely turn.
how.easier: Keep the straight leg higher, or slow down.
how.harder: Hold each turn for two seconds.

video.title: How to Do Bicycle Crunches: A Guide from Physical Therapists

how.gist: Lie with knees bent and shoulders curled up, and reach side to side to tap each heel with your hand.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent and feet flat, a little wider than hips.
Curl your head and shoulders up, arms long by your sides.
Bend sideways to reach one hand to tap that heel.
Come back to centre and reach to the other side.
how.watch: Letting the head and shoulders drop to the floor between taps.
how.easier: Bring your feet closer to your hips.
how.harder: Set your feet farther away.

how.gist: Hang from a bar and raise your knees up and toward one side, then lower and switch sides.
steps: Hang from a bar with straight arms, legs together.
Brace your stomach to stop any swing.
Raise your knees up and across toward one shoulder, turning your hips.
Lower with control and raise them toward the other side.
how.watch: Swinging the legs up with momentum.
how.easier: Do a Captain's chair knee raise, turning to the side.
how.harder: Raise straight legs to the side instead of bent knees.

video.title: HANGING OBLIQUE KNEE RAISES

how.gist: From a forearm plank, turn your hips to dip one side toward the floor, then the other.
steps: Get into a forearm plank, feet together.
Brace your stomach and keep your shoulders square.
Turn your hips to lower one hip toward the floor.
Turn back through the middle and dip the other hip.
how.watch: Hips piking up as they turn.
how.easier: Do it from your knees.
how.harder: Move slowly and pause at each dip.

video.title: How to Do Plank Hip Dips | Health

how.gist: Lying on your back with knees bent, curl your hips off the floor to bring your knees toward your chest, then lower slowly.
steps: Lie on your back, arms by your sides or holding a bench behind your head.
Lift your knees over your hips, bent to 90°.
Breathe out and curl your hips up off the floor, knees toward your chest.
Lower your hips slowly, one vertebra at a time.
how.watch: Swinging the legs instead of curling the hips up.
how.easier: Make the curl smaller, or do a Dead bug.
how.harder: Do a Lying leg raise instead.

video.channel: Lift With Michelle - Exercise Form Tutorials
video.title: Reverse Crunch | Core & Ab Strength Exercise Tutorial

how.gist: Lying on your back, raise your straight legs to vertical and lower them slowly without your back arching.
steps: Lie on your back, hands under your hips or holding a bench behind your head.
Press your low back toward the floor and keep your legs straight.
Raise your legs until they point at the ceiling.
Lower them slowly, stopping before your low back arches.
how.watch: Low back arching off the floor as the legs come down.
how.easier: Do a Reverse crunch instead, or bend your knees.
how.harder: Do a Hanging leg raise instead.

video.title: How To Perform The Lying Leg Raise Exercise

how.gist: Lie with your legs straight up and reach your hands toward your toes, lifting your shoulders off the floor.
steps: Lie on your back and raise your legs straight up toward the ceiling.
Reach both arms up toward your feet.
Breathe out and curl your shoulders off the floor, reaching for your toes.
Lower your shoulders slowly, legs staying up.
how.watch: Legs drifting toward the face instead of staying vertical.
how.easier: Bend your knees slightly, or do a Crunch.
how.harder: Hold a light plate or medicine ball in your hands.

video.title: How to do a Toe Touch Crunch | Core Workout

how.gist: Sit leaning back on your hands, then pull your knees in to your chest and push your legs back out without your feet touching down.
steps: Sit on the floor or a bench edge, hands behind your hips, leaning back a little.
Lift your feet and stretch your legs out long.
Pull your knees in toward your chest as your chest comes toward them.
Push your legs back out, keeping your feet off the floor.
how.watch: Leaning far back on the hands so the stomach does little.
how.easier: Let your heels touch down between reps.
how.harder: Hold a dumbbell between your feet, or do a V-up.

video.title: How to Do a Seated Knee Tuck

how.gist: With feet hooked on a decline bench, sit up from lying until upright, then lower slowly.
steps: Lie back on a decline bench with your feet hooked under the pads.
Cross your arms on your chest or hold a weight to it.
Curl your head and shoulders up and sit all the way up.
Lower back down slowly, rounding down rather than dropping.
how.watch: Yanking on the head with the hands to get up.
how.easier: Do a Sit-up on the floor, or set the bench flatter.
how.harder: Hold a weight plate to your chest.

video.title: How To: Decline Sit-Up

how.gist: Sitting with your soles together and knees out, lie back to touch the floor overhead, then sit up and touch your feet.
steps: Sit with the soles of your feet together and knees falling out.
Put an AbMat or folded towel behind your low back.
Lie back with arms overhead until your hands touch the floor.
Swing your arms forward and sit up to touch your feet.
how.watch: Dropping back fast and hitting the head on the floor.
how.easier: Do a Crunch instead.
how.harder: Do a GHD sit-up.

video.title: The AbMat Sit-up

how.gist: Sitting on a GHD with feet locked, lean back until about parallel, then kick your knees straight to sit up and touch the footplate.
steps: Sit on the GHD pad facing away from the footplate, feet locked in and knees slightly bent.
Lean back with your arms reaching, until your body is about parallel to the floor.
Straighten your knees hard to bring your body back up.
Sit up and reach your hands toward the footplate.
how.watch: Doing full range and high reps on the first sessions; build range and volume gradually.
how.easier: Lean back only to above parallel, or do a Butterfly sit-up.
how.harder: Lean back further, below parallel.

video.title: Midline Stabilization: The GHD Sit-Up

how.gist: Sit in an ab crunch machine and curl your ribs toward your hips against the resistance, then return slowly.
steps: Set the seat and pads so you sit tall with the pads or handles at your chest or shoulders.
Brace your stomach.
Curl your ribs down toward your hips, rounding your upper back.
Return slowly until your back is straight.
how.watch: Pulling with the arms instead of rounding the spine.
how.easier: Use a lighter setting, or do a Crunch.
how.harder: Do a Cable crunch instead.

video.title: Life Fitness Circuit Series Ab Crunch Instructions

how.gist: Lie with your low back on a stability ball and crunch your shoulders up, then lower over the ball.
steps: Sit on a stability ball and walk your feet out until your low back is on the ball.
Plant your feet hip-width and put your fingertips at your temples.
Breathe out and curl your shoulders up, ribs toward your hips.
Lower back over the ball so your stomach lengthens.
how.watch: Sitting too far up the ball, so the ball is under the hips and the range is lost.
how.easier: Do a Crunch on the floor instead.
how.harder: Hold a weight plate to your chest.

video.title: How To Swiss Ball Crunch | Nuffield Health

how.gist: Lying on your back with straight legs just off the floor, cross them over and under each other side to side.
steps: Lie on your back, hands under your hips, and press your low back toward the floor.
Lift both straight legs a few inches off the floor.
Open the legs a little and cross one over the other.
Open and cross again with the other leg on top, keeping a steady rhythm.
how.watch: Low back arching off the floor.
how.easier: Lift your legs higher.
how.harder: Lift your head and shoulders off the floor too.

video.title: Scissor Kicks (horizontal)- Cantrell Center Exercise Instructional Videos

how.gist: With your back on the pad and forearms on the rests, raise your knees toward your chest and lower them slowly.
steps: Stand in a captain's chair, back against the pad, forearms on the arm rests.
Lift your feet off the step and let your legs hang.
Raise your knees toward your chest, curling your pelvis up at the top.
Lower your legs slowly without swinging.
how.watch: Swinging the legs up and dropping them.
how.easier: Do a Reverse crunch instead.
how.harder: Raise straight legs, or do a Hanging leg raise.

video.title: How To Do A CAPTAIN'S CHAIR KNEE RAISE | Exercise Demonstration Video and Guide

how.gist: Hang from a bar and pull your knees up until they touch your elbows, then lower with control.
steps: Hang from a bar, hands shoulder-width.
Press the bar down with straight arms to engage your lats.
Curl your knees up and touch them to your elbows.
Lower your legs with control back under the bar.
how.watch: Swinging wildly so the legs come up on momentum and the body sways.
how.easier: Do a Hanging knee raise instead.
how.harder: Do Toes to bar.

video.title: The Strict Knees to Elbows

how.gist: Sit with legs straight and hands beside your knees, and lift your heels off the floor using your hip flexors.
steps: Sit with your legs straight and together, or in a wide straddle.
Put your hands on the floor beside your knees, fingers forward.
Lean forward slightly and lift both heels off the floor, knees locked.
Hold for a second, lower, and repeat.
how.watch: Bending the knees or leaning back to get the heels up.
how.easier: Lift one leg at a time.
how.harder: Put your hands farther back toward your hips, or do an L-sit.

video.title: Core Compression, Seated Pike Leg Lifts

how.gist: From a high plank with your feet on a ball, lift your hips into a pike with straight legs, then lower back to plank.
steps: Get into a high plank with your shins or feet on a stability ball.
Brace your stomach so your body is one line.
Keep your legs straight and lift your hips toward the ceiling, rolling the ball in.
Lower your hips back down to the plank without sagging.
how.watch: Hips sagging below the line on the way back down.
how.easier: Do a Stability ball knee tuck instead.
how.harder: Do it with your feet in suspension straps or on sliders.

video.title: Stability Ball Pike Tutorial // School of Calisthenics

how.gist: From a high plank with your shins on a ball, pull your knees toward your chest, then push the ball back out.
steps: Get into a high plank with your shins on a stability ball.
Brace your stomach so your body is one line.
Pull your knees in toward your chest, rolling the ball under you.
Push your legs back out to the plank.
how.watch: Hips sagging as the legs straighten.
how.easier: Hold a Stability ball plank first, or do a Mountain climber.
how.harder: Do a Stability ball pike instead.

video.title: Core Exercises: Knee Tuck on Stability Ball

how.gist: Lying on your back, pass a stability ball from your hands to your feet at the top of a V-up, then back on the next rep.
steps: Lie on your back, arms overhead holding a stability ball, legs straight.
Lift your arms and legs together and pass the ball into your feet.
Lower both with the ball between your feet, stopping before your back arches.
Lift again and pass the ball back to your hands.
how.watch: Low back arching as the arms and legs come down.
how.easier: Bend your knees, or lower only part way.
how.harder: Lower slowly, close to the floor, each rep.

video.channel: Get Healthy U - with Chris Freytag
video.title: How to do a Stability Ball Feet-Hand Pass Off

how.gist: Lying flat, lift one straight leg and your upper body together to reach for that foot, then lower and switch.
steps: Lie on your back, legs straight and arms overhead.
Lift one straight leg and your upper body at the same time.
Reach both hands toward that foot.
Lower with control and switch legs.
how.watch: Jerking up with the arms instead of curling up.
how.easier: Do a Toe-touch crunch instead.
how.harder: Do a V-up.

video.title: Alternating V-Ups

how.gist: Sit balanced on your sit bones with a long back, legs lifted and arms reaching forward, and hold the V shape.
steps: Sit with knees bent and feet on the floor, hands behind your thighs.
Lean back a little with a long, straight back.
Lift your feet until your shins are parallel to the floor.
Reach your arms forward, straighten your legs if you can, and hold.
how.watch: Rounding the back so the chest collapses.
how.easier: Keep your knees bent, or hold behind your thighs.
how.harder: Straighten your legs, or hold a weight plate to your chest.

video.channel: YYOGA at Home — yoga classes + tutorials
video.title: Boat Pose Yoga Tutorial (to strengthen your core)

how.gist: Lie on your back, legs up, and lower them together to one side and back, then the other, keeping your shoulders down.
steps: Lie on your back, arms out wide, palms down.
Lift your legs straight up, or bent at 90°, knees together.
Lower both legs to one side as far as your shoulders stay down.
Bring them back up through the middle and lower to the other side.
how.watch: The opposite shoulder lifting off the floor.
how.easier: Bend your knees to 90°, and go only part way.
how.harder: Do a Windshield wiper hanging from a bar.

video.title: How To Do A LYING WINDSHIELD WIPER | Exercise Demonstration Video and Guide

how.gist: Lying on your back with a band around your feet, drive one knee up toward your chest against the band, lower it slowly, and switch.
steps: Lie on your back, legs long, with a mini band around both feet, or no band.
Press your low back flat and keep your ribs down.
Drive one knee up toward your chest while the other leg stays long.
Lower it slowly and switch legs, keeping your low back flat.
how.watch: Low back arching off the floor as the knee drives up.
how.easier: Do it without a band, or with the resting foot flat and its knee bent.
how.harder: Use a stronger band, or hold the knee up for two seconds.

video.title: Supine Banded Hip Flexor March

how.gist: Lying with your knees bent, tilt your pelvis to flatten your low back into the floor, hold a moment, then let it go.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
Breathe out and tilt your pelvis back so your low back flattens into the floor.
Hold for a second or two without lifting your hips.
Breathe in and let your pelvis roll back to a small natural arch.
how.watch: Lifting the hips off the floor into a bridge.
how.easier: Make the movement smaller.
how.harder: Do a Dead bug.

video.title: How to do a Posterior Pelvic Tilt - Posture, Strength, & Warm Up - Wellen

how.gist: Breathe all the way out, draw your belly in toward your spine and up under your ribs, and hold.
steps: Stand tall, or start on hands and knees.
Breathe all the way out.
Draw your belly button in toward your spine and up under your ribs.
Hold for 10–20 seconds with small breaths, then relax.
how.watch: Lifting the chest and shoulders instead of drawing the belly in.
how.easier: Do it lying on your back with knees bent.
how.harder: Hold it longer, or keep it drawn in while you walk.

video.title: How To Do A Stomach Vacuum - Train Your Transverse Abdominis

how.gist: Curled up with legs lifted, pump your straight arms up and down, breathing in for five pumps and out for five, ten times.
steps: Lie on your back and lift your legs to tabletop, or straight at an angle you can hold.
Curl your head and shoulders up and reach your arms long by your sides, just off the mat.
Pump your arms up and down a few inches.
Breathe in for five pumps and out for five. Do ten breaths, 100 pumps.
how.watch: Legs lower than you can hold, so the low back arches off the mat.
how.easier: Keep your knees bent in tabletop, or rest your head down.
how.harder: Straighten your legs and lower them closer to the mat.

video.title: PA Archives | Pilates Exercise: The Hundred

how.gist: From lying with arms overhead, peel your spine up off the mat one vertebra at a time to reach over your legs, then roll back down.
steps: Lie on your back, legs long and together, arms overhead.
Breathe in and bring your arms up toward the ceiling.
Breathe out, nod your chin and peel your spine up off the mat to reach over your legs.
Roll back down one vertebra at a time and reach the arms overhead.
how.watch: Jerking up with momentum so the legs fly off the mat.
how.easier: Bend your knees, or hold a band looped around your feet.
how.harder: Go slower, or do a Pilates teaser.

video.title: How To Do The Pilates Roll Up Exercise - For Anyone!

how.gist: Curled up, hug one knee in while the other leg reaches out long, then switch legs and hands with your torso still.
steps: Lie on your back and curl your head and shoulders up.
Draw one knee in. Put that side's hand on its ankle and the other hand on the knee.
Reach the other leg out straight at about 45°.
Switch legs, swapping your hands, keeping your torso still.
how.watch: Torso rocking side to side as the legs switch.
how.easier: Reach the straight leg higher, or rest your head down.
how.harder: Lower the straight leg, or do the Double-leg stretch.

video.title: PA Archives | Pilates Exercise: Single Leg Stretch

how.gist: Curled up and hugging your knees, reach your arms overhead and legs out long together, then circle the arms round to hug back in.
steps: Lie on your back, curl your head and shoulders up and hold your shins, knees in.
Breathe in and reach your arms overhead and your legs out long at once.
Keep your head and shoulders up and your low back on the mat.
Breathe out, circle your arms round to your shins and hug your knees back in.
how.watch: Head dropping back to the mat as the arms go overhead.
how.easier: Reach the legs higher, or do the Single-leg stretch.
how.harder: Reach the legs out lower.

video.title: PA Archives | Pilates Exercise: Double Leg Stretch

how.gist: Curled up with both legs straight, pull one leg toward you and hover the other low, then switch legs with a double pulse.
steps: Lie on your back and curl your head and shoulders up.
Lift one straight leg toward your face and hold its calf or ankle with both hands.
Hover the other straight leg just off the mat.
Switch legs in a scissor, pulsing the top leg twice toward you each time.
how.watch: Bending the knees instead of keeping both legs long.
how.easier: Keep the low leg higher, or hold behind the thigh.
how.harder: Take your hands off and switch faster.

video.title: Pilates Scissors straight leg stretch

how.gist: With legs lifted at about 45°, roll up into a V balanced on your sit bones, arms parallel to your legs, then roll down.
steps: Lie on your back, legs straight and together, lifted to about 45°.
Reach your arms overhead, then breathe in and bring them toward your legs.
Breathe out and roll up until you balance on your sit bones in a V, arms parallel to your legs.
Roll back down one vertebra at a time, legs staying where they are.
how.watch: The legs dropping as the body rolls up.
how.easier: Keep one foot on the mat with the knee bent, or do a Pilates roll-up.
how.harder: Lower and lift your legs with your body each rep.

video.title: PA Archives | Pilates Exercise: The Teaser

how.gist: Balance in a tight ball behind your sit bones, roll back onto your shoulder blades and roll up to balance without your feet landing.
steps: Sit and hug your shins, heels close to your seat and head tucked.
Lean back to balance just behind your sit bones, feet off the mat.
Breathe in and roll back onto your shoulder blades, keeping the shape.
Breathe out and roll up to balance again without your feet touching down.
how.watch: Rolling back onto the neck and head.
how.easier: Hold behind your thighs instead of your shins.
how.harder: Pull your heels in closer and make the ball tighter.

video.title: PA Archives | Pilates Exercise: Rolling Like A Ball

how.gist: Lying with one leg pointing at the ceiling, draw circles with it across your body and around, keeping your pelvis still.
steps: Lie on your back, arms by your sides, one leg straight up and the other long on the mat.
Press the backs of your arms into the mat to keep your pelvis level.
Draw a circle with the raised leg: across your body, down, out and back up.
Do five circles each way, then switch legs.
how.watch: Pelvis rocking with the leg as the circles get too big.
how.easier: Bend the bottom knee with the foot flat, and make the circles smaller.
how.harder: Make the circles bigger while the pelvis stays still.

video.title: Pilates Leg Circles with Alisa Wyatt

how.gist: Lying with your legs in tabletop, lower one foot to tap the floor with the knee still bent, lift it back and switch.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent to 90° over your hips.
Breathe out and draw your stomach in so your low back stays still.
Keep the knee bent and lower one foot to tap the floor.
Lift it back to tabletop and tap the other foot.
how.watch: Low back arching off the mat as the foot lowers.
how.easier: Keep one foot on the floor and tap with the other only.
how.harder: Tap both feet together, or do a Dead bug.

video.title: Toe Taps On the Mat⎮Pilates Encyclopedia

how.gist: Lying face down with arms and legs lifted, flutter opposite arm and leg in small quick beats while you breathe in and out.
steps: Lie face down, arms reaching overhead and legs straight, hip-width.
Lift your head, chest, arms and legs just off the mat, looking at the floor.
Flutter opposite arm and leg up and down in small, quick beats.
Breathe in for five beats and out for five, then rest.
how.watch: Cranking the head back and looking forward, which bunches the neck.
how.easier: Lift only the arms, or only the legs, or do a Bird dog.
how.harder: Go longer, keeping the arms and legs long and low.

video.title: PA Archives | Pilates Exercise: Swimming

how.gist: Pull the bar from the floor, extend hips and knees hard, then pull under and catch it on your shoulders in a full front squat.
steps: Bar over the middle of your feet, hands just outside your legs, back flat, shoulders over the bar.
Push the floor away and raise the bar past your knees, keeping it close and your back angle steady.
From mid-thigh, extend hips and knees explosively so the bar brushes your upper thighs.
Pull yourself under, elbows whipping round, and catch the bar on your shoulders in a front squat.
Stand up from the squat.
how.watch: Bending the arms to pull before the hips and knees have finished extending.
how.easier: Do Hang clean instead.

video.title: Clean | Olympic Weightlifting Exercise Library

how.gist: Pull the bar from the floor and catch it on your shoulders in a partial squat, thighs above parallel.
steps: Set up as for a clean: bar over mid-foot, hands just outside your legs, back flat.
Push through your legs to bring the bar past your knees, close to your shins and thighs.
From mid-thigh, extend hips and knees explosively.
Pull under fast and catch the bar on your shoulders, elbows high, in a quarter squat.
Stand tall to finish.
how.watch: The bar swinging away from the body as the hips open.
how.easier: Do Hang clean instead.
how.harder: Do Clean instead, catching in a full squat.

video.title: Power Clean | Olympic Weightlifting Exercise Library

how.gist: Start standing with the bar at your thighs, lower it to above the knees, drive up explosively and catch it on your shoulders.
steps: Stand tall holding the bar with hands just outside your thighs.
Push your hips back to lower the bar to just above the knees, back flat, shoulders over the bar.
Extend hips and knees explosively, keeping the bar close.
Pull under and catch it on your shoulders, elbows high, in a squat, then stand.
how.watch: Bending the arms before the hips and knees finish extending.
how.easier: Use dumbbells, or start with the bar higher on the thigh.
how.harder: Do Clean instead, from the floor.

video.title: Hang Clean | Olympic Weightlifting Exercise Library

how.gist: Clean the bar from the floor to your shoulders, stand up, then drive it overhead with a dip and split under it.
steps: Clean the bar from the floor and catch it on your shoulders in a front squat.
Stand up, then reset your breath and grip, elbows slightly forward.
Dip a few inches straight down at the knees, torso upright.
Drive up hard and push yourself under the bar into a split, arms locked.
Step the front foot back, then the back foot forward, and stand with the bar overhead.
how.watch: Dipping forward onto the toes, so the drive sends the bar out in front.
how.easier: Practise the Clean and the Split jerk on their own first.

video.title: Clean & Jerk | Olympic Weightlifting Exercise Library

how.gist: Lift the bar from the floor to overhead in one movement with a wide grip, catching it in a full overhead squat.
steps: Take a grip wide enough that the bar sits in your hip crease standing; bar over mid-foot, back flat.
Push the floor away and raise the bar past your knees, keeping it close.
From high on the thigh, extend hips and knees explosively so the bar meets your hips.
Pull yourself under fast and punch your arms straight, catching in an overhead squat.
Stand up with the bar locked overhead.
how.watch: The bar looping away from you after the hips, so you chase it forward.
how.easier: Do Hang snatch or Power snatch instead.

video.title: Snatch | Olympic Weightlifting Exercise Library

how.gist: Snatch the bar from the floor to overhead, catching it on locked arms in a partial squat, thighs above parallel.
steps: Set up with a wide snatch grip, bar over mid-foot, back flat.
Raise the bar past your knees, keeping it close to your legs.
From high on the thigh, extend hips and knees explosively.
Pull under and punch your arms straight, catching in a quarter squat.
Stand tall with the bar locked overhead.
how.watch: Pressing the bar out at the end instead of catching it on locked arms.
how.easier: Do Hang snatch instead.
how.harder: Do Snatch instead, catching in a full squat.

video.title: Power Snatch | Olympic Weightlifting Exercise Library

how.gist: Start standing with a wide grip, lower the bar to above your knees, then jump it overhead and catch it on locked arms.
steps: Stand tall holding the bar with a wide snatch grip.
Hinge to lower the bar to just above the knees, back flat, shoulders over the bar.
Extend hips and knees hard so the bar meets your hips.
Pull under and catch it overhead on locked arms, then stand.
how.watch: Pulling with the arms before the hips have fully extended.
how.easier: Do Dumbbell snatch instead.
how.harder: Do Snatch instead, from the floor.

video.title: Hang Snatch | Olympic Weightlifting Exercise Library

how.gist: With the bar on your shoulders, dip and drive it upward, then split your feet and catch it on locked arms.
steps: Hold the bar on your shoulders, hands just outside them, feet hip-width.
Dip a few inches straight down at the knees, torso upright.
Drive up hard through the legs and push yourself under the bar.
Land in a split, front shin vertical, back knee bent, arms locked.
Step the front foot back, then the back foot forward, to stand.
how.watch: Dipping forward onto the toes so the bar goes out in front.
how.easier: Do Push press instead.

video.title: Split Jerk | Olympic Weightlifting Exercise Library

how.gist: Dip, drive the bar up off your shoulders with your legs, and catch it on locked arms in a shallow squat, feet side by side.
steps: Hold the bar on your shoulders, hands just outside them, feet hip-width.
Dip a few inches straight down, torso upright.
Drive hard through the legs to launch the bar.
Push yourself under it, catching on locked arms with knees bent.
Stand up with the bar overhead.
how.watch: Pressing the bar out with the arms instead of dropping under it.
how.easier: Do Push press instead.
how.harder: Do Split jerk instead.

video.title: Push Jerk | Olympic Weightlifting Exercise Library

how.gist: Lift the bar from the floor as in a clean and finish with a hard extension and shrug, without pulling under it.
steps: Set up as for a clean: hands just outside your legs, bar over mid-foot, back flat.
Push the floor away and bring the bar past your knees, close to your legs.
From mid-thigh, extend hips and knees hard, rising onto the balls of your feet.
Finish with a shrug, arms straight, then lower the bar under control.
how.watch: Bending the arms to pull instead of finishing with the legs and hips.

video.title: Clean Pull | Olympic Weightlifting Exercise Library

how.gist: Lift the bar from the floor with a wide snatch grip and finish with a hard extension and shrug, without pulling under.
steps: Set up as for a snatch: wide grip, bar over mid-foot, back flat.
Push the floor away and bring the bar past your knees, close to your legs.
From high on the thigh, extend hips and knees hard, rising onto the balls of your feet.
Finish with a shrug, arms straight, then lower the bar under control.
how.watch: Hips rising faster than the shoulders off the floor, tipping you forward over the bar.

video.title: Snatch Pull | Olympic Weightlifting Exercise Library

how.gist: From the hang, drive your hips and knees straight explosively and pull the weight up to chest height, elbows high and out.
steps: Stand holding the weight in front of your thighs, hands about shoulder-width.
Hinge back slightly to lower it toward your knees.
Drive your hips forward and stand up fast.
Let that drive carry the weight up as you pull your elbows high and out to chest height.
Lower it back under control.
how.watch: Lifting with the arms like an upright row, with no drive from the hips.

video.title: HIGH PULL | Shoulders | How-To Exercise Tutorial

how.gist: Front squat with the weight at your shoulders, then use the drive out of the bottom to push it overhead in one motion.
steps: Hold the weight at your shoulders, elbows up, feet shoulder-width.
Squat to full depth, chest up.
Stand up fast and drive the weight overhead as your hips straighten.
Lock out, then lower the weight to your shoulders as you drop into the next squat.
how.watch: Elbows dropping in the squat, so the weight pulls your chest forward.
how.easier: Use dumbbells or a lighter bar.

video.title: The Thruster

how.gist: Hold a weight locked out overhead on straight arms and squat to full depth underneath it.
steps: Lock the weight overhead; on a bar use a wide grip with the insides of your elbows facing forward.
Keep the weight over the middle of your feet.
Sit down into a full squat, chest up, pushing up into the bar.
Stand up with your arms locked throughout.
how.watch: The bar drifting forward as the chest drops.
how.easier: Use a PVC pipe or an empty bar.

video.title: The Overhead Squat

how.gist: Pull explosively from a hang to above a bar or rings, turn your wrists over the top and press to straight arms.
steps: Hang from a bar, hands about shoulder-width, gripping over the top.
Pull hard and high, bringing the bar toward your lower chest.
As the bar reaches your chest, lean forward and roll your wrists over it.
Press down to straight arms above the bar.
Lower back to the hang with control.
how.watch: Pulling only to the chin, too low to get the chest over the bar.
how.easier: Build both halves with Chest-to-bar pull-up and Straight-bar dip.

video.title: Bar Muscle-up Tutorial

how.gist: Swing your arms and jump from both feet onto a box, landing softly in a quarter squat, then step down.
steps: Stand a short step from the box, feet hip-width.
Swing your arms back and dip into a quarter squat.
Jump, driving the arms forward, and land with both feet flat on the box.
Land softly, knees over toes, then stand tall and step down.
how.watch: Using a box so high you land in a deep squat.
how.easier: Use a lower box.

video.title: How to Do Box Jumps

how.gist: Swing your arms and jump forward as far as you can from both feet, landing softly in a squat.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width, arms raised in front.
Swing your arms back as you hinge and bend your knees.
Throw the arms forward and jump out and up.
Land on both feet, knees bent, and hold the landing before the next jump.
how.watch: Landing stiff-legged or with the knees caving in.
how.harder: Link several jumps in a row without pausing.

how.gist: Step off a low box, land on both feet and rebound straight up into a jump as quickly as you can.
steps: Stand on the edge of a low box, knee height or lower.
Step off rather than jumping down.
Land on both feet and spring straight back up at once.
Land the second jump softly and reset before the next rep.
how.watch: Sinking into a deep squat on the first landing instead of rebounding fast.
how.easier: Do Box jump instead.

video.title: Depth Jump | Olympic Weightlifting Exercise Library

how.gist: Lift a medicine ball overhead and slam it hard into the floor in front of you, then pick it up and repeat.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width, holding the ball at your chest.
Reach it overhead, rising onto your toes.
Slam it down just in front of your feet, hinging and bending your knees.
Squat to pick it up and go straight into the next rep.
how.watch: Rounding the back to pick the ball up.

how.gist: Throw a medicine ball from your chest at a wall as hard as you can, catch the rebound and repeat.
steps: Stand a couple of steps from a solid wall, holding the ball at your chest.
Step toward the wall and push the ball out hard with both hands.
Finish with your arms straight, thumbs pointing down.
Catch the rebound at your chest and reset.
how.watch: Throwing with the arms alone, with no push from the legs.
how.easier: Use a lighter ball.

how.gist: Swing a kettlebell back between your legs and drive it up close to your body into the rack position at your shoulder.
steps: Hinge over the bell and hike it back between your legs.
Drive your hips forward, keeping your elbow close to your side.
Let the bell travel up close to your body, loosening your grip so it turns round your wrist.
Catch it softly in the rack: forearm vertical, bell resting against your forearm and chest.
Drop it back between your legs into the next rep.
how.watch: Swinging the bell out wide so it flips over and bangs your forearm.
how.easier: Learn the Kettlebell swing first.
how.harder: Do Kettlebell clean and press instead.

video.title: Master the Kettlebell Clean | A Complete Guide for Beginners

how.gist: Swing a kettlebell between your legs and in one movement drive it overhead to a locked-out arm.
steps: Hike the bell back between your legs, hinging at the hips.
Drive your hips forward hard and let the bell float up close to your body.
As it passes your chest, punch your hand up through the handle.
Lock out overhead, the bell resting on the back of your forearm.
Let it drop back toward you, then hinge to swing it between your legs.
how.watch: The bell arcing out wide and flopping over onto the forearm.
how.easier: Learn the Kettlebell swing and Kettlebell clean first.

video.title: Movement Demo - One Arm Kettlebell Snatch

how.gist: Lying with a weight pressed up in one hand, stand up step by step and lie back down, arm locked and eyes on the weight.
steps: Lie on your back, weight locked out above one shoulder, that knee bent and foot flat.
Roll onto the opposite elbow, then push up onto that hand.
Lift your hips and sweep the straight leg back under you to kneel.
Turn the back knee to face forward and stand up out of the lunge.
Reverse each step to lie back down, keeping the arm vertical.
how.watch: Taking your eyes off the weight and letting the arm drift from vertical.
how.easier: Practise the steps with no weight, or only up to the hand.

video.title: Turkish Get-Up Basics

how.gist: Jump straight up and pull your knees toward your chest at the top, then land softly and go again.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width, arms ready to swing.
Dip quickly and jump straight up, driving your arms up.
At the top, pull your knees toward your chest.
Straighten your legs to land softly on the balls of your feet, knees bending, and rebound.
how.watch: Landing stiff-legged, or with the knees caving in.
how.easier: Do Jump squats.
how.harder: Spend less time on the ground between jumps.

video.title: How to Tuck Jump (Technique Guide)

how.gist: Jump sideways off one leg and land on the other, stick the landing, then bound back.
steps: Stand on your right leg, knee and hip bent, left foot off the floor.
Push off sideways to the left, swinging your arms.
Land softly on your left foot, knee bent and over the toes.
Hold the landing for a moment, then bound back to the right.
how.watch: Landing knee caving inward.
how.easier: Make the jumps shorter and let the other foot touch down.
how.harder: Go further, or bound continuously without the pause.

video.title: Lateral Bounds ‘Lateral Jumps’ | Lateral Power & Agility Training

exercises.name: Rotational medicine ball throw
exercises.equipment: Medicine ball and a solid wall

how.gist: Stand side-on to a wall and throw a medicine ball into it by turning hard from the back hip through the trunk.
steps: Stand side-on to a wall, a step or two away, holding the ball at your back hip.
Load by turning away from the wall and sitting into the back hip.
Drive the back hip round and let the trunk and arms whip the ball into the wall.
Catch the rebound, reset and repeat; then do the same facing the other way.
how.watch: Throwing with the arms while the hips stay still.
how.easier: Learn the turn first with a light Woodchop.
how.harder: Step into each throw, or use a heavier ball.

video.title: How to Properly Execute Rotational Med Ball Throws | CrossFit Invictus

how.gist: In one move, take a dumbbell from between your feet to straight overhead, driven by a jump of the hips.
steps: Stand over a dumbbell, feet hip width; hinge and grip it with one hand, arm straight.
Drive hard through the legs and hips, keeping the dumbbell close to your body.
As it rises, pull the elbow high, then punch the arm up, dipping slightly to catch it.
Stand tall with the arm locked, then lower it to the shoulder and the floor.
how.watch: Lifting with the arm and back instead of jumping the hips first.
how.easier: Start from just above the knee with a lighter dumbbell.
how.harder: Do a Kettlebell snatch, or alternate arms each rep.

video.title: The Dumbbell Power Snatch

how.gist: Clean a kettlebell to rest on your forearm at the shoulder, then press it straight overhead and bring it back down.
steps: Hike the bell back between your legs with one hand, then drive the hips forward.
Keep the elbow close so the bell rolls onto your forearm in the rack, not onto your wrist.
Brace, squeeze your glutes and press it up until the arm is straight by your ear.
Lower it to the rack, then let it drop between your legs to start the next clean.
how.watch: The bell swinging wide and flipping over, so it bangs the forearm.
how.easier: Practise the Kettlebell clean and the Overhead press separately.
how.harder: Use two kettlebells, one in each hand.

video.title: Kettlebell Clean And Press

how.gist: Lift a sandbag from the floor into your lap, then drive the hips to pop it onto your chest and stand tall.
steps: Stand over the bag, feet just wider than hips, and wrap your hands under its sides.
Squat and hinge to lift it onto your thighs, sitting back with the bag in your lap.
Drive the hips forward hard and pull the bag up your body, dropping your elbows under it.
Catch it high on your chest, stand tall, then lower it back to the floor.
how.watch: Curling the bag up with the arms instead of driving it with the hips.
how.easier: Use a lighter bag and pause in the lap every rep.
how.harder: Clean it to one shoulder, alternating sides.

video.title: How to Perfect the Sandbag Clean

how.gist: Pick up a heavy weight in each hand and walk tall with short, steady steps.
steps: Deadlift a weight up in each hand and stand tall.
Pull your shoulders down and back and brace.
Walk with short, quick steps, looking ahead.
Stop under control and set the weights down with a flat back.
how.watch: Shoulders rounding forward and the chest dropping as the grip tires.

how.gist: Carry a heavy weight in one hand and walk tall without leaning toward or away from it.
steps: Pick up a weight in one hand like a suitcase.
Stand tall with your shoulders level.
Walk with steady steps without leaning to either side.
Swap hands and walk the same distance.
how.watch: Leaning away from the weight, or letting the loaded shoulder drop.
how.easier: Use a lighter weight and a shorter distance.

video.title: How To Perform The Suitcase Carry

how.gist: Lock one or two weights overhead on straight arms and walk, keeping your ribs down.
steps: Press the weight overhead and lock your elbow.
Stack the weight over your shoulder and hip, upper arm by your ear.
Keep your ribs down so your back does not arch.
Walk with short steps, then lower the weight under control.
how.watch: Arching the low back to keep the weight overhead.
how.easier: Carry a single kettlebell overhead and keep the distance short.

video.title: Do it Right: Kettlebell Overhead Carry with Celebrity Trainer Don Saladino

how.gist: Hold one or two weights at your shoulders in the front rack and walk tall without leaning back.
steps: Clean the weights to your shoulders, elbows tucked, wrists straight.
Stand tall and brace, ribs down.
Walk with short, steady steps, breathing behind the brace.
Lower the weights with control at the end.
how.watch: Leaning back so the low back takes the load.

video.title: How to perform the Kettlebell Front Rack Carry

how.gist: Lean into a loaded sled with your arms extended and drive it forward with low, powerful steps.
steps: Grip the uprights, high or low, with your arms nearly straight.
Lean in until your body is at about 45° to the floor.
Drive off the balls of your feet, pushing the floor back behind you.
Keep your back flat and your steps short and steady.
how.watch: Hips rising above the shoulders so the back rounds.

video.title: How To Do The Sled Push The RIGHT Way! (AVOID MISTAKES!)

how.gist: Hold straps tied to a loaded sled and walk backwards dragging it with short, steady steps; forwards in a harness also counts.
steps: Face the sled holding the straps or handle, arms straight.
Sit back into a slight squat and lean away from the sled.
Walk backwards, pushing through the front of each foot.
Keep tension on the straps and your chest up.
how.watch: Pulling with the arms instead of driving with the legs.

video.title: The ULTIMATE Sled Push/Pull Tutorial

how.gist: Stand under a loaded yoke with the bar on your upper back, lift it and walk forward with short, fast steps.
steps: Set the crossbar on your upper back as for a squat, hands on the bar or uprights.
Brace hard and stand up to lift the frame off the ground.
Walk with short, fast steps, hips and shoulders level.
Stop, steady the frame, then bend your knees to set it down.
how.watch: Long strides that set the yoke swinging side to side.

video.title: Improve Your Yoke Walk | CERBERUS STRENGTH PRO TIPS

how.gist: Bear-hug a sandbag tight against your chest and walk with it, staying upright.
steps: Pick the bag up and hug it tight to your chest.
Lock your hands or forearms under the bag, elbows tucked.
Walk with short, steady steps, standing tall.
Set the bag down by squatting, not by rounding over it.
how.watch: Letting the bag slide down so you lean back to hold it.
how.harder: Carry it on one shoulder, switching shoulders each length.

how.gist: Hold the ends of an anchored rope and whip them up and down in fast waves, knees bent and trunk braced.
steps: Hold one end in each hand and step back until the rope has a little slack.
Stand in a half squat, chest up, feet shoulder-width.
Whip your arms up and down fast, alternating, to send waves to the anchor.
Keep the waves reaching the anchor until the set ends.
how.watch: Standing up straight-legged, so the waves die out halfway to the anchor.
how.harder: Move both arms together (double waves) or slam the ropes.

video.title: Exercise of the Week: Battling Ropes Alternating Waves

how.gist: Squat holding a medicine ball at your chest, drive up and throw it to a target high on the wall, catching it into the next squat.
steps: Stand about an arm's length from the wall, ball held at your chest.
Squat below parallel, chest up.
Drive up and throw the ball at the target as your hips straighten.
Catch it on the way down and drop straight into the next squat.
how.watch: Throwing with the arms after the legs have stopped driving.
how.easier: Use a lighter ball or a lower target.

video.title: The Wall-Ball Shot

how.gist: Drop to the floor with your chest down, get back up and jump with your hands overhead.
steps: Squat and put your hands on the floor.
Jump your feet back and lower your chest to the floor.
Push up and jump your feet back to your hands.
Stand and jump, reaching overhead.
how.watch: Hips sagging so the low back arches as you push up.
how.easier: Step the feet back and in, and leave out the jump.

how.gist: On hands and feet with knees just off the floor, crawl forward moving opposite hand and foot together.
steps: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Lift your knees an inch off the floor, back flat.
Step one hand and the opposite foot forward a short way.
Switch sides, keeping your hips low and level.
how.watch: Hips rising high so it turns into a walk on straight arms and legs.
how.easier: Do Bear plank instead.
how.harder: Crawl backwards or sideways.

video.title: Bear Crawl Exercise - Kinetic Sports Rehab

how.gist: Turn a rope with your wrists and hop over it on the balls of your feet with small, quick jumps.
steps: Hold the handles at hip height, elbows close to your sides.
Turn the rope from your wrists, not your arms.
Hop an inch or two off the floor on the balls of your feet.
Land softly and keep a steady rhythm.
how.watch: Jumping too high and tucking the knees to clear the rope.
how.harder: Do double-unders: two turns of the rope per jump.

how.gist: Sit with your hands behind you and feet flat, lift your hips, and walk forward or back on hands and feet.
steps: Sit on the floor, feet flat, hands behind your hips with fingers pointing back or out.
Push into your hands and feet to lift your hips off the floor.
Walk by moving opposite hand and foot together, hips staying up.
Go forward, backward or sideways for the time or distance.
how.watch: Hips sagging toward the floor as you move.
how.easier: Cover a shorter distance and rest between.
how.harder: Lift your hips higher, level with your knees.

how.gist: Jump your feet out wide as your arms swing overhead, then jump them back together as your arms come down.
steps: Stand with your feet together and arms at your sides.
Jump your feet out wider than your shoulders as your arms swing up overhead.
Jump your feet back together as your arms come down.
Stay light on the balls of your feet and keep a steady rhythm.
how.watch: Landing flat-footed and heavy.
how.easier: Step one foot out at a time instead of jumping.

how.gist: Run on the spot, driving each knee up to about hip height and landing lightly on the balls of your feet.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width.
Drive one knee up to about hip height as the opposite arm swings forward.
Switch legs quickly, landing on the ball of each foot.
Keep your chest up and torso tall for the whole set.
how.watch: Leaning back to get the knees higher.
how.easier: March on the spot, lifting the knees without the hop.
how.harder: Go faster, or travel forward as you go.

how.gist: Do a burpee with your hands on two dumbbells, then swing both from the floor to overhead in one move.
steps: Stand with two dumbbells on the floor in front of your feet, handles parallel.
Hands on the handles, jump your feet back, lower your chest to the floor, then jump in.
Hinge over the bells with a flat back and swing them back between your legs.
Drive the hips forward so both bells travel overhead in one move; lock out, then lower.
how.watch: Rounding the back to pull the bells off the floor instead of hinging.
how.easier: Use one dumbbell, or step back and in instead of jumping.
how.harder: Use heavier dumbbells, or hold a steady pace for longer.

video.title: How to do a Dumbbell Devil Press with Jason Khalipa

how.gist: Walk holding a kettlebell upside down by its handle at shoulder height, keeping it balanced and still.
steps: Clean or flip a light kettlebell so its bottom points up, and grip the handle hard.
Hold it in front of your shoulder, elbow bent about 90° and close to your ribs.
Walk slowly and tall, wrist straight, keeping the bell from tipping.
Walk the set distance, set it down, and switch hands.
how.watch: Grip loosening so the bell tips, or the elbow flaring out wide.
how.easier: Do a Front-rack carry with the bell the right way up.
how.harder: Use a heavier bell, or carry one in each hand.

video.title: EricCressey.com: Coaching Up the Bottoms-up Kettlebell Carry

exercises.name: Zercher carry
exercises.equipment: Barbell in a rack, or a sandbag

how.gist: Hold a barbell or sandbag in the crooks of your elbows, tight to your body, and walk tall for the set distance.
steps: Set a bar in a rack at about waist height; pad it if it digs in.
Hook the bar into the crooks of your elbows, clasp your hands and pull it to your body.
Stand it out of the rack, brace hard and keep your chest up.
Walk with short, quick steps for the distance, then put it back in the rack.
how.watch: The upper back rounding forward under the bar.
how.easier: Hug a sandbag in your elbows, or do a Front-rack carry.
how.harder: Add load, or walk further.

video.title: How To Perform The Zercher Carry

how.gist: Swing a sledgehammer over your shoulder and down onto a tyre, sliding your top hand down to meet the other.
steps: Stand square to a big tyre, about a hammer's length away, feet shoulder width.
Hold the handle with one hand near the end and the other near the head.
Lift the hammer over one shoulder, then swing it down, sliding the top hand to the bottom one.
Strike the tyre with knees bent and trunk braced, and let the hammer bounce up.
Swap your hands and swing over the other shoulder, by rep or by set.
how.watch: Straight legs and a rounded back as the hammer lands, instead of bending the knees.
how.easier: Use a lighter hammer, or do a Medicine ball slam.
how.harder: Use a heavier hammer, or work for time.

video.title: SLEDGEHAMMER TRAINING - How to Swing a Sledgehammer or Splitting Maul Like a Pro! Stop Looking Silly

how.gist: Squat at a big tyre, fingers under its edge, then drive it up and forward with your legs and hips and push it over.
steps: Squat at the tyre, feet back, chest against it, fingers under its edge, palms up.
Drive the tyre forward and up with your legs and hips, chest staying on it.
As it rises, step in and knee or hip it to keep it moving.
Turn your hands over and push it the rest of the way with straight arms, then reset.
how.watch: Pulling with bent arms and a rounded back instead of driving into it with the legs.
how.easier: Use a lighter tyre, or learn the hip drive with a Sandbag clean.
how.harder: Use a heavier tyre, or flip it for time or distance.

video.title: Tire Flipping Do's & Don'ts

exercises.equipment: Bench, towel and a light plate

how.gist: Lie face up with your head off a bench and slowly curl your chin toward your chest, then lower back to level.
steps: Lie on your back on a bench with your head past the end.
Fold a towel on your forehead; hold a light plate on it if you use one.
Tuck your chin, then slowly curl your head up toward your chest.
Lower slowly to level without letting your head drop back far.
how.watch: Jerking the head, or using a weight too heavy to move slowly.
how.easier: Use no plate, or do Chin tuck instead.
how.harder: Hold the top for 2 seconds each rep.

exercises.equipment: Bench, towel and a light plate

how.gist: Lie face down with your head off a bench and slowly raise it from chin-down until your face points forward.
steps: Lie face down on a bench with your head past the end.
Fold a towel on the back of your head; hold a light plate on it if you use one.
Let your chin lower slowly toward your chest.
Raise your head until your face points forward, no further, then lower.
how.watch: Throwing the head back past level.
how.easier: Use no plate, or do Neck isometric hold instead.
how.harder: Hold the top for 2 seconds each rep.

exercises.equipment: Bench, towel and a light plate

how.gist: Lie on your side with your head off a bench and slowly raise your ear toward your shoulder, then lower.
steps: Lie on your side on a bench with your head past the end.
Fold a towel on the side of your head; hold a light plate on it if you use one.
Lower your ear slowly toward the floor.
Raise it toward your top shoulder, then switch sides after the set.
how.watch: Turning the head or rolling the body instead of bending straight sideways.
how.easier: Use no plate, or do Neck isometric hold instead.
how.harder: Hold the top for 2 seconds each rep.

how.gist: Without tipping your head down, slide your chin straight back to make a double chin, hold briefly, then relax.
steps: Sit or stand tall, looking straight ahead.
Slide your head straight back, as if a finger pushed your chin, eyes staying level.
Hold 3–5 seconds, feeling the back of the neck lengthen.
Relax forward to neutral and repeat.
how.watch: Nodding the chin down to the chest instead of sliding the head straight back.
how.easier: Do it lying on your back, nudging the back of your head into the floor.
how.harder: Tuck against a light band looped behind your head.

video.title: Chin Tuck Exercise

how.gist: Press your head into your own hand at the front, back or side without letting it move, hold, then change direction.
steps: Sit or stand tall with your head level and chin slightly tucked.
Put a hand on your forehead, the back of your head, or one side.
Push your head into the hand while the hand pushes back, so nothing moves.
Build up gently, hold for the set time, ease off, then work each direction.
how.watch: Pushing so hard the head moves or the shoulders shrug up.
how.easier: Push at about a quarter of your effort.
how.harder: Move on to Neck flexion and Neck extension with load.

video.title: 6 - Isometric Neck Strengthening Exercises - Ask Dr. Abelson

how.gist: Sit with both knees bent 90°, one shin in front and one to the side, and lean over the front shin to stretch the outer hip.
steps: Sit with your front shin across your body and your back shin out to the side, both knees bent about 90°.
Sit tall and turn your chest to face over the front shin.
Hinge forward from the hips over the front shin until the outer hip stretches.
Hold and breathe, then switch to face the other way.
how.watch: Rounding the back to get lower instead of hinging from the hips.
how.easier: Sit on a cushion, or keep your hands on the floor behind you.
how.harder: Lean further over the shin with a long back, then hold over the back leg too.

video.title: Hip 90/90 Stretch (Hip Mobility for Internal & External Rotation)

how.gist: Sit in 90/90 and rotate both knees over to the other side with your feet in place, moving the hips through rotation.
steps: Sit in 90/90, hands on the floor behind you, feet a little wider than your hips.
Keep your feet planted, lift both knees and rotate them over to the other side.
Lower into 90/90 facing the other way; that switch is one rep.
Move slowly and sit tall; take your hands off the floor once that is easy.
how.watch: Swinging the legs over with momentum instead of controlling the turn.
how.easier: Lean back on your hands and turn the knees only as far as is comfortable.
how.harder: Do it with your arms crossed or reaching forward, no hands on the floor.

video.title: How to Do the 90/90 Switch for Hip Mobility (Step-by-Step Tutorial)

how.gist: With one shin across under you and the other leg straight back, lower your hips and fold forward to stretch the outer hip.
steps: From all fours, bring one knee forward behind the same wrist, shin angled across under you.
Slide the other leg straight back, top of the foot on the floor.
Keep your hips level and lower them toward the floor, propped on your hands.
Fold forward over the front shin if you can; hold, breathe, then switch sides.
how.watch: Front knee aching; bring the front heel in toward your hips to ease it.
how.easier: Put a cushion under the front hip, or do Figure-four stretch lying down.
how.harder: Bring the front shin closer to parallel with the front of the mat.

video.title: Pigeon Stretch | Do It Right!

how.gist: Lying on your back, cross one ankle over the other knee and pull that thigh toward you to stretch the glute.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee and let the crossed knee open out.
Lift the bottom foot and pull that thigh toward your chest, hands behind it.
Hold and breathe with your head and shoulders down, then switch sides.
how.watch: Head and shoulders lifting to reach the leg; loop a towel round it instead.
how.easier: Leave the bottom foot on the floor and just let the crossed knee open.
how.harder: Do Pigeon stretch instead.

video.title: Figure 4 stretching

exercises.name: Couch stretch
aka: rear foot elevated hip flexor stretch

how.gist: Kneel with one shin up a wall or couch and the other foot forward, then lift your chest to stretch the front of the back thigh.
steps: Kneel with your back to a wall or couch, one knee in the corner and that shin up the wall.
Step the other foot forward into a lunge, front shin upright.
Squeeze the glute of the back leg and tuck your pelvis under.
Lift your chest toward upright as far as you can; hold, breathe, then switch.
how.watch: Arching the low back instead of tucking the pelvis, which loses the stretch.
how.easier: Lean your chest forward onto your hands, or do Kneeling hip flexor stretch instead.
how.harder: Get fully upright and reach the arm on the back-leg side overhead.

video.title: The Couch Stretch Done Correctly

how.gist: Kneel on one knee, tuck your pelvis under and shift your hips forward to stretch the front of the kneeling hip.
steps: Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward, both knees at about 90°.
Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg and tuck your tailbone under.
Shift your hips forward a little until the front of that hip stretches.
Keep your chest tall; hold and breathe, then switch sides.
how.watch: Arching the low back and lunging far forward instead of tucking the pelvis.
how.easier: Put a folded towel under the knee and hold something for balance.
how.harder: Reach the arm on the kneeling side up and over, or do Couch stretch.

video.title: Bulletproof Step-by-step Guide to the Half Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch" [stretching advice]

how.gist: From a deep lunge with both hands inside the front foot, sink your hips forward and down to open the hips and groin.
steps: From a lunge, put both hands on the floor inside your front foot.
Lower the back knee to the floor and walk the front foot slightly out to the side.
Let your hips sink forward and down, front knee in line with your toes.
Drop to your forearms if you can; hold, breathe, then switch sides.
how.watch: Front knee falling inward instead of staying over the foot.
how.easier: Stay on your hands, or rest them on blocks.
how.harder: Lift the back knee off the floor and straighten that leg.

video.title: Lizard Pose: Achieve Optimal Hip Mobility

how.gist: On all fours with your knees wide and shins parallel, ease your hips back to stretch the inner thighs.
steps: Start on all fours on a soft surface, then slide your knees wide apart.
Keep your shins parallel and ankles in line with your knees, feet flexed.
Lower onto your forearms and ease your hips back toward your heels.
Stop at a strong stretch in the inner thighs; hold and breathe.
how.watch: Spreading the knees too far too soon; pressure in the inner knee means come in.
how.easier: Bring your knees closer together and stay on your hands.
how.harder: Widen the knees a little at a time between holds.

video.title: "Frog" Adductor Stretch

how.gist: Sit with the soles of your feet together and knees out, then hinge forward to stretch the inner thighs.
steps: Sit tall with the soles of your feet together and knees falling out to the sides.
Hold your feet and draw your heels in as close as is comfortable.
Hinge forward from the hips with a long back until the inner thighs stretch.
Hold and breathe, letting the knees settle lower over time.
how.watch: Rounding the back to bring the head down instead of hinging from the hips.
how.easier: Sit on a cushion and keep your feet further from you.
how.harder: Do Frog stretch for a deeper groin stretch.

video.title: How to Do a Butterfly Stretch: A Guide from Physical Therapists

how.gist: On all fours with one leg straight out to the side, rock your hips back toward your heel and forward again.
steps: Start on all fours and straighten one leg out to the side, foot flat on the floor.
Keep your back flat and rock your hips back toward your heel.
Stop at a stretch in the inner thigh of the straight leg, then rock forward.
Each rock back and forward is one rep; finish the set and switch sides.
how.watch: Back rounding as the hips go back, instead of staying flat.
how.easier: Bend the outstretched knee a little, or rock back a shorter way.
how.harder: Do Cossack squat to work the same range standing.

video.title: How to Stretch Your Adductors with the Adductor Rock Back

how.gist: Standing on one leg, draw the biggest slow circle you can with the other knee, moving only at the hip, then reverse.
steps: Stand on one leg holding a wall, and brace your trunk so only the hip moves.
Lift the free knee up in front of you as high as you can.
Open the knee out to the side, turn it round behind you, and lower it back to standing.
That full circle is one rep; reverse the direction, then switch legs.
how.watch: Twisting or leaning the trunk to make the circle bigger, so the hip is not doing it.
how.easier: Do them on all fours, or make the circles smaller.
how.harder: Let go of the wall, and move slower with more tension.

video.title: Standing Hip CARs (controlled articular rotations)

how.gist: Sit down into the deepest squat you can with your heels flat, and stay there, breathing and relaxed.
steps: Stand with feet about shoulder-width, toes turned out a little.
Sit straight down as low as you can, heels flat and knees out over your toes.
Hold the bottom with your chest up, elbows pushing your knees out if it helps.
Breathe and relax into the hold, then stand up.
how.watch: Heels lifting off the floor; widen your stance or put plates under the heels.
how.easier: Hold a doorframe, or hold a kettlebell or plate in front as a counterweight.
how.harder: Bring the feet closer and the toes straighter, hands free.

video.title: How to Do a Deep Squat According to Physical Therapists

how.gist: Holding your toes, drop into a deep squat with your chest up, then lift your hips to straighten your legs.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width, fold forward and hold your toes, knees bent as needed.
Keep hold of your toes and drop your hips into a deep squat, chest up.
Push your knees out with your elbows, then lift your hips and straighten your legs.
Down into the squat and back up to the fold is one rep; let go and stand at the end.
how.watch: Heels lifting as you drop into the squat.
how.easier: Hold your shins instead of your toes.
how.harder: At the bottom, reach one arm up to the ceiling, then the other.

video.title: Squat Mobility: Squat-To-Stand

how.gist: Lying on your back, hold the outsides of your feet with knees wide and draw the knees down beside your ribs.
steps: Lie on your back and draw your knees toward your chest.
Hold the outsides of your feet, knees wider than your body, soles facing up.
Gently pull the knees down toward the floor beside your armpits, shins upright.
Keep your head and low back down; hold and breathe, rocking side to side if you like.
how.watch: Tailbone and low back curling up off the floor as you pull.
how.easier: Hold your ankles or shins, or loop a strap round each foot.

video.title: How to Do the Happy Baby Pose: A Guide from Physical Therapists

how.gist: From a long lunge, drop an elbow to the front foot, turn that arm to the ceiling, then straighten the front leg.
steps: Step into a long lunge, right foot forward, and put your left hand on the floor.
Drop your right elbow toward the inside of your right foot.
Reach the right arm up to the ceiling, eyes on the hand, then put it on the floor.
Lift your front toes and push your hips back to straighten the front leg.
Step back to standing; that is one rep. Switch sides each rep.
how.watch: Swinging only the arm up instead of turning the chest with it.
how.easier: Put the back knee down and skip the elbow drop.

video.title: The World's Greatest Stretch (Mobility Exercise) by Squat University

how.gist: Sit with your legs straight and hinge forward from the hips with a long back to stretch the hamstrings.
steps: Sit tall with your legs straight in front of you, toes pointing up.
Hinge forward from the hips with a long back, reaching for your shins, feet or a strap.
Stop where the backs of the thighs stretch strongly; soften the knees if needed.
Hold and breathe, easing a little further as the stretch lets go.
how.watch: Rounding the back to bring the head to the knees instead of hinging from the hips.
how.easier: Sit on a cushion with knees slightly bent, or loop a strap round your feet.
how.harder: Do Pancake stretch to work the hamstrings and inner thighs together.

video.title: Seated Forward Fold - Beginner Hamstring Stretch (Video Tutorial)

how.gist: Lying on your back, raise one straight leg and draw it toward you with a strap to stretch the back of the thigh.
steps: Lie on your back and loop a strap, band or towel round one foot.
Straighten that leg up toward the ceiling, the other leg bent or flat on the floor.
Draw the leg toward you with the strap until the back of the thigh stretches.
Keep both hips on the floor; hold, breathe, then switch legs.
how.watch: Hips lifting or the knee bending a lot as the leg is pulled closer.
how.easier: Keep the other knee bent with that foot flat on the floor.
how.harder: Keep the other leg straight on the floor, toes pointing up.

video.title: Hamstring Stretch with a Strap, Supine - Ask Doctor Jo

how.gist: Sit with your legs wide and straight and fold forward from the hips, chest leading, to stretch inner thighs and hamstrings.
steps: Sit with your legs straight and as wide as is comfortable, knees and toes pointing up.
Sit tall and tip your pelvis forward, hands on the floor in front of you.
Walk your hands forward, folding from the hips with your chest leading.
Hold at a strong stretch in the inner thighs and hamstrings and breathe.
how.watch: Rounding from the upper back while the pelvis stays tipped back.
how.easier: Sit on a cushion or block, or bend the knees slightly.
how.harder: Hold a light plate out in front of you to draw you deeper.

video.title: Full Guide: How to Pancake Stretch (Beginner to Advanced)

how.gist: Standing on a box with straight legs, slowly roll your spine down one segment at a time, arms past your toes, then roll back up.
steps: Stand on a box or bench with straight legs, holding nothing at first.
Tuck your chin and roll down slowly from the head, one part of the spine at a time.
Let your arms hang past your toes as far as you can control.
Roll back up from the low back first and the head last, just as slowly.
Down and up is one rep; add weight only in small steps after weeks without.
how.watch: Going heavy or fast: this is a slow, light stretch, not a lift.
how.easier: Do it standing on the floor, knees slightly bent, no weight.
how.harder: Hold a light dumbbell or kettlebell, adding weight a little at a time.

video.title: Jefferson Curl | Do It Right!

how.gist: From all fours, push your hips up and back into an upside-down V, arms long and heels sinking toward the floor.
steps: Start on all fours, hands shoulder-width apart, toes tucked under.
Lift your knees and push your hips up and back into an upside-down V.
Press the floor away with long arms and let your heels sink toward the floor.
Bend your knees if needed to keep your back long; hold and breathe.
how.watch: Rounding the back to get the heels down; bend the knees and lift the hips instead.
how.easier: Bend your knees a lot, or do Puppy pose.
how.harder: Pedal the heels, or lift one leg high behind you.

video.title: Downward Dog - Downward Facing Dog Yoga Pose

how.gist: Fold forward, walk your hands out to a plank, then walk your feet in to your hands with legs as straight as you can.
steps: Stand tall, fold forward and put your hands on the floor, bending your knees only as needed.
Walk your hands forward until you are in a high plank.
Keeping your legs as straight as you can, walk your feet in toward your hands.
Hands out and feet in is one rep; stand up, or keep travelling forward.
how.watch: Hips sagging in the plank at the far end.
how.easier: Bend your knees more, and walk out only as far as you can hold.
how.harder: Add a push-up at the plank, or walk the hands out past your shoulders.

video.title: Inch Worm Exercise

how.gist: On all fours, slowly arch your back with your belly down and eyes up, then round it up toward the ceiling.
steps: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Breathe in and let your belly drop, chest forward and eyes up (cow).
Breathe out and round your back up to the ceiling, chin toward chest (cat).
One arch and one round is one rep; move slowly through the whole spine.
how.watch: Moving only the low back while the upper back stays still.
how.harder: Move one segment at a time, starting from the tailbone.

video.title: Loosen Your Back Muscles With The Cat Cow Stretch | Form Check | Men's Health Muscle

how.gist: Lying on your side with knees bent, sweep the top arm over to the other side, turning your chest, then bring it back.
steps: Lie on your side, hips and knees bent to 90°, arms straight out in front, palms together.
Keep your knees together on the floor, holding them down with the bottom hand if needed.
Sweep the top arm up and over to the other side, turning your chest and head with it.
Pause, then bring it back; that is one rep. Finish the set and switch sides.
how.watch: Knees sliding apart or lifting, so the twist comes from the low back.
how.easier: Rest your head on a pillow and open only as far as is easy.

video.title: Open Books (Sidelying Thoracic Rotation)

how.gist: On all fours, slide one arm under your body to rest the shoulder down, then reach it up to the ceiling.
steps: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Slide one arm under your body along the floor, palm up, until that shoulder rests down.
Reverse and reach the same arm up to the ceiling, turning your chest and eyes with it.
Under and up is one rep; keep your hips still, then switch sides.
how.watch: Hips swinging sideways instead of the upper back turning.
how.harder: Hold each end for a few breaths before moving on.

video.title: How to Do a Thread the Needle Stretch: A Guide from Physical Therapists

how.gist: Lie back over a foam roller across your upper back and let the upper spine bend back over it, then curl up.
steps: Sit with a foam roller across your back, just below the shoulder blades.
Lie back over it with your hands behind your head, elbows in, hips on the floor.
Let your upper back bend back over the roller, then curl back up; that is one rep.
Move the roller up an inch and repeat; stay above the bottom of the ribs.
how.watch: Arching the low back and lifting the hips instead of bending over the roller.
how.easier: Use a softer roller or a rolled towel.
how.harder: Reach your arms overhead toward the floor as you lean back.

video.title: Foam Roll: Mid-Back (Thoracic) Extension

how.gist: Kneel, sit your hips back to your heels and fold forward with your arms out, resting your forehead on the floor.
steps: Kneel with your big toes together and knees hip-width or wider.
Sit your hips back toward your heels.
Fold forward, reach your arms out in front and rest your forehead on the floor.
Let your back and shoulders relax, breathing slowly into your back.
how.watch: Straining to keep hips on heels; put a cushion between them and relax.
how.easier: Put a cushion under your hips or forehead.

video.title: How to do Childs Pose PROPERLY | Yoga for Beginners Pose Tutorial

how.gist: Lying face down, press your chest up on your hands while your hips stay on the floor, arching the back gently.
steps: Lie face down with your hands under your shoulders and legs straight behind you.
Press up slowly, lifting your chest while your hips stay on the floor.
Straighten your arms only as far as is comfortable; ease off if the low back pinches.
Hold and breathe with shoulders down, then lower slowly.
how.watch: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears as you press.
how.easier: Stay on your forearms with elbows under your shoulders (sphinx).
how.harder: Straighten your arms fully while your hips stay down.

video.title: Cobra Pose - Yoga With Adriene

how.gist: Lying on your back with arms out, lower both bent knees to one side while your shoulders stay down.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your arms out to the sides.
Lower both knees to one side while your shoulders stay on the floor.
Turn your head the other way if comfortable; hold and breathe.
Bring the knees back through the middle and switch sides.
how.watch: The far shoulder lifting off the floor.
how.easier: Rest the knees on a cushion.
how.harder: Straighten the bottom leg and cross the top bent knee over it.

video.title: How to do Supta Matsyendrasana - Supine Spinal Twist - Beginners Yoga

how.gist: Lying on your back, press up through hands and feet into an arch, arms straight and chest pushed toward your hands.
steps: Lie on your back, feet flat near your hips, hands by your ears with fingers toward your feet.
Press through hands and feet to lift your hips; rest on the crown of your head first if needed.
Straighten your arms and push your chest toward the wall behind your hands.
Hold and breathe, then tuck your chin and lower slowly onto your upper back.
how.watch: Bending only at the low back with bent arms and shoulders that never open.
how.easier: Practise Glute bridge and Cobra stretch until both are easy.
how.harder: Walk your hands and feet closer together, or hold for longer.

video.title: How To BACK BRIDGE For Beginners (FLEXIBLE & STRONG)

how.gist: Lying face down with arms out wide, swing one bent leg up and across behind you toward the other hand, then back.
steps: Lie face down with your arms straight out to the sides, palms down.
Bend one knee and swing that foot up and across behind you toward the opposite hand.
Keep both shoulders on the floor and let your hips turn.
Return to the floor; that is one rep. Alternate sides.
how.watch: Flinging the leg over fast instead of moving it with control.
how.easier: Go only part way across, letting the far shoulder lift a little.

video.title: How To Do The Scorpion Stretch

how.gist: Lying on your side, hold the top knee down in front and the bottom foot behind you, then turn your chest open.
steps: Lie on your right side, draw your left knee up in front and hold it down with your right hand.
Bend your right knee behind you and hold that foot with your left hand.
Breathe out and turn your chest and left shoulder toward the floor behind you.
Hold, opening a little more on each breath out, then switch sides.
how.watch: Top knee lifting off the floor as you turn, so the low back twists instead.
how.easier: Loop a strap round the back foot, or rest the top knee on a cushion.

video.title: How To Perform The Bretzel Stretch

how.gist: With your forearms on a door frame, step through and lean forward to stretch the chest and front of the shoulders.
steps: Stand in a doorway with your forearms on the frame, elbows at or just below shoulder height.
Step one foot through the doorway.
Lean your chest gently forward until the chest and front of the shoulders stretch.
Keep your shoulders down; hold and breathe. Ease off if the shoulder pinches.
how.watch: Shoulders rolling forward or shrugging as you lean, instead of the chest opening.
how.easier: Do one arm at a time, or lean less.
how.harder: Raise the elbows a little higher to move the stretch to the lower chest.

video.title: How to do Doorway Pec Stretch - Flexibility - Wellen

how.gist: Lying on your side, bottom arm bent 90° in front, gently press that forearm toward the floor to stretch the back of the shoulder.
steps: Lie on your side, rolled back slightly, bottom arm out in front at shoulder height.
Bend that elbow to 90° so your fingers point at the ceiling.
With the top hand, gently press the bottom forearm down toward the floor.
Stop at a mild stretch at the back of the shoulder; hold, breathe, then switch.
how.watch: Pressing hard into pinching at the front of the shoulder instead of easing off.
how.easier: Roll further back toward lying flat to take weight off the shoulder.

video.title: Sleeper Shoulder Stretch - Physical Therapy Exercises

how.gist: Bring one straight arm across your chest and draw it in with the other hand to stretch the back of the shoulder.
steps: Stand or sit tall and bring one straight arm across your chest.
Hold it just above the elbow with the other hand.
Draw it gently toward you, shoulder down, until the back of the shoulder stretches.
Hold and breathe, then switch arms.
how.watch: Shoulder shrugging up toward the ear as you pull.

video.title: Cross Body Shoulder Stretch: How to Do It Correctly

how.gist: With a wide grip on a band or dowel, take it over your head with straight arms to behind your hips, and back.
steps: Hold a band or dowel in front of your hips with a wide grip, arms straight.
Keep your arms straight and raise it up over your head.
Carry on until it touches behind your hips, then return the same way.
Over and back is one rep; narrow your grip slowly over weeks, not in one go.
how.watch: Bending one elbow to get round, which means the grip is too narrow.
how.easier: Use a band, and a wider grip.
how.harder: Narrow your grip a little at a time.

video.title: Shoulder Dislocates for Shoulder Flexibility
